### Scenario C: Official `modelscript.org` & `ansatz.social` Cloud Production Deployment

`modelscript.org` and `ansatz.social` run on a shared multi-container **Enterprise Edition** stack via [`docker-compose.yml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/docker-compose.yml) + [`docker-compose.prod.yml`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/docker-compose.prod.yml) (`--profile flagship` or `--profile federated`) behind Caddy automatic multi-domain TLS (`PUBLIC_DOMAIN=ansatz.social`, `DOCS_DOMAIN=modelscript.org`). Host-based routing in Nginx serves the **Unified VitePress Documentation & PDF Manual** (`/` and `/docs`, `/guide/*`, `/ansatz/*`, `/languages/*`, `/pricing`) on `modelscript.org` and the **Ansatz Federated Web SPA** (`/`, `/home`, `/explore`, `/packages`, `/repos`, `/morsel`) on `ansatz.social`, alongside Studio (`/studio`, `/vscode`) and Enterprise API (`/api/*`, `/git/*`).

#### C.1 Initial Server Provisioning (`/opt/modelscript`)

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/modelscript/config
cd /opt/modelscript

# Copy docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.prod.yml, config/Caddyfile, config/mosquitto.conf, config/init-timescaledb.sql
cp .env.production.example .env.production
chmod 600 .env.production

# Edit .env.production to set production secrets:
#   PUBLIC_DOMAIN=ansatz.social
#   DOCS_DOMAIN=modelscript.org
#   PUBLIC_URL=https://ansatz.social
#   CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://ansatz.social,https://modelscript.org,https://ide.ansatz.social,https://ide.modelscript.org
#   MSX_EDITION=ee
#   MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE=true
#   MSX_LICENSE_KEY=<pre-minted modelscript-cloud-prod Ed25519 token>
#   JWT_SECRET=<production-64-char-hex-secret>
#   TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY=<production-64-char-hex-key>
#   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_...
#   STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET=whsec_...

# Pull prebuilt GHCR images and launch the production stack
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship pull

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship up -d --wait --remove-orphans
```

#### C.2 Automated CI/CD Rollouts (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` & `.github/workflows/release.yml`)

Every push to `main` and every tagged release in GitHub Actions builds and pushes all 6 Docker images (`api-ee`, `api-ce`, `web`, `cli-ee`, `cli-ce`, `appliance`) to `ghcr.io/modelscript/*` (tagged with both `:sha-<commit>` / `:<version>` and `:latest`) and triggers the `deploy_production` rollout job under a shared `production-deploy` concurrency lock. Before rolling out new containers, the deployment job executes an online SQLite `VACUUM INTO` snapshot inside the running `api` container (`/app/apps/api/data/backups/pre-deploy-<timestamp>.db`). Configure either SSH or Webhook secrets in GitHub repository settings:

| GitHub Secret                          | Description                                                                                  |
| :------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PROD_SSH_HOST`                        | Hostname or IP of the shared `modelscript.org` / `ansatz.social` production server           |
| `PROD_SSH_USER`                        | Deployment SSH user (with `docker` group permissions)                                        |
| `PROD_SSH_KEY`                         | Ed25519 private SSH key for `PROD_SSH_USER`                                                  |
| `PROD_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS` _(optional)_    | Pinned SSH host key entry for `PROD_SSH_HOST` (falls back to `ssh-keyscan` if omitted)       |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_PATH`                     | Directory on the production host (defaults to `/opt/modelscript`)                            |
| `PROD_ENV_FILE` _(optional)_           | Complete content of `.env.production` to automatically write and secure on the host          |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` _(optional)_ | Webhook URL if triggering rollouts via an external orchestrator (Portainer / Coolify / Argo) |
| `PROD_DEPLOY_TOKEN` _(optional)_       | Bearer token for `PROD_DEPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL`                                                   |

#### C.3 Issuing & Verifying Customer License Keys (Maintainer Runbook)

The offline Ed25519 license keypair generator and token signer lives in `ee/src/cli/license-cli.ts`:

```bash
# 1. Generate a new Ed25519 keypair (stored in .keys/, which is gitignored)
npm run ee:keygen -- --out-dir=.keys

# 2. Mint a signed offline customer license token
npm run ee:sign-license -- \
  --private-key=.keys/msx-license-private.pem \
  --org="Acme Aerospace Corp" \
  --tier=appliance \
  --seats=100 \
  --days=365 \
  --out=.keys/acme-aerospace.license.json

# 3. Verify any license token offline against the embedded production public key
npm run ee:verify-license -- msx_lic_<PAYLOAD>.<SIGNATURE>
```

---

### 9.7 Upgrading & Rollback Runbook

Follow this standard operating procedure whenever upgrading a self-hosted Ansatz hub or Enterprise appliance:

```bash
# 1. Place the hub in read_only maintenance mode so in-flight jobs finish cleanly
curl -X PATCH https://hub.corp.internal/api/v1/admin/settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Admin-Sudo-Token: $SUDO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"maintenanceMode": "read_only"}'

# 2. Take an atomic pre-upgrade snapshot and verify health
msx db backup --label pre-upgrade
msx db doctor

# 3. Pull the target release images and preview pending schema migrations
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship pull
msx db upgrade --dry-run

# 4. Recreate containers and verify post-upgrade integrity
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship up -d --wait --remove-orphans
msx db verify

# 5. Exit maintenance mode once /health and /api/v1/ready report healthy
curl -X PATCH https://hub.corp.internal/api/v1/admin/settings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Admin-Sudo-Token: $SUDO_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"maintenanceMode": "off"}'
```

If a release verification check fails and an immediate rollback is required:

```bash
# 1. Restore the pre-upgrade SQLite snapshot atomically
msx db restore --file modelscript-backup-pre-upgrade.db

# 2. Pin the previous image tag in .env.production (or docker-compose.prod.yml) and restart
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env.production --profile flagship up -d --wait
```

## 10. Production Security Hardening & Pre-Flight Verification

For commercial paid deployments (`modelscript.org`, `ansatz.social`, and customer VPC appliances), ModelScript applies a defense-in-depth security model designed to safeguard compute infrastructure, proprietary models, and billing ledgers.

### 10.1 Automated Pre-Flight Sentinel (`npm run preflight:prod`)

Before launching containers or opening public ingress, execute the pre-flight sentinel to audit host permissions, kernel sandboxing capabilities, and secret entropy:

```bash
# Run security pre-flight sentinel
npm run preflight:prod
```

The sentinel audits five core hardening areas:

- **Sandbox Isolation**: Verifies Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) is installed and rootless unprivileged user namespaces (`--unshare-net`) function on the host kernel.
- **Cryptographic Secrets**: Checks `JWT_SECRET` for $\ge 32$ characters and entropy (rejects dictionary words), validates `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` format (`whsec_...`), and verifies `AUDIT_HMAC_SECRET`.
- **Storage & Registry Permissions**: Validates that local package stores and S3/MinIO CAS buckets are accessible and writable under unprivileged UID 1000.
- **Network & Reverse-Proxy**: Ensures `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind reverse proxies (Caddy/Cloudflare) to prevent rate-limit bypass via header spoofing.
- **Regulatory Licensing**: Validates offline Ed25519 `MSX_LICENSE_KEY` signatures in Enterprise mode.

> [!TIP]
> The automated rollout script ([`scripts/ops/deploy.sh`](https://github.com/modelscript/modelscript/blob/main/scripts/ops/deploy.sh)) executes this sentinel as **Step 2c**. If any critical (P0) security check fails, the deployment halts automatically before modifying active containers.

### 10.2 Worker Sandboxing & Execution Isolation

Native C simulation models and external FMU binaries execute within a multi-layered sandbox:

- **Bubblewrap (`bwrap`) Containerization**: Worker processes run with `--unshare-net` (no outbound network access), `--ro-bind / /` (read-only root filesystem), `/tmp` mounted on memory tmpfs (`size=512m`), `--cap-drop ALL`, and bind mounts strictly restricted to the job's working directory.
- **Watchdogs & Quotas**: Simulation execution is bound to wall-clock timeouts (`15 min` default) and memory watchdogs that terminate runaway processes without stalling the API event loop.

### 10.3 Ingress DoS Defense & Distributed Rate Limiting

- **Pre-Buffering Ingress Gate**: Incoming request bodies are inspected before memory allocation: strict **256KB** limits on `/api/v1/auth/*` and **2MB** limits on standard JSON API endpoints (exempting streaming CAS package tarballs and admin migration bundles).
- **Distributed Redis Rate Limiter**: When `REDIS_URL` is set, rate-limiting counters are synchronized across all cluster replicas via atomic `INCR` + `PEXPIRE` commands, with automatic fallback to local memory maps if Redis becomes unreachable.
- **Content Security Policy (CSP)**: Default CSP headers enforce `default-src 'self'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'self'`, and `frame-ancestors 'self'` across all API and web routes, with support for custom environment policies via `CUSTOM_CSP`.

### 10.4 Financial Escrow & Dispute Kill-Switches

- **Two-Phase Credit Escrow**: Simulation job dispatch pre-authorizes maximum estimated compute credits before worker execution begins; upon completion or cancellation, exact seconds are settled and unused funds are refunded.
- **Active Job Kill-Switch**: If an account receives a payment dispute or chargeback, all running and queued Slurm or local worker jobs for that user are immediately canceled via `scancel` and `SIGKILL`.

### 10.5 Package Immutability & Regulatory Non-Repudiation

- **CAS Immutability Early Guard**: Publishing an existing package version (`name@version`) immediately fast-fails with `409 Conflict` before archive extraction or AST parsing.
- **DHF Merkle Hash Chaining**: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 and ISO 13485 compliance dossiers link consecutive attestations in an unbroken SHA-256 Merkle chain (`previousAttestationHash`) verified via `verifyComplianceAttestationChain()`.
- **Clock Rollback Protection**: Monotonic timestamp checks reject system clock manipulation attempts to extend expired offline licenses.

# Ansatz Platform Overview

**Ansatz** (`ansatz.social`) is a federated engineering network and cloud computational platform powered by **ModelScript**. It extends the local ModelScript compiler and numerical solvers into a collaborative, web-native environment for systems engineers, dynamicists, researchers, and CAE practitioners.

---

## What is Ansatz?

While **ModelScript** provides the core command-line toolchain (`msx`), WebAssembly GLR parsers, and linear-memory DAE simulation engine, **Ansatz** serves as the collaborative platform layer. It provides:

1. **A Polyglot Package Registry:** A centralized and federated index for publishing and versioning Modelica, SysML v2, STEP, SBML, and ModelScript libraries with SPDX license auditing and polyglot standard library discovery (`msx stdlib`).
2. **Federated Engineering Feeds ("Morsels"):** W3C ActivityPub-powered social collaboration where engineers share executable simulation runs across 81 languages, 3D CAD/FEA/CFD snapshots, and schematic diffs across independent nodes.
3. **Scholarly Citations & Literature Graph (`/references`):** Integrated OpenAlex, Crossref, BibTeX, and RIS bibliographic hub linking peer-reviewed literature (`[@cite_key]`) directly to executable models, parameters, and verification morsels.
4. **Personal Activity Git Vault:** Every user account is backed by a cryptographically signed, user-owned Git repository vault that versions posts, model snapshots, citations, and annotations for complete data sovereignty and offline Git portability.
5. **Cloud HPC Simulation Dispatcher:** An orchestration gateway bridging browser-based design with remote Slurm HPC clusters and continuum CAE solvers.
6. **Interactive Browser Runtime:** Monaco-powered code editing, WebAssembly client-side simulation, equation-level DAP debugging, SVG schematic layout, and Three.js 3D CAD visualization.
7. **Digital Thread Explorer:** Cross-domain hypergraph navigation connecting requirements (`@satisfies`), tests (`@verifies`), scholarly references, and multi-physics artifacts.

---

## Architectural Separation: ModelScript vs. Ansatz

The monorepo maintains a clear boundary between the engine and the platform:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Ansatz Platform (apps/)                         │
│   • apps/web: React 19 SPA (ansatz.social, /morsel, /references)       │
│   • apps/api: Express, GraphQL, SPARQL, Git Smart HTTP, ActivityPub   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│             Enterprise Edition (ee/ — LicenseRef-Enterprise)           │
│   • @modelscript/ee: SSO/SAML, RBAC, Slurm HPC, NERC CIP, Historian   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│            ModelScript Open-Core Engine (packages/, languages/)        │
│   • packages/runtime: SoA DAE arena, BLT, Salsa query engine           │
│   • packages/simulate: SUNDIALS CVODE/IDA, WebGPU solver               │
│   • packages/dsl: WASM GLR parser compiler, TGG graph rewriting        │
│   • languages/*: 81 engineering & scientific domain language parsers   │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The ModelScript engine is designed to be completely headless and can run inside the CLI (`msx`), inside local Node.js environments, or embedded directly inside the browser using WebAssembly. Ansatz is the cloud platform that hosts, shares, and coordinates these computations.

---

## Platform Surfaces

| Surface                  | Route               | Description                                                                                   |
| :----------------------- | :------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Home & Feeds**         | `/home`, `/explore` | ActivityPub engineering posts, executable simulation morsels, and discussion threads.         |
| **Ansatz Morsel**        | `/morsel`           | Dual-pane Monaco editor and live simulation canvas powered by client-side WebAssembly.        |
| **Ansatz Studio**        | `/studio`           | Web-native engineering IDE workbench with LSP intelligence and DAP simulation debugger.       |
| **Scholarly References** | `/references`       | OpenAlex / DOI / BibTeX citation manager and literature-to-model traceability graph.          |
| **Package Registry**     | `/packages`         | Search, publish, and inspect versioned engineering libraries with dependency trees.           |
| **Digital Thread**       | `/thread`           | Visual hypergraph explorer tracing requirements and Triple Graph Grammar correspondences.     |
| **Personal Git Vault**   | `/settings`         | Cloneable, signed Git repository backing all personal morsels, models, and scholarly records. |
| **Administration**       | `/admin`            | Instance governance, moderation queues, S2S federation policies, and database backups.        |
| **Setup Wizard**         | `/setup`            | First-boot guided configuration for initializing standalone or enterprise nodes.              |

## Replacing Legacy Desktop Workflows

Ansatz serves as the collaborative platform layer designed to systematically displace the file silos, seat-tax barriers, and isolated environments of legacy first-party engineering tools (Dassault Systèmes Dymola and Cameo, MathWorks Simulink, Manitoba Hydro PSCAD, and SLB OLGA).

For a detailed analysis of the 5-stage adoption wedge (Zero-Install Review, Cross-Domain Digital Thread, Git-Native CI/CD, Executable Decision Records, and Cloud HPC Offload) and tool-specific displacement playbooks, see the [Workflow Replacement Guide](/ansatz/workflow-replacement).

# Replacing First-Party Engineering Workflows with Ansatz

**Ansatz** (`ansatz.social`) is designed to displace the fragmented, desktop-bound workflows of legacy first-party engineering tools—including Dassault Systèmes Dymola, Cameo / MagicDraw, MathWorks MATLAB/Simulink, Manitoba Hydro PSCAD, and SLB OLGA.

Rather than functioning as a generic consumer social network, Ansatz serves as the **Collaborative Systems Engineering Cloud**: uniting the zero-install accessibility of web-native CAD/vector tools, the branching and review rigor of modern software version control, and the model distribution capabilities of contemporary package registries for 81 physical and mathematical engineering domains.

---

## The Incumbent Failure Modes

Practicing engineers in automotive, aerospace, energy, defense, and biomedical sectors frequently encounter structural bottlenecks in traditional first-party toolchains:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ The First-Party Workflow Bottleneck Matrix                             │
├────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────┤
│ Dimension          │ Legacy First-Party Status   │ Ansatz Architecture │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Licensing          │ $20k–$80k/seat FlexLM node  │ Open-core engine &  │
│                    │ locks & floating starvation │ web-native access   │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Distribution       │ 500MB proprietary zip files │ URL permalinks &    │
│                    │ emailed or stored on shared │ WebAssembly runtime │
│                    │ network folders             │ in the browser      │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Collaboration      │ Monolithic binary files     │ Git Smart HTTP with │
│                    │ (.slx, .pscx, .mdzip) that  │ visual schematic    │
│                    │ prevent code review         │ & trajectory diffs  │
├────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────┤
│ Interoperability   │ Isolated disciplinary silos │ Cross-domain Salsa  │
│                    │ bridged only by static      │ hypergraph linking  │
│                    │ PowerPoint screenshots      │ 81 format parsers   │
└────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────┘
```

---

## The 5-Stage Replacement Wedge

Displacing an entrenched engineering monolith cannot occur through immediate, disruptive rip-and-replace mandates. Ansatz employs a phased adoption wedge that provides immediate utility before expanding into primary authoring:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Wedge1["Stage 1: Zero-Install Review & Handoff<br/>(Replace 500MB zip emails & viewer seats)"]
    Wedge2["Stage 2: Cross-Domain Digital Thread<br/>(Connect SysML v2, Modelica, PSCAD & CAD)"]
    Wedge3["Stage 3: Git-Native Engineering CI/CD<br/>(Automated PR diffs & trajectory regression)"]
    Wedge4["Stage 4: Living Decision Records & Literature<br/>(Link DOI references & runnable calibration)"]
    Wedge5["Stage 5: Primary Authoring & Cloud HPC<br/>(In-browser Studio & Slurm cluster offload)"]

    Wedge1 --> Wedge2
    Wedge2 --> Wedge3
    Wedge3 --> Wedge4
    Wedge4 --> Wedge5
```

### Stage 1: Zero-Install Review and Client Handoff

- **The Problem:** Non-authoring stakeholders—project managers, systems certifiers, contracting officers, and downstream integration teams—are routinely locked out of inspecting engineering models because acquiring a dedicated desktop license seat cannot be justified for read-only evaluation.
- **The Ansatz Workflow:**
  1. An author opens or imports an existing model in **Ansatz Morsel** (`/morsel`).
  2. The entire multi-domain model is encoded into a deterministic, compressed permalink or published as a versioned engineering morsel.
  3. The reviewer opens the URL in any standard web browser on Linux, macOS, Windows, or iPadOS.
  4. The model compiles and simulates directly on the client using WebAssembly, exposing interactive parameter sliders, schematic diagrams, 3D CAD viewports, and numerical time-series charts.
- **Workflows Replaced:**
  - Purchasing costly read-only or review licenses.
  - Assembling manual 60-slide PowerPoint presentations containing static trajectory captures.
  - Waiting for organizational IT clearance to install multi-gigabyte desktop client binaries.

### Stage 2: Cross-Disciplinary Digital Thread Integration

- **The Problem:** Single-domain tools are fundamentally incapable of validating multi-physics and cross-domain constraints. Systems architects define requirements in Cameo; thermal engineers model heat exchangers in Dymola; electrical teams model protection schemes in PSCAD; structural teams model casings in STEP CAD. Cross-domain inconsistencies are typically identified late during physical test-bench integration.
- **The Ansatz Workflow:**
  - Ansatz maintains a unified **Digital Thread Explorer** (`/thread`) powered by Triple Graph Grammars (TGG) and ModelScript's Salsa query engine.
  - Requirements authored in SysML v2 (`requirement def`) are bound directly to continuous differential algebraic equations (DAEs) in Modelica and electrical grid components in PSCAD.
  - Mathematical balance and constraint satisfaction are verified automatically across domain boundaries.
- **Workflows Replaced:**
  - Manual verification matrices maintained in disconnected spreadsheets.
  - Point-to-point co-simulation setups susceptible to algebraic loops and numerical divergence.
  - Unsynchronized requirements databases.

### Stage 3: Git-Native Engineering CI/CD and Pull Requests

- **The Problem:** Legacy tools treat source control as an afterthought. Binary model files cannot be inspected in traditional git diff tools, leading to blind merges, undetected regressions, and parameter drift.
- **The Ansatz Workflow:**
  - Repositories in Ansatz are backed by standard Git Smart HTTP storage.
  - Pull requests trigger automated validation pipelines:
    - **Visual Schematic Diffs:** Identifies added, removed, and modified components, connector ports, and routing coordinates.
    - **Trajectory Regression Testing:** Compares simulation trajectories against reference baselines using RMSE and Normalized Max Relative Error thresholds.
    - **Physical Rule Audits:** Evaluates unit consistency, DAE algebraic index, and domain safety standards (such as IEEE Std 2800 for power grids or EN 14363 for rail vehicles).
- **Workflows Replaced:**
  - Manual design review meetings dedicated to inspecting line-item changes.
  - Undetected parameter overwrites during multi-engineer project handoffs.
  - Unvalidated pull requests in engineering repositories.

### Stage 4: Living Engineering Decision Records (EDRs)

- **The Problem:** Organizational knowledge is commonly fragmented across internal wikis, static PDFs, and local spreadsheets. When project personnel change, the physical rationale, experimental telemetry, and bibliographic citations behind critical parameters are lost.
- **The Ansatz Workflow:**
  - Replaces static wiki entries with **Executable Engineering Decision Records (EDRs)**.
  - Each EDR incorporates:
    - Bibliographic references queried directly from OpenAlex and Crossref (`[@cite_key]`).
    - Embedded client-side simulation runners with locked or tunable parameter bands.
    - Experimental calibration datasets (CSV) paired with automated optimization routines (such as Nelder-Mead simplex or gradient descent).
- **Workflows Replaced:**
  - Internal documentation containing disconnected, outdated screenshots.
  - Static research papers whose governing equations cannot be evaluated or reproduced.
  - Spreadsheets storing untracked calibration constants.

### Stage 5: Primary Authoring and Cloud HPC Offload

- **The Problem:** High-dimension parameter sweeps, Monte Carlo reliability studies, and 3D continuum simulations monopolize local workstation CPU cores for hours, halting other engineering activities.
- **The Ansatz Workflow:**
  - Authors construct models within **Ansatz Studio** (`/studio`), utilizing Monaco code editing, language server diagnostics (`@modelscript/lsp`), and equation-level Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) stepping.
  - Parametric sweeps and surrogate model training are dispatched directly to remote Slurm HPC clusters or batched WebGPU kernels via the Ansatz Cloud Dispatcher.
- **Workflows Replaced:**
  - Workstation lockups during large computational batch sweeps.
  - Purchasing dedicated parallel computing toolbox licenses per user workstation.

```mermaid

    PSCAD -->|IEEE 2800 CI Gates| Registry
    Simulink -->|B2B Trajectory Parity| Morsel
    OLGA -->|Flow Assurance Pre-Flight| Studio
```

### 1. Modelica & Multi-Physics (vs. Dymola & Wolfram SystemModeler)

- **Incumbent Pain:** Dymola licenses require dedicated Windows workstations and flex license management; OpenModelica lacks collaborative web workspaces.
- **Ansatz Solution:**
  - Native in-browser GLR parsing and linear-memory DAE compilation.
  - Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) simulation debugging: engineers step through continuous-time integration intervals ($\Delta t$), monitor Jacobian condition numbers, and inspect algebraic state iterations inside VS Code / Studio.
  - Content-Addressable Package Registry (`/packages`) with automated dependency resolution, replacing manual folder unzipping.

### 2. Systems Modeling & MBSE (vs. Cameo & IBM Rhapsody)

- **Incumbent Pain:** Cameo is constrained by legacy SysML v1 constructs and heavyweight desktop runtimes, lacking direct numerical execution of physical differential equations.
- **Ansatz Solution:**
  - Native parser and Salsa query engine for **SysML v2** and **KerML**.
  - Direct translation of SysML v2 parts into continuous DAE representations for dynamic simulation.
  - Bidirectional visual editing between textual SysML v2 source code and graphical block definition diagrams (BDD) / internal block diagrams (IBD).

### 3. Electrical Power Systems (vs. PSCAD & PSS/E)

- **Incumbent Pain:** PSCAD relies on legacy Fortran toolchains, Windows operating system constraints, and cannot be integrated into automated cloud CI/CD pipelines.
- **Ansatz Solution:**
  - Fixed-step nodal admittance electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation directly from `.pscx` XML models.
  - Automated **IEEE Std 2800-2022** grid compliance testing (LVRT/HVRT voltage and frequency ride-through verification) executing as automated pull request checks.
  - Direct export of PSCAD schematics into standardized Modelica and FMI/SSP container topologies.

### 4. Dynamic Control Systems (vs. MATLAB / Simulink)

- **Incumbent Pain:** Massive software footprints (exceeding 40GB), proprietary binary `.slx` formats that resist version control, and costly per-toolbox pricing structures.
- **Ansatz Solution:**
  - Parsing and AST transformation of Simulink models into readable Modelica and C99 code.
  - Automated ISO 26262 Back-to-Back (B2B) trajectory equivalence testing verifying numeric output tolerances.
  - Shareable URL permalinks for instantaneous stakeholder evaluation without MATLAB installed.

### 5. Flow Assurance & Chemical Process (vs. SLB OLGA & Aspen HYSYS)

- **Incumbent Pain:** Specialized transient multiphase and chemical licenses represent substantial ongoing software expenditures ($50k+ per seat).
- **Ansatz Solution:**
  - Pre-flight automated linting for multiphase pipelines (evaluating Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy stability criteria, hydrate formation subcooling margins, and severe riser slugging risks).
  - Parsing and visualization of `.tpl` and `.ppl` trend/profile logs into interactive web charts and spatial pipeline elevation diagrams.

---

## Enterprise Trust and Security

To satisfy operational requirements in regulated and defense engineering environments, Ansatz provides specific architectural guarantees:

1. **Client-Side Sandbox Execution:** In Ansatz Morsel, compilation, Salsa dependency resolution, and numerical integration execute inside the client's WebAssembly sandbox. Model source code and equations do not need to be transmitted to remote servers.
2. **Cryptographic Data Sovereignty:** Every project repository is backed by standard Git Smart HTTP infrastructure with support for Ed25519 commit verification. Teams retain complete local data ownership and can clone or export full histories at any time.
3. **Air-Gapped On-Premises Deployment:** Organizations can deploy standalone Ansatz nodes (`ansatz-ce` or `ansatz-ee`) inside sovereign VPCs, Kubernetes clusters, or air-gapped internal intranets with LDAP, SAML/SSO, and Slurm HPC cluster federation.

================================================================================
DOCUMENT: ActivityPub Federation
CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/ansatz/federation
================================================================================

# ActivityPub Federation & Engineering Morsels

Ansatz implements the **W3C ActivityPub** standard (Server-to-Server and Client-to-Server) extended with an engineering namespace (`https://modelscript.org/ns/morsel#`) to enable decentralized collaboration across research labs, universities, and enterprise engineering hubs. Rather than confining models, simulations, and peer reviews to a single centralized silo, independent Ansatz instances federate, exchange executable artifacts, and verify cryptographic proofs across domains.

---

## 1. What is an Engineering Morsel?

In conventional social networks, posts consist of plain text, raster images, or static video. In Ansatz, posts carry **Morsels**—compact, self-contained, executable engineering payloads embedded directly inside ActivityStreams 2.0 `Note` or `Article` objects:

1. **Executable Multi-Physics Models**: Deflate-compressed (`#m=...`) or content-addressed source bundles across any of the 68 supported languages (`Modelica`, `SysML v2`, `PSCAD`, `CIM/CGMES`, `OLGA`, `SPICE`, `URDF`, `OpenSCAD`, `DICOM-RT`).
2. **Reproducible Simulation Trajectories**: Encapsulated DAE/ODE time-series datasets (`Vega-Lite` / Arrow binary attachments) paired with exact solver tolerances, Pantelides index metrics, and initial conditions.
3. **Interactive 3D CAD, FEA & CFD Views**: Compressed STEP B-Rep geometries, 3MF surgical guides, or VTK Unstructured Grid (`.vtu`) von Mises stress fields rendered directly in the feed via Three.js and `CanvasContextPool`.
4. **Semantic Architecture & Schematic Diffs**: Structural AST/DAE diffs (`PolyglotVersionDiffView`) highlighting added, modified, or deleted components and equations across Git revisions.

---

## 2. Federation Protocol & JSON-LD Schema

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Alice as "Alice (@alice@lab-a.org)"
    participant NodeA as "Ansatz Node A (Outbox)"
    participant NodeB as "Ansatz Node B (Inbox)"
    participant WorkerB as "Node B WASM Verification Worker"

    Alice->>NodeA: Sign post via `msx sign` (eddsa-jcs-2022) & publish Morsel
    NodeA->>NodeB: POST /api/v1/inbox (HTTP Signature + JSON-LD Create Activity)
    NodeB->>NodeA: GET /.well-known/webfinger & Fetch Actor Public Key
    NodeB->>WorkerB: Verify HTTP Signature, W3C Proof & SHA-256 Artifact Digest
    WorkerB-->>NodeB: Compile in sandboxed WASM arena & attach Verification Badge
    NodeB-->>Alice: Deliver to local followers & federated timeline
```

### 2.1 Actor Discovery via WebFinger (RFC 7033)

Every engineer and autonomous verification bot on an Ansatz node has a federated handle formatted as `@username@domain`. Remote instances resolve actor endpoints via RFC 7033 WebFinger:

```http
GET /.well-known/webfinger?resource=acct:alice@ansatz.social HTTP/1.1
Host: ansatz.social
Accept: application/jrd+json
```

The server returns a JSON Resource Descriptor (JRD) linking to the actor's ActivityPub profile document (`/api/v1/users/alice`), outbox (`/api/v1/users/alice/outbox`), shared inbox (`/api/v1/inbox`), and public key registry.

### 2.2 ActivityStreams 2.0 Payload with Engineering Extensions

When an engineer publishes a Morsel, the instance serializes an ActivityStreams 2.0 `Create` activity carrying both the human-readable Markdown/LaTeX commentary and the structured `morsel:artifact` attachment:

```json
{
  "@context": [
    "https://www.w3.org/ns/activitystreams",
    "https://w3id.org/security/v1",
    "https://w3id.org/security/data-integrity/v2",
    {
      "morsel": "https://modelscript.org/ns/morsel#",
      "dialect": "morsel:dialect",
      "codeHash": "morsel:codeHash",
      "daeMetrics": "morsel:daeMetrics"
    }
  ],
  "id": "https://ansatz.social/activities/98412",
  "type": "Create",
  "actor": "https://ansatz.social/api/v1/users/alice",
  "object": {
    "id": "https://ansatz.social/posts/4821",
    "type": "Note",
    "content": "<p>Verified LVRT reactive current injection on the 380 kV interconnector.</p>",
    "attachment": [
      {
        "type": "PropertyValue",
        "morsel:dialect": "modelica",
        "morsel:codeHash": "sha256:8f4e2b9a1c3d...",
        "morsel:daeMetrics": { "variables": 42, "equations": 42, "index": 1 }
      }
    ],
    "proof": {
      "type": "DataIntegrityProof",
      "cryptosuite": "eddsa-jcs-2022",
      "verificationMethod": "https://ansatz.social/api/v1/users/alice#ed25519-key-1",
      "proofPurpose": "assertionMethod",
      "proofValue": "z3y8Bk7..."
    }
  }
}
```

---

## 3. Dual-Layer Cryptographic Security

Ansatz separates **transport authentication** from **author non-repudiation**:

1. **Server-to-Server HTTP Signatures (`draft-cavage-http-signatures`)**: Every outbound `POST /api/v1/inbox` delivery is signed over `(request-target)`, `host`, `date`, and `digest` (`SHA-256` of the HTTP body) using the originating node's RSA-2048/Ed25519 actor key.
2. **End-to-End W3C Data Integrity Proofs (`eddsa-jcs-2022`)**: Engineers with **Signed Accounts** (`msx keys register`) sign the canonicalized JSON (RFC 8785 JCS) of their posts and models using their personal, non-custodial Ed25519 keypair (`msx sign`). Even if a remote server forwards or boosts (`Announce`) the post across multiple hops, any receiving node can independently verify that the author's mathematical equations and source code were not altered in transit.

---

## 4. Supported Activity Types

| Activity Type                  | Object             | Behavior                                                                                              |
| :----------------------------- | :----------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Create`                       | `Note` / `Article` | Publishes a new engineering post, threaded reply, or interactive Morsel attachment.                   |
| `Update`                       | `Note` / `Person`  | Updates an existing post (accompanied by a fresh `eddsa-jcs-2022` proof) or refreshes actor metadata. |
| `Follow` / `Accept` / `Reject` | `Actor`            | Establishes or revokes cross-instance follower subscriptions.                                         |
| `Announce`                     | `Note`             | Boosts a verified engineering post or simulation benchmark to local followers.                        |
| `Like`                         | `Note`             | Bookmarks and endorses an engineering artifact.                                                       |
| `Delete`                       | `Tombstone`        | Retracts a post and purges cached attachment blobs from federated nodes.                              |

---

## 5. Domain Moderation & Federation Policies

Instance administrators control inbound and outbound federation traffic via the **Federation** tab in `/admin` (or environment policies in air-gapped enterprise deployments):

| Policy Tier          | Behavior                                                                                           |
| :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Open Federation**  | Connects to any compliant ActivityPub node with valid HTTP Signatures and TLS.                     |
| **Domain Allowlist** | Restricts federation exclusively to approved partner organizations (e.g., OEM + Tier-1 suppliers). |
| **Silenced Domain**  | Remote posts are excluded from public/explore timelines and visible only to direct followers.      |
| **Suspended Domain** | All inbound and outbound ActivityPub deliveries and media caching with the domain are blocked.     |

# Polyglot Package Registry

The **Ansatz Package Registry** ([ansatz.social/packages](https://ansatz.social/packages)) provides versioned dependency management, cryptographic supply-chain verification, and pre-indexed symbol distribution for multi-domain engineering libraries. It supports native ModelScript packages alongside standard Modelica 3.x libraries, SysML v2 / KerML architecture packages, STEP AP242 CAD assemblies, and FMI/SSP containers.

---

## 1. Supported Package Formats

| Format             | Scope & Manifest                    | Primary Usage                                                                 |
| :----------------- | :---------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ModelScript**    | `package.json` / `modelscript.json` | Native multi-domain models, equations, formal contracts, and simulation decks |
| **Modelica**       | `package.mo` / `package.order`      | Complete Modelica 3.x libraries (MSL, OpenIPSL, Buildings, Thermal)           |
| **SysML v2**       | `sysml.library` / `.sysmlx`         | OMG Systems Modeling Language v2 and KerML requirement and architecture packs |
| **STEP & 3D CAD**  | `step.json` / `.stp` / `.scad`      | ISO 10303 AP214/AP242 B-Rep parts, kinematic mates, and ISO 23952 QIF plans   |
| **SSP Containers** | `SystemStructure.ssd` (`.ssp`)      | System Structure and Parameterization multi-FMU co-simulation topologies      |

---

## 2. Package Lifecycle & CLI Workflows

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Author Workspace (modelscript.json)"] -->|"msx pack --pre-index"| B["Deterministic .zip + .lsp-bundle.zip"]
    B -->|"msx publish --signature"| C["Ansatz Package Registry (SHA-256 CAS)"]
    C -->|"msx install @scope/pkg"| D["Consumer Workspace (modelica_modules/ + msx.lock)"]
```

### 2.1 Authoring & Manifest Configuration

Initialize a package manifest using `msx init` or configure `package.json` / `modelscript.json` with semantic version constraints, SPDX license identifiers, and maturity tier metadata:

```json
{
  "name": "@powergrid/entsoe-hvdc-lib",
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "license": "MPL-2.0",
  "modelscript": {
    "tier": "stable",
    "languages": ["modelica", "pscad", "cgmes", "sysml2"],
    "entry": "package.mo"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@modelscript/msl": "^4.0.0",
    "@powergrid/ieee2800-templates": "^1.4.0"
  }
}
```

### 2.2 Pre-Indexed Bundling & Cryptographic Publishing

Before publishing, `msx pack --pre-index` compiles the package's `SymbolIndex`, QUDV unit tables, and component SVG icons into a binary `.lsp-bundle.zip` snapshot so downstream IDE and browser consumers can load thousands of library symbols without cold-parsing every source file:

```bash
# Initialize a new package manifest
msx init

# Create an offline distribution archive with pre-indexed Salsa symbol tables
msx pack . --pre-index --out ./dist

# Publish the package to the registry with a dist-tag
msx publish . --tag latest

# Install a versioned package into modelica_modules/ and update msx.lock
msx install @powergrid/entsoe-hvdc-lib
```

---

## 3. Supply-Chain Security & Deterministic Lockfiles (`msx.lock`)

Engineering simulations for safety-critical aerospace, nuclear, and medical systems require strict provenance guarantees:

- **Content-Addressable Storage (SHA-256)**: Every published archive is indexed by its SHA-256 Merkle digest. Modifying a single byte of an equation or parameter table alters the digest and fails lockfile verification.
- **Detached Ed25519 Publisher Signatures (`--signature`)**: Publishers sign package digests using their registered Ed25519 keys (`msx keys`). During `msx install`, the CLI verifies both the SHA-256 integrity hash and the publisher's cryptographic signature.
- **SPDX License Compatibility Auditing**: During upload and installation, the registry parses SPDX license expressions (`AGPL-3.0-or-later`, `MPL-2.0`, `Apache-2.0`, `MIT`, or commercial licenses) and warns when a dependency tree mixes incompatible copyleft and proprietary terms.
- **Polyglot Standard Library Sync (`msx stdlib`)**: Built-in standard libraries across all 68 languages can be inspected and synchronized offline via `msx stdlib`.

---

## 4. Industrial Handover & Standards Export Gateways

Any package version hosted in the Ansatz Registry (or packed locally) can be cross-compiled into standardized industrial exchange containers:

- **IDTA Asset Administration Shell (`.aasx`)**: Generates an Industry 4.0 AAS v3.0 package containing `TechnicalData`, `SimulationModels` (FMI/FMU), and `HandoverDocumentation` submodels (`msx ddp to-aasx`).
- **ISO/PAS 81346 Digital Data Package (`.ddp`)**: Packages multi-aspect system reference designations (`=` function, `+` location, `-` product) and traceability graphs (`msx ddp pack`).
- **DIN SPEC 3105 Open Know-How (`okh.json`)**: Exports open-hardware bill-of-materials (BoM), CAD meshes, and manufacturing tolerances for distributed fabrication.

# Cloud HPC & Distributed Simulation

While interactive 1D DAE and multibody simulations execute directly in the browser via WebAssembly and WebGPU, large-scale multi-physics parameter sweeps, high-dimensional Monte Carlo uncertainty quantification, and continuum 3D finite-element (CalculiX/FEBio) or finite-volume CFD (SU2/OpenFOAM) meshes require dedicated cluster compute. Ansatz provides a unified **Cloud HPC Launcher** connecting the browser workbench and `msx cloud` CLI with remote Slurm HPC clusters and GPU worker pools.

---

## 1. Architecture: Browser & CLI to Slurm Cluster Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Studio / Morsel / msx cloud"] -->|"POST /api/v1/cloud/jobs"| B["Ansatz API Gateway & Credit Ledger"]
    B -->|"Deterministic .zip Bundle"| C["Slurm Controller (slurmctld / sbatch)"]
    C -->|"MPI / CUDA Allocation"| D["Compute Nodes (CPU / A100 / H100)"]
    D -->|"Zero-Copy RingBuffer Logs"| B
    B -->|"WebSocket Telemetry Stream"| A
    D -->|"Parquet Trajectories & .vtu Meshes"| E["Content-Addressed Object Storage"]
    E -->|"Presigned Range URL"| A
```

---

## 2. Compute Hardware Profiles & Credit Metering

Organizations and individual engineers allocate jobs against pre-configured hardware profiles. Credits are reserved atomically prior to `sbatch` submission and settled based on actual wall-clock core-seconds (`BillingService`), with unused reservations automatically refunded upon early termination or `msx cloud cancel`:

| Profile ID                | Hardware Allocation                                       | Rate      | Interconnect & Accelerator         | Target Workloads                                                                              |
| :------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :--------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `standard`                | 4 vCPU, 16 GB ECC RAM                                     | 10 cr/hr  | Shared NVMe scratch                | Stiff Modelica/PSCAD DAE sweeps, Sobol DoE (up to 512 runs), SPICE transient corners          |
| `high-memory`             | 16 vCPU, 256 GB ECC RAM                                   | 35 cr/hr  | High-bandwidth DDR5                | Full-grid ENTSO-E CGMES / PSS/E $N-1$ contingency screening, 3D tetrahedral FEA assembly      |
| `gpu-a100`                | 8 vCPU, 64 GB RAM, 1× NVIDIA A100                         | 80 cr/hr  | NVLink / CUDA 12                   | Batched ensemble DAE integration, Neural/PINN surrogate training, TOPAS Monte Carlo dose      |
| `hpc-mpi-64`              | 64 Cores (2 Nodes × 32 ranks), 128 GB RAM                 | 150 cr/hr | InfiniBand NDR (400 Gb/s)          | Distributed OpenMPI SU2/OpenFOAM RANS/LES aerodynamics and multi-well ECLIPSE reservoir decks |
| `emt-distributed-cluster` | 64 Cores (4 Nodes × 16 ranks), 4× NVIDIA A100, 128 GB RAM | 180 cr/hr | InfiniBand NDR & Shared RingBuffer | Multi-island EMT power grid partitioning with Bergeron transmission line delay decoupling     |

---

## 3. Containerized Slurm Job Dispatch & Sandboxing

When a job is submitted via the **Cloud Simulation Modal** in `/morsel` or via `msx cloud dispatch`:

1. **Deterministic Workspace Packaging**: The compiler resolves `msx.lock` dependencies, verifies SHA-256 digests, and packs the model, compiled `.wasm` arena snapshot, and solver configuration into a content-addressed bundle.
2. **Rootless Apptainer / Singularity Execution**: The Slurm job script runs inside an immutable, network-isolated Apptainer image (`modelscript-hpc-runtime.sif`) containing SUNDIALS 7.x (KLU/SuperLU_MT sparse linear solvers), CalculiX, SU2, and OpenMPI.
3. **Live Checkpointing & Preemption Recovery**: Long-running transient integrations periodically flush binary DAE state checkpoints (`checkpoint_<step>.bin`) to scratch storage so preempted spot allocations resume without losing progress.

---

## 4. Headless CLI Workflows (`msx cloud`)

Engineers and CI/CD pipelines can inspect hardware profiles, check organization credit balances, dispatch jobs, stream real-time solver logs, and download completed trajectory or mesh artifacts from the terminal:

```bash
# List available CPU/GPU execution profiles and credit rates
msx cloud profiles

# Check organization compute credit wallet balance
msx cloud balance

# Dispatch a workload to the high-memory or GPU cluster profile
msx cloud dispatch ThermalGrid.mo --profile high-memory --domain modelica

# Monitor active jobs and follow live worker stdout/stderr logs
msx cloud jobs
msx cloud status job_01j9x8k2m
msx cloud logs job_01j9x8k2m --follow

# Download completed Parquet trajectories and VTK (.vtu) field meshes
msx cloud download job_01j9x8k2m --output ./results
```

---

## 5. Interactive 3D Field & Trajectory Streaming

When continuum or ensemble simulations complete, results are indexed in object storage and streamed into the browser using HTTP Range requests:

- **3D Stress, Thermal & Velocity Fields**: Visualized from binary VTK Unstructured Grid (`.vtu`) and OpenUSD (`.usdc`) files with hardware-accelerated color maps, iso-surfaces, streamtubes, and interactive cutting planes.
- **Arrow / Parquet Time-Series Overlays**: Multi-gigabyte Monte Carlo fan charts (P10 / P50 / P90 quantile bands) and Bode envelopes are decimated on the fly using Largest-Triangle-Three-Buckets (LTTB) downsampling for smooth 60 FPS zooming.

# Self-Hosting Ansatz & ModelScript

Ansatz can be deployed as an independent federated instance, a public flagship cluster, or a private corporate intranet appliance using **Docker Compose**, **Cloudflare Tunnels (Zero Open Ports)**, or **Caddy** for automated TLS certificate provisioning.

---

## Deployment Architecture Profiles

Ansatz offers targeted deployment profiles to match your infrastructure sizing and operational goals:

| Profile              | Active Containers                                           | Target Use Case                                                                 | Database Engine                     | Min. RAM   |
| :------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :---------------------------------- | :--------- |
| **`flagship`**       | `caddy`, `web`, `api` (EE), `timescaledb`, `mqtt`, `tunnel` | `modelscript.org` + `ansatz.social` public cluster with dual-domain routing     | SQLite WAL + TimescaleDB            | 4–8 GB     |
| **`federated`**      | `caddy`, `web`, `api`, `timescaledb`, `mqtt`, `tunnel`      | Research lab with live IoT simulation telemetry streaming                       | SQLite WAL + TimescaleDB            | 4 GB       |
| **`federated-lite`** | `caddy`, `web`, `api`, `tunnel`                             | **Embedded DB only** (no Postgres/MQTT). Lightweight homelabs & VPS             | **SQLite WAL only**                 | **1–2 GB** |
| **`corporate`**      | `caddy`, `web`, `api` (EE), `timescaledb` (optional)        | Enterprise intranet, air-gapped enclave, SSO domain allowlist, internal `/docs` | SQLite WAL (+ optional TimescaleDB) | 2–4 GB     |
| **`quick-tunnel`**   | `caddy`, `web`, `api`, `quick-tunnel`                       | Zero-config demo with ephemeral `trycloudflare.com` URL                         | SQLite WAL only                     | 1.5 GB     |

---

## Zero-Open-Port Ingress via Cloudflare Tunnel

If you are hosting behind residential CGNAT, corporate firewalls, or on a developer workstation where opening ports `80` and `443` is impossible or undesirable:

1. Create a free tunnel in the [Cloudflare Zero Trust Dashboard](https://one.dash.cloudflare.com/) (**Networks → Tunnels → Create Tunnel**).
2. Route your public hostname (e.g., `hub.mydomain.org`) to `http://caddy:80`.
3. Add the tunnel token to your `.env`:
   ```dotenv
   CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN="eyJh..."
   ```
4. Start the stack:
   ```bash
   docker compose --profile federated-lite --profile tunnel up -d
   ```
5. You can now close all inbound firewall ports (`sudo ufw default deny incoming`). The tunnel connects outbound to Cloudflare Edge over encrypted QUIC/HTTP2.

---

## Quick Start Deployment

### 1. Scaffold or Download Configuration Files

You can scaffold the deployment directory with the `msx hub init` CLI command:

```bash
msx hub init --profile federated --dir ansatz --domain hub.mycompany.org
cd ansatz
```

Or download the compose files and runtime configs (`config/Caddyfile`, `config/mosquitto.conf`, and `config/init-timescaledb.sql`) directly with `curl`:

```bash
mkdir -p ansatz/config && cd ansatz
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/docker-compose.yml
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/docker-compose.prod.yml
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/.env.production.example
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/config/Caddyfile -o config/Caddyfile
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/config/mosquitto.conf -o config/mosquitto.conf
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/modelscript/modelscript/main/config/init-timescaledb.sql -o config/init-timescaledb.sql
cp .env.production.example .env
```

### 2. Configure Environment (`.env`)

```dotenv
PUBLIC_DOMAIN=hub.mycompany.org
PUBLIC_URL=https://hub.mycompany.org
NODE_ENV=production
JWT_SECRET=generate-with-openssl-rand-hex-32
TOTP_ENCRYPTION_KEY=generate-with-openssl-rand-hex-32

# Cloudflare Tunnel (optional for zero-port ingress; leave blank for direct Caddy ACME)
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# Headless Preinstallation (Optional: skip setup wizard automatically on first boot)
AUTO_SEED_ADMIN=true
ADMIN_INIT_USERNAME=admin
ADMIN_INIT_EMAIL=admin@mycompany.org
ADMIN_INIT_PASSWORD=StrongSecurePassword123!
DEPLOYMENT_PRESET=tier1_federated
```

### 3. Launch Services

#### Option A: Lightweight Homelab / VPS (Embedded SQLite only, ~1-2 GB RAM)

```bash
docker compose --profile federated-lite up -d
```

#### Option B: Full Federated Node (with TimescaleDB Telemetry Historian)

```bash
docker compose --profile federated up -d
```

#### Option C: Flagship Cluster (`modelscript.org` + `ansatz.social`)

Both `--profile flagship` and `--profile federated` activate the production stack (`caddy`, `web`, `api`). Add `--profile tunnel` to enable Cloudflare Zero Trust Tunnel ingress:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml \
  --env-file .env --profile flagship up -d
```

#### Option D: 1-Click Ephemeral Demo (No Account or Domain Needed)

```bash
docker compose --profile quick-tunnel up
```

## First-Run Setup Wizard (`/setup`) vs. Headless Preinstall

### Interactive Setup Wizard

When launching a fresh federated node without pre-seeded admin variables:

1. Open `https://hub.mycompany.org/setup` in your browser.
2. Select your **Deployment Profile**:
   - **Tier 1: Independent Federated Node:** Open ActivityPub S2S federation with peer nodes.
   - **Tier 2: Corporate Intranet Appliance:** Outbound federation disabled, restricted to corporate email domains.
   - **Tier 3: Public Flagship Hub:** Open registration with anti-Sybil verification.
3. Create the founding **Administrator Account** and initial cryptographic keys.
4. Complete configuration and download your initial baseline snapshot. The wizard locks permanently upon completion.

### Headless Preinstallation

For automated CI/CD, Terraform, or Ansible deployments, setting `ADMIN_INIT_USERNAME`, `ADMIN_INIT_PASSWORD`, and `DEPLOYMENT_PRESET` automatically provisions the administrator, applies tier settings, generates cryptographic keys, and permanently locks the setup wizard on first boot.

---

## Database Operations, Diagnostics & Hot Backups

- **Primary Application Database (Always Embedded SQLite WAL):** Users, social graph, ActivityPub outbox/inbox, packages, permissions, and audit logs run on high-performance `better-sqlite3` on the persistent `api-data` volume.
- **Telemetry Historian (Optional PostgreSQL / TimescaleDB):** Handled via TimescaleDB when the `federated` or `flagship` profile is active.

### Hot SQLite Backups & Diagnostics (`msx db`)

To create an online hot backup, run deep health checks, or export a redacted diagnostic bundle without stopping the service:

```bash
# Create an online SQLite WAL snapshot with SHA-256 verification
msx db backup --label nightly

# Or invoke inside the running production API container
docker compose exec api node apps/cli/dist/main.js db backup --label nightly

# Run deep operational health checks (SQLite integrity, audit hash-chain, disk headroom)
msx db doctor

# Generate a redacted diagnostic support bundle (zero secrets or password hashes)
msx db support-bundle --file support-diagnostic.json

# Export or import a portable instance migration bundle (settings, federation rules, flags)
msx db export-bundle --file migration-bundle.json
msx db import-bundle --file migration-bundle.json
```

Backups are recorded in `apps/api/data/backups/` and verified with SHA-256 checksums and SQLite `PRAGMA integrity_check`.

---

## Maintenance Mode, Step-Up Sudo & Prometheus Metrics

### Multi-Tiered Maintenance Mode

Operators can transition a node between four operational states via the **Admin Console → Settings** tab (`PATCH /api/v1/admin/settings`) or environment variables (`MSX_MAINTENANCE_MODE`, `MSX_MAINTENANCE_ETA`):

- **`off`**: Normal read/write operation.
- **`scheduled`**: Displays an upcoming maintenance window banner and `maintenanceEta` countdown across Web and Docs without blocking traffic.
- **`read_only`**: Allows `GET`/`HEAD`/`OPTIONS` browsing and package downloads while returning `503 Service Unavailable` (with `Retry-After`) on user mutations.
- **`lockdown`**: Blocks all non-admin requests while allowing staff administrators to perform upgrades or forensic recovery.

### Step-Up Sudo Mode (`REQUIRE_ADMIN_SUDO=true`)

Destructive administrative mutations (role promotions, database restores, migration bundle imports, and DMCA counter-notice restorations) support **Step-Up Sudo** verification (`POST /api/v1/admin/sudo`), issuing a short-lived 15-minute `admin_sudo` elevation token after re-verifying the administrator's password or TOTP code.

### Prometheus & OpenMetrics Endpoint

Scrape `GET /api/v1/admin/metrics` (authenticated with an admin Bearer token or `ms_bot_*` monitoring token) to collect OpenMetrics gauges and counters for Node.js heap/RSS memory, SQLite WAL & backup footprint, user/package/post totals, ActivityPub S2S delivery states, and HPC job queue depth.

---

## Upgrading & Rollback Runbook

### Standard Zero-Data-Loss Upgrade

1. **Enable Read-Only Drain (Optional):** Set Maintenance Mode to `read_only` in `/admin` or run a pre-upgrade snapshot:
   ```bash
   docker compose exec api node apps/cli/dist/main.js db backup --label pre-upgrade
   ```
2. **Preview & Apply Schema Migrations:**
   ```bash
   docker compose exec api node apps/cli/dist/main.js db upgrade --dry-run
   ```
3. **Pull New Images & Recreate Containers:**
   ```bash
   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env --profile flagship pull
   docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env --profile flagship up -d --wait --remove-orphans
   ```
4. **Verify Post-Upgrade Health:**
   ```bash
   docker compose exec api node apps/cli/dist/main.js db doctor
   ```

### Point-in-Time Rollback Procedure

If a deployment needs to be rolled back to a previous release:

1. **Restore the Pre-Upgrade SQLite Snapshot** (automatically creates a `pre-restore` safety backup before swapping the database file):
   ```bash
   docker compose exec api node apps/cli/dist/main.js db restore --file modelscript-backup-pre-upgrade.db
   ```
2. **Pin the Previous Container Image Tag** (`IMAGE_TAG=sha-<previous>` or `IMAGE_TAG=<previous-version>`) and restart:
   ```bash
   IMAGE_TAG=0.1.0 docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file .env --profile flagship up -d --wait
   ```

# Architecture Overview

ModelScript is built on a **data-oriented, WebAssembly-first compiler architecture**. Rather than allocating deep hierarchies of garbage-collected JavaScript AST wrapper objects, every stage of the compiler—from GLR parsing to DAE flattening, sparse linear algebra, and formal verification—operates on contiguous **Struct-of-Arrays (SoA)** arenas in WebAssembly linear memory.

---

## End-to-End Compilation Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Languages["Polyglot Source Languages (81 Formats — 24 Stable & 57 Beta)"]
        direction TB
        MO[".mo (Modelica 3.x) / .mod (AMPL)"]
        SYS[".sysml / .kerml / .reqif / .oscal.json"]
        STEP[".step / .usd / .qif / .scad / .3mf"]
        OWL[".owl / .ofn / .ttl (OWL2)"]
        SSP[".ssp / .ssd / .ssv (SSP 1.0/2.0)"]
        PSCAD[".pscx / .raw / .dsl / .epc / .dss / .cir / .va"]
        TELECOM[".optical / .ran / .fiber / .ocpp / .openadr"]
        CAE[".cfd / .su2 / .fea / .inp / .feb"]
        MBD[".spck / .calc / .adm / .urdf / .osim / .gtfs"]
        FLOW[".opi / .lps / .bkp / .gproms / .yaml / .pqi / .tough / .prj / .nam"]
        AUTO[".arxml / .st / .aml / .slx / .ez5"]
        SPACE[".oem / .opm / .xtce / .roc"]
        BIO[".sbml / .ant / .bngl / .sbol / .ctl / .cellml"]
        MED[".rtplan / .topas / .nii / .igtl"]
        MSX[".msx / .modelscript (ModelScript)"]
    end

    subgraph Frontend["1. Linear-Memory Parsing & Indexing (@modelscript/dsl)"]
        GLR["Native WASM GLR Parser (parser.wasm)"]
        CST["Linear Memory CST Arena"]
        IDX["SymbolIndexer & Unified WorkspaceIndex"]
    end

    subgraph Semantics["2. Incremental Semantic Engine (@modelscript/runtime)"]
        SALSA["Salsa QueryEngine (Memoized Dependency Graph)"]
        TGG["Triple Graph Grammar (TGG) & DPO Rewriting Engine"]
        LINT["CompilerLint & Multi-Domain Semantic Lints"]
    end

    subgraph Lowering["3. Arena DAE Lowering & Formal Verification"]
        FLAT["ModelicaFlattener (AssemblyScript WASM Kernel + TS Bridge)"]
        DAE["DAEBuilder (SoA Linear Memory: varData, exprData, eqData)"]
        THEORY["Multi-Domain Theory Coordinator (13 Domain Oracles)"]
    end

    subgraph Backend["4. Causalization, Codegen & Execution (@modelscript/simulate)"]
        BLT["Hopcroft-Karp Matching + Tarjan BLT + Pantelides Index Reduction"]
        SOLVE["SUNDIALS IDA / CVODE / Radau IIA / Rodas4P / TR-BDF2 / Tsit5 / Dommel EMT / WebGPU"]
        FMU["FMI 2.0 / 3.0 C99 & WASM FMU Exporter (@modelscript/exchange)"]
    end

    Languages --> GLR --> CST --> IDX --> SALSA
    SALSA --> LINT
    SALSA --> TGG
    SALSA --> FLAT --> DAE
    DAE --> THEORY
    DAE --> BLT --> SOLVE
    DAE --> FMU
```

---

## Core Architectural Pillars

### 1. Zero-Wrapper Linear Memory CST & DAE Arena

Equations, expressions, and statements are lowered directly from 32-bit linear-memory CST node pointers (`u32`) into `DAEBuilder` integer IDs (`VarId`, `ExprId`, `EqId`, `StmtId`). This eliminates garbage-collection pauses even when flattening multi-thousand-equation Modelica Standard Library (MSL) models.

### 2. Demand-Driven Incremental Compilation (Salsa)

Inspired by the Rust compiler (`rust-analyzer`), `QueryEngine` implements the **Salsa** incremental recomputation algorithm (`fetch → deep_verify → execute → backdate`). When a user edits a parameter in the IDE, only queries whose transitive input hashes actually changed are recomputed.

### 3. Polyglot Synchronization via Triple Graph Grammars (TGG)

Cross-language traceability is enforced algebraically via **Double-Pushout (DPO)** graph rewriting (`packages/dsl/src/tgg.ts`) with **Critical Pair Analysis (CPA)** confluence verification (`packages/dsl/src/cpa.ts`). Changes in SysML v2 requirements, Modelica parameters, STEP CAD assemblies, or ModelScript `@unmanaged` structs propagate bidirectionally without losing comments or formatting.

### 4. Multi-Domain Theory Coordinator ($\text{CDCL}(\mathcal{T})$)

Thirteen specialized **Domain Theory Oracles**—spanning OWL2 Description Logic (`OntologyTheoryOracle`), SysML v2 intervals (`ConstraintTheoryOracle`), Zones/Octagons (`AbstractDomainOracle`), Barrier Certificates & Taylor Flowpipes (`ContinuousSafetyOracle`), DAE trajectories (`DynamicSimulationOracle`), 3D B-Rep clearance (`SpatialPhysicsOracle`), FEA/CFD contracts (`CaeContractOracle`), DAE structural matching (`CausalizationOracle`), SI dimensional analysis (`DimensionalOracle`), Assume-Guarantee refinement (`EntailmentOracle`), Kirchhoff/stream conservation (`FlowAlgebraOracle`), AP242 GD&T stack-up (`ToleranceStackOracle`), and Conformal UQ (`UqOracle`)—exchange variable bounds and Nelson-Oppen equalities until a global fixpoint or minimal unsatisfiable core (`UnsatCore`) is reached.

---

# Monorepo Architecture: ModelScript & Ansatz

ModelScript and Ansatz are developed together within a single unified monorepo. This document details the architectural rationale, the four-layer taxonomy, and the boundary enforcement mechanisms that keep the computational engine decoupled from web and cloud platforms.

---

## The 4-Layer Architectural Taxonomy

To maintain modularity and avoid circular dependencies, the codebase is structured into four explicit layers:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Layer 4: Enterprise Edition (ee/)                                     │
│   • Air-gapped Ed25519 licensing, ITAR / NERC CIP, FDA 21 CFR Part 11  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 3: The Ansatz Platform (apps/web, apps/api, packages/embed)      │
│   • ansatz.social, package registry, ActivityPub, Cloud HPC, billing   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 2: Developer Tooling & Surfaces (apps/cli, desktop, ide, docs)   │
│   • msx CLI, VS Code Web extension, Tauri desktop app, VitePress portal │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Layer 1: Core Engine & Languages (languages/*, packages/{dsl,runtime…})│
│   • WASM GLR parsers, CST arena, DAEBuilder, solvers, TGG, CAD, FMI    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Layer 1: Core Engine & Languages

- **Directories:** `languages/*` (81 domain languages across `Stable` [24] and `Beta` [57] tiers) and `packages/{dsl,runtime,simulate,cad,diagram,exchange,lsp,mcp}`.
- **Rule:** Pure computation, formal theory, parsers, and solvers. Zero UI dependencies, zero database dependencies, and zero Express/HTTP servers.
- **Independence:** Can be compiled and embedded in any JavaScript, Node.js, WebAssembly, or desktop runtime.

### Layer 2: Developer Tooling & Surfaces

- **Directories:** `apps/cli`, `apps/ide`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/docs`.
- **Rule:** User-facing toolchains and documentation. Imports from Layer 1 to expose commands (`msx`), IDE extensions, and the reference manual.

### Layer 3: The Ansatz Platform

- **Directories:** `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `packages/embed`, `packages/react`, `packages/design-tokens`.
- **Rule:** The flagship web platform (`ansatz.social`), polyglot package registry, ActivityPub federation, Slurm HPC cluster execution, and enterprise team governance.
- **Relationship:** Consumes Layer 1 and Layer 2 packages via workspace dependencies, providing the visual modeling and collaborative cloud surface for the compiler.

### Layer 4: Enterprise Edition

- **Directories:** `ee/`.
- **Rule:** Commercial features subject to the Enterprise License. Open-core libraries in Layer 1 and Layer 2 never import from `ee/`.

---

## Architectural Rationale: Why a Unified Monorepo?

### 1. Atomic Co-Evolution

Ansatz is a scientific and engineering platform, not a simple CRUD service. When changes occur in the WebAssembly DAE arena, the CST parser nodes, or the solver output formats, the API dispatch layer and the browser-native WebAssembly UI are updated in the same commit.

### 2. Elimination of Publishing Bottlenecks

`@modelscript/api` and `@modelscript/web` consume over 20 internal workspace packages. Developing across separate repositories would require continuous version bumps, registry publishing, and downstream synchronization, introducing operational delay.

### 3. End-to-End Type Safety

TypeScript interfaces, AST node structures, and simulation results share exact definitions across the compiler, backend services, and web client. Breaking API changes are caught at compile time across all packages.

---

## Boundary Enforcement Mechanisms

Architectural separation is enforced automatically in CI:

1. **Nx Project Graph Verification (`npm run lint:repo`):**
   - The dependency graph is inspected by `scripts/check-nx-cycles.js`.
   - Core engine packages (`packages/*`) and languages (`languages/*`) are verified to have zero imports from `apps/*` or `ee/`.
2. **One-Way Open-Core Boundary:**
   - ESLint and `scripts/lint-package-manifests.ts` verify that open-core packages never declare dependencies on `@modelscript/ee`.
3. **Hardware-Aware Testing:**
   - Dynamic resource management in `scripts/test-coordinator.js` partitions tests based on CPU and memory availability.

DOCUMENT: DAE Arena in Linear Memory
CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/architecture/dae-arena
================================================================================

# Linear Memory DAE Arena & Lowering

The Differential Algebraic Equations (DAE) representation in ModelScript is implemented via `DAEBuilder` in `@modelscript/runtime` (`packages/runtime/src/dae/wasm_dae.ts`).

Unlike traditional compilers that construct linked expression trees using heap-allocated objects, `DAEBuilder` operates strictly on **flat, contiguous typed arrays** (Struct-of-Arrays) in WebAssembly linear memory.

---

## Arena Struct-of-Arrays (SoA) Layout

The arena maintains three primary contiguous arrays:

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      DAEBuilder Linear Memory                     │
├─────────────────┬──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┤
│ Buffer          │ Element Size     │ Contents                     │
├─────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ varData         │ 32 bytes         │ Name, type, variability,     │
│                 │                  │ causality, start value, flags│
├─────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ exprData        │ 16 bytes         │ OpKind, data1, leftExprId,   │
│                 │                  │ rightExprId                  │
├─────────────────┼──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┤
│ eqData          │ 24 bytes         │ EqKind, lhsExprId,           │
│                 │                  │ rhsExprId, flags             │
└─────────────────┴──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────┘
```

Every variable, expression, and equation is assigned a persistent 32-bit integer handle:

- `VarId`: Handle to a variable in `varData`
- `ExprId`: Handle to an expression node in `exprData`
- `EqId`: Handle to an equation in `eqData`

---

## Lowering Pipeline

Flattening a high-level Modelica model into linear DAE form proceeds in two coordinated layers:

### Layer 1: Components & Hierarchy

Reads Salsa queries (`instantiate`, `classInstance`, `variability`) to allocate variables and parameters in `DAEBuilder`:

- Scalar variables (`Real`, `Integer`, `Boolean`, `String`)
- Array dimensions and indices
- Start values, nominals, and min/max boundaries

### Layer 2: Equations & Statements

Walks the linear CST of the class body (`db.cstNode(classId)`):

- Lowers binary, unary, and call expressions directly into `ExprId` nodes in linear memory.
- Emits equality equations (`lhs = rhs`), initial equations, and algorithm statements.

---

## Expression Lowering Rules

To match OpenModelica's canonical output, the flattener applies specific normalization rules:

1. **Real Coercion in Binary Operations**: If one operand of an arithmetic operator is `Real` and the other is `Integer`, the integer operand is automatically cast to Real using `castToRealExpr()`.
2. **Negation Distribution**: Expressions of the form `-(a * b)` are rewritten canonically to `(-a) * b`.
3. **Binding Literal Kind Matching**: When a binding expression is lowered, `addIntLiteral()` is used for `VarType.Integer` and `addRealLiteral()` for `VarType.Real` (e.g. `parameter Real R = 100` becomes `100.0`).

---

## Optimization & Transformation Passes

Once lowered to the arena, equations pass through four high-performance transformations:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    LOWER["DAE Lowering"] --> FOLD["1. Constant Folding<br/>(foldArenaConstants)"]
    FOLD --> ALIAS["2. Alias Elimination<br/>(eliminateArenaAliases)"]
    ALIAS --> PANT["3. Pantelides Algorithm<br/>(Index Reduction)"]
    PANT --> BLT["4. Tarjan BLT<br/>(Block Lower Triangular Partition)"]
    BLT --> SOLVE["Numerical Solvers"]
```

1. **Constant Folding (`foldArenaConstants`)**: Recursively simplifies compile-time constant arithmetic expressions directly in the arena.
2. **Alias Elimination (`eliminateArenaAliases`)**: Detects trivial equality equations ($x = y$) generated by connectors and replaces all references with a single canonical variable handle.
3. **Pantelides Index Reduction**: Differentiates high-index algebraic constraints to reduce the DAE index to 1 or 0 for stable numerical integration.
4. **Tarjan BLT Partitioning**: Constructs the bipartite incidence graph between variables and equations, computes maximum matching, and finds Strongly Connected Components (SCC) using Tarjan's algorithm.

================================================================================
DOCUMENT: WASM GLR Parser
CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/architecture/glr-parser
================================================================================

# WebAssembly GLR Incremental Parser

ModelScript avoids external runtime parser dependencies. Instead, every supported language in `languages/` is parsed using a custom, ahead-of-time (AOT) compiled **Generalized LR (GLR)** parser executing directly in WebAssembly (`parser.wasm`).

The parser compiler is implemented in `@modelscript/dsl` under `packages/dsl/src/codegen/`.

---

## Why GLR in WebAssembly?

1. **Handling Complex Engineering Grammars**: Engineering modeling languages like Modelica and SysML v2 possess ambiguities that cannot be parsed by strict deterministic LR(1) or LALR parsers. The GLR algorithm handles non-deterministic grammar paths by branching parse stacks and pruning invalid branches dynamically.
2. **Zero-Allocation Memory Footprint**: Rather than allocating JavaScript AST object wrappers for every identifier and operator, tokens and CST nodes are laid out in a flat WebAssembly linear memory arena.
3. **Web-Native Performance**: The compiled `parser.wasm` executes at near-native speeds in both Node.js server environments and client-side browser contexts (such as the IDE and Ansatz Morsel).

---

## Parser Initialization

In TypeScript or AssemblyScript code, parsers are loaded and registered via `createWasmParser`:

```typescript
import { createWasmParser } from "@modelscript/modelica/parser";
import { Context } from "./src/context.js";

// Load the compiled WebAssembly parser binary
const modelicaWasmPath = require.resolve("@modelscript/modelica/parser.wasm");
const { parser } = await createWasmParser(modelicaWasmPath);

// Register file extension mapping in the compilation Context
Context.registerParser(".mo", parser);
```

---

## Linear CST Memory Layout

When a source file is parsed, the parser allocates a continuous buffer of node headers in linear memory. Each CST node is referenced by a 32-bit integer pointer (`u32` node offset) rather than an object reference:

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   Linear CST Node Arena                │
├───────────┬───────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────┤
│ Field     │ Offset    │ Type         │ Description     │
├───────────┼───────────┼──────────────┼─────────────────┤
│ typeId    │ 0         │ uint16       │ Node type code  │
│ flags     │ 2         │ uint16       │ Semantic flags  │
│ startOffset │ 4         │ uint32       │ Start byte pos  │
│ endOffset   │ 8         │ uint32       │ End byte pos    │
│ firstChild│ 12        │ uint32       │ Offset to child │
│ nextSibling│ 16       │ uint32       │ Offset to sib   │
└───────────┴───────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────┘
```

### Direct Field Accessors (`Cst`)

High-performance accessors read typed node properties directly from the linear buffer:

```typescript
import { Cst } from "@modelscript/modelica/language";

// Accessing child fields without constructing intermediate wrappers
const comp = Cst.ComponentClause.componentDeclarationList(node);
for (const decl of comp) {
  const nameNode = Cst.ComponentDeclaration.declaration(decl);
  const identifier = db.ast.text(nameNode);
}
```

---

## Incremental Re-Parsing

When editing code in the Language Server Protocol (LSP) or Studio, the GLR parser performs incremental tree re-use:

- Text edits pass line and character delta offsets.
- Unaffected subtrees in linear memory remain unchanged and are spliced into the new parse tree.
- Syntax diagnostics are generated during parsing and stored in the diagnostics arena.

================================================================================
DOCUMENT: Salsa Query Engine
CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/architecture/salsa-queries
================================================================================

# Salsa Incremental Query Engine

ModelScript's semantic analysis and symbol resolution pipeline is driven by an incremental query computation engine inspired by the open-source [Salsa](https://github.com/salsa-rs/salsa) incremental query framework.

The engine lives in `@modelscript/runtime` and provides memoized, demand-driven evaluation across multi-file engineering workspaces.

---

## The Query Life Cycle

Every query executed in ModelScript follows a 4-phase lifecycle to ensure maximum cache re-use and correct invalidation:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant Salsa as QueryEngine
    participant Storage as DependencyGraph

    Caller->>Salsa: query(key)
    alt Cache hit & revision current
        Salsa-->>Caller: Cached result (immediate)
    else Revision changed
        Salsa->>Storage: deep_verify(dependencies)
        alt All dependencies unchanged
            Storage-->>Salsa: verified valid
            Salsa->>Salsa: backdate revision
            Salsa-->>Caller: Cached result
        else Any dependency changed
            Storage-->>Salsa: invalid
            Salsa->>Salsa: execute query function
            Salsa->>Storage: record new dependencies
            Salsa-->>Caller: Fresh computed result
        end
    end
```

### The 4 Stages

1. **`fetch`**: Checks if the query result exists in the memoization table.
2. **`deep_verify`**: If the workspace revision has advanced, transitively checks whether any input queries or files that contributed to this result have actually changed.
3. **`execute`**: Re-runs the query definition if inputs have genuinely changed, tracking any newly accessed queries.
4. **`backdate`**: If re-executing the query produces an output value identical to the previous result, the query's revision is backdated to prevent cascading invalidation down the dependency tree.

---

## Key Compiler Queries

The query engine handles semantic resolution, type checking, and specialization:

| Query                   | Scope     | Description                                                                             |
| :---------------------- | :-------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `instantiate`           | Class     | Resolves all direct components, inherited elements, and nested declarations of a class. |
| `classInstance`         | Component | Specializes a generic class definition with specific modifier expressions.              |
| `resolveSimpleName`     | Scope     | Performs hierarchical lexical scoping and imports resolution.                           |
| `variability`           | Component | Computes effective variability: `constant`, `parameter`, `discrete`, or `continuous`.   |
| `causality`             | Component | Computes signal causality: `input`, `output`, or `internal`.                            |
| `effectiveModification` | Hierarchy | Resolves and merges class modification clauses across multi-level inheritance graphs.   |

---

## Salsa & Linear CST Synergy

AST wrapper nodes are **never** stored inside the Salsa cache. Storing heavy AST objects would duplicate memory and defeat garbage collection guarantees.

Instead:

- The Salsa cache stores semantic integer handles and primitive metadata (e.g. `SymbolId`, resolved `TypeInfo`, variability enums).
- Concrete CST nodes are retrieved on-demand from linear memory using `db.cstNode(symbolId)` only when lowering or evaluating equations.
