### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Proves cross-domain assertions spanning discrete architectural modes, differential equations, interval constraints, 3D CAD collisions, and clinical radiology/surgical safety envelopes.

- **Modifications**: Extended beyond traditional software theories (uninterpreted functions, bit-vectors) to **13 engineering domains** (matching [Multi-Domain Theory Coordinator](../architecture/theory-coordinator.md)) including OWL2 Description Logic, CAD B-Rep spatial physics, DAE continuous trajectories, and `RadiologyCasTheoryOracle` for radiation oncology and computer-assisted surgery; combines learned conflict clause propagation with Salsa query invalidation:

| #   | Theory Oracle                           | Domain (`TheoryDomain`)   | Primary Decision / Propagation Procedure                                                                                                                                                         |
| :-- | :-------------------------------------- | :------------------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1   | `OntologyTheoryOracle`                  | `ontology`                | $\mathcal{SROIQ}(\mathcal{D})$ Tableau reasoning over OWL 2 axioms, class disjointness, and property domains                                                                                     |
| 2   | `ConstraintTheoryOracle`                | `constraints`             | HC4 interval arithmetic and relational constraint propagation over SysML v2 requirements                                                                                                         |
| 3   | `AbstractDomainOracle`                  | `abstract_interpretation` | Floyd-Warshall Difference Bound Matrix (DBM) closure over Zone ($x_i - x_j \le c$) and Octagon ($\pm x_i \pm x_j \le c$) domains                                                                 |
| 4   | `ContinuousSafetyOracle`                | `continuous_safety`       | Control Barrier Function (CBF) Lie-derivative positivity and Taylor-model flowpipe reachability                                                                                                  |
| 5   | `DynamicSimulationOracle`               | `simulation`              | Sensitivity-guided DAE trajectory integration (CVODE/IDA) with exact zero-crossing root finding                                                                                                  |
| 6   | `SpatialPhysicsOracle`                  | `spatial`                 | 3D CAD B-Rep minimum clearance distance, mass budget, and BVH interference checks                                                                                                                |

## 3. Craig Interpolation

### Academic Citations

- **Craig, W. (1957)**. _"Linear reasoning. A new form of the Herbrand-Gentzen theorem."_  
  **Journal of Symbolic Logic**, 22(3), pp. 250–268. DOI: [10.2307/2963593](https://doi.org/10.2307/2963593)
- **McMillan, K. L. (2003)**. _"Interpolation and SAT-based model checking."_  
  **Computer Aided Verification (CAV 2003)**, LNCS 2725, pp. 1–13. DOI: [10.1007/978-3-540-45069-6_1](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-45069-6_1)
- **Pudlák, P. (1997)**. _"Lower bounds for resolution and cutting planes proofs and monotone computations."_  
  **Journal of Symbolic Logic**, 62(3), pp. 981–998. DOI: [10.2307/2275583](https://doi.org/10.2307/2275583)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Given unsatisfiable mutually contradictory formulas $A \land B \models \bot$, Craig interpolation synthesizes an interpolant $I$ such that:
$$A \implies I \quad \text{and} \quad I \land B \models \bot$$
where $\text{vars}(I) \subseteq \text{vars}(A) \cap \text{vars}(B)$.

- **Modifications**: Employs Pudlák-McMillan resolution graph traversal to generate certified interpolants explaining cross-domain requirement violations without revealing proprietary subsystem equations.

## 3. Worst-Case Optimal Joins (WCOJ / Leapfrog Triejoin)

### Academic Citations

- **Ngo, H. Q., Porat, E., Ré, C., & Rudra, A. (2012)**. _"Worst-case optimal join algorithms."_  
  **ACM PODS '12**, pp. 37–48. DOI: [10.1145/2213556.2213565](https://doi.org/10.1145/2213556.2213565)

  **ICDT '14**, pp. 96–106. DOI: [10.4230/LIPIcs.ICDT.2014.96](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ICDT.2014.96)
- **Atserias, A., Grohe, M., & Marx, D. (2008)**. _"Size bounds and query plans for relational joins."_  
  **IEEE FOCS '08**, pp. 739–748. (The AGM Bound)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Traditional binary relational joins suffer from exponential intermediate result explosions on cyclic subgraphs (e.g. triangle topologies between ports, connectors, and component definitions). WCOJ guarantees runtime strictly bounded by the Atserias-Grohe-Marx (AGM) bound, achieving $\mathcal{O}(N^{3/2})$ for triangle queries rather than $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$.

- **Modifications**: Formulates Leapfrog Triejoin iteration orders using descending vertex degree heuristics; emits execution plans directly into the AOT WebAssembly compilation engine.

## 1. Spacer CHC Engine (Generalized PDR)

### Academic Citations

- **Komuravelli, A., Gurfinkel, A., & Chaki, S. (2014)**. _"SMT-Based Model Checking for Recursive Programs."_  
  **Computer Aided Verification (CAV 2014)**, LNCS 8559, pp. 17–34.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-319-08867-9_2](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-08867-9_2)
- **Hoder, K., & Bjørner, N. (2012)**. _"Generalized Property Directed Reachability."_  
  **Theory and Applications of Satisfiability Testing (SAT 2012)**, LNCS 7317, pp. 157–171.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-31612-8_13](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-31612-8_13)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Constrained Horn Clauses (CHCs) represent systems of logical relations of the form:
$$\forall X. \; \phi(X) \land P_1(X) \land \dots \land P_k(X) \implies H(X)$$
Spacer solves CHCs by combining inductive generalization, Craig interpolation, and under-approximated reachability trees without bounding the unrolling depth. In ModelScript, Spacer verifies infinite-state state machine transitions and recursive cyber-physical control architectures.

- **Modifications**: Directly integrates with ModelScript's in-WASM CDCL SAT core and Craig interpolator; implements specialized heuristics for linear real arithmetic over cyber-physical invariants.

---

## 2. IC3 / Property Directed Reachability (PDR)

### Academic Citations

- **Bradley, A. R. (2011)**. _"SAT-based model checking without unrolling."_  
  **VMCAI 2011**, LNCS 6538, pp. 70–87.  
  DOI: [10.1007/978-3-642-18275-4_7](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-18275-4_7)
- **Een, N., Mishchenko, A., & Brayton, R. (2011)**. _"Efficient implementation of property directed reachability."_  
  **Formal Methods in Computer-Aided Design (FMCAD 2011)**, pp. 125–134.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Proves whether safety property $P$ holds across all reachable states of a discrete or hybrid transition system without unrolling the transition relation $T(s, s')$ to a fixed horizon $k$.

- **Modifications**: Maintains inductive clause frames $F_0, F_1, \dots, F_k$ where $F_i$ over-approximates states reachable in up to $i$ steps; uses counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) to block Proof Obligations (POBs); propagates clauses forward to find an inductive invariant ($F_i \equiv F_{i+1}$) proving unbounded safety.

---

## 3. Stochastic Barrier Certificates (`wasm_stochastic_barrier.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Prajna, S., Jadbabaie, A., & Pappas, G. J. (2007)**. _"A framework for worst-case and stochastic safety verification using barrier certificates."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control**, 52(8), pp. 1415–1428.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TAC.2007.902736](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2007.902736)
- **Kushner, H. J. (1967)**. _Stochastic Stability and Control._  
  **Academic Press**.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

For continuous-time stochastic differential equations (Itô diffusions) driven by standard Wiener processes $W_t$:
$$dx(t) = f(x) \, dt + \sigma(x) \, dW_t$$
deterministic trajectories do not exist, and safety verification requires bounding the tail probability that $x(t)$ ever enters an unsafe region $\mathcal{X}_u = \{ x \mid \|x\|_2 \ge r_u \}$.

`StochasticBarrierSynthesizer` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_stochastic_barrier.ts`) synthesizes non-negative supermartingale barrier candidates $B(x) = x^T P x \ge 0$ using the **infinitesimal generator** $\mathcal{L}$ of the Itô process:
$$\mathcal{L} B(x) = \nabla B(x) \cdot f(x) + \frac{1}{2} \text{tr}\!\left(\sigma(x) \sigma(x)^T \nabla^2 B(x)\right) \le -c$$

- **Doob's Maximal Supermartingale Inequality**: Bounds the infinite-horizon and finite-horizon probability of unsafe set entry via:
  $$\mathbb{P}\!\left(\sup_{t \ge 0} \|x(t)\|_2 \ge r_u\right) \le \frac{B(x_0) + \frac{\text{tr}(\Sigma P)}{2 \alpha}}{\lambda_{\min}(P) r_u^2} \le \delta_{\text{risk}}$$
  where $\Sigma = \sigma(0)\sigma(0)^T$ is the diffusion noise covariance and $\alpha$ is the linearized drift decay rate.
- **Soundness & Rigor Reporting**: Emits structured `VerificationVerdict` diagnostics distinguishing fast linearized quadratic risk estimates from Sum-of-Squares (SOS) / LP certified supermartingales.

---

## 4. WebGPU Datalog / OWL 2 RL Saturation Reasoner (`webgpu_reasoner.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Motik, B., Patel-Schneider, P. F., & Parsia, B. (2012)**. _"OWL 2 Web Ontology Language: Profiles (Second Edition) — OWL 2 RL."_  
  **W3C Recommendation**. [https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-profiles/](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl2-profiles/)
- **Warshall, S. (1962)**. _"A theorem on Boolean matrices."_  
  **Journal of the ACM**, 9(1), pp. 11–12. DOI: [10.1145/321105.321107](https://doi.org/10.1145/321105.321107)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Large-scale systems engineering ontologies (`languages/owl2/` and SysML v2 KerML specialization hierarchies) contain $10^5$ to $10^7$ ABox/TBox assertions. Evaluating transitive role closures (`subClassOf`, `partOf`, `satisfies`) and SHACL numeric property constraints sequentially on the CPU becomes a bottleneck during workspace-wide verification.

`WebGPUOntologyReasoner` (`packages/runtime/src/gpu/webgpu_reasoner.ts`) implements a massively parallel GPU relational join and saturation co-processor with a CPU SIMD bitset fallback:

- **Bit-Packed Adjacency Matrix (`BitsetGraph`)**: Encodes an $N \times N$ directed graph as a flat `Uint32Array` where each node row $u$ occupies $\lceil N / 32 \rceil$ 32-bit words, achieving $32\times$ memory compression and single-instruction bitwise row unions.
- **Parallel Logarithmic Doubling in WGSL (`TRANSITIVE_CLOSURE_WGSL`)**: Dispatches compute workgroups (`workgroups = ceil(N / 64)`) over ping-pong storage buffers (`bufIn`, `bufOut`) for $\lceil \log_2 N \rceil + 1$ doubling rounds, computing the full reflexive-transitive closure $R^*$ in $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ GPU passes.
- **Parallel SHACL Constraint Kernel (`SHACL_VALIDATION_WGSL`)**: Validates `SHACLNumericConstraint` bounds (`minInclusive`, `maxInclusive`, `expectedClassId`) across strided `Float32Array` instance attribute tables and writes compact violation bitsets.

---

## 5. ISO 26262 / DO-178C Back-to-Back Equivalence Verification (`b2b_verifier.ts`, `v_cycle_verifier.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **ISO 26262-6:2018 & ISO 26262-8:2018**. _Road vehicles — Functional safety — Part 6: Product development at the software level (Table 7: Back-to-back comparison test between model and code) & Part 8: Supporting processes (Clause 11: Confidence in the use of software tools, TCL1)._
- **RTCA DO-178C /DO-331 (2011)**. _Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification — Model-Based Development and Verification Supplement._

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Safety-critical automotive (ISO 26262 ASIL-D) and avionics (DO-178C DAL-A) standards require proving that generated embedded production code (zero-allocation C99 or standalone WASM FMU artifacts) is numerically and behaviorally equivalent to the high-level specification model (SysML v2 / Modelica).

`B2BEquivalenceVerifier` (`packages/runtime/src/simulation/b2b_verifier.ts`, orchestrated by `UnifiedVerifier` in `packages/runtime/src/simulation/unified_verifier.ts`) automates end-to-end **Model-in-the-Loop (MiL) vs. Software-in-the-Loop (SiL)** back-to-back verification:

1. **MiL Reference Trajectory Execution**: Simulates the high-level DAE arena (`simulateArenaAsync`) over $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{stop}}]$ to obtain reference trajectories $y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t)$.
2. **Standalone C99 Code Generation & Cryptographic Hashing**: Invokes `generateStandaloneCSources` (`@modelscript/exchange/fmu`) to emit self-contained, zero-allocation C99 sources (`<Model>_standalone.h`, `<Model>_standalone.c`), computing a SHA-256 artifact digest (`cSourceHash`) for V-cycle traceability.
3. **Automated Test Harness & Native Compilation**: Synthesizes a deterministic C99 fixed-step RK4 test harness (`<Model>_b2b_harness.c`), compiles the binary via `gcc -O2 -Wall -Wextra -std=c99 -lm`, and streams CSV output trajectories $y^{\text{SiL}}_j(t_k)$.
4. **Bisimulation & Signal-Tolerance Equivalence Checking**: Aligns SiL samples against binary-searched linearly interpolated MiL trajectories and verifies the combined absolute/relative tolerance envelope across all $K$ time steps and $M$ output signals:
   $$\forall j \in \{1, \dots, M\}, \; \forall k \in \{1, \dots, K\}: \quad \left| y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t_k) - y^{\text{SiL}}_j(t_k) \right| \le \epsilon_{\text{abs}} + \epsilon_{\text{rel}} \left| y^{\text{MiL}}_j(t_k) \right|$$

## 1. Bourdoncle Weak Topological Ordering (WTO) Fixpoint Solver

### Academic Citations

- **Bourdoncle, F. (1993)**. _"Efficient chaotic iteration strategies with widenings."_  
  **Formal Methods in Programming and Their Applications**, LNCS 735, pp. 128–141. DOI: [10.1007/BFb0039704](https://doi.org/10.1007/BFb0039704)
- **Cousot, P., & Cousot, R. (1977)**. _"Abstract interpretation: A unified lattice model for static analysis of programs by construction or approximation of fixpoints."_  
  **ACM POPL'77**, pp. 238–252. DOI: [10.1145/512950.512973](https://doi.org/10.1145/512950.512973)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Computes sound abstract over-approximations of state variables across complex nested loops and recursion without simulating unbounded trajectories.

- **Modifications**: Implements Bourdoncle's recursive hierarchical WTO decomposition to identify minimal loop heads; accelerates convergence using delayed widening ($\nabla$) followed by monotonic narrowing ($\Delta$).

---

## 2. Two Variables Per Inequality (TVPI) Polyhedral Domain

### Academic Citations

- **Simon, A., King, A., & Howe, J. M. (2002)**. _"Two Variables per Inequality as an Abstract Domain."_  
  **LOPSTR 2002**, LNCS 2664, pp. 71–89. DOI: [10.1007/3-540-36388-2_7](https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-36388-2_7)
- **Nelson, G. (1978)**. _"An $n^{O(\log n)}$ algorithm for the two-variable-per-inequality integer programming problem."_  
  **Technical Report**, Stanford University.

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Captures planar relational linear invariants of the form:
$$a x_i + b x_j \le c \quad (a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q})$$
Much more expressive than simple intervals or octagons, allowing ModelScript to prove physical conservation laws (e.g. $p_1 + p_2 = \text{const}$) without the exponential vertex-facet explosion of general convex polyhedra.

- **Modifications**: Planar Graham-scan convex hull algorithms in WebAssembly typed memory; relational projection routines optimized for physical parameter spaces.

---

## 3. Octagon Difference Bound Matrices (DBM) Domain

### Academic Citations

- **Miné, A. (2006)**. _"The octagon abstract domain."_  
  **Higher-Order and Symbolic Computation**, 19(1), pp. 31–100.  
  DOI: [10.1007/s10990-006-8609-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10990-006-8609-1)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Restricts linear relationships to constraints of the form:
$$\pm x_i \pm x_j \le c$$
Achieves cubic time complexity $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$ via Floyd-Warshall shortest path algorithms over $2n \times 2n$ potential graphs.

- **Modifications**: Direct integration into the `@modelscript/dsl` type inference system and `AbstractDomainOracle` in the Nelson-Oppen coordinator.

## 4. Array Segment Partitioning

### Academic Citations

- **Cousot, P., Cousot, R., & Logozzo, F. (2011)**. _"A Parametric Segmentation Functor for Fully Automatic and Scalable Array Content Analysis."_  
  **ACM POPL'11**, pp. 505–518. DOI: [10.1145/1926385.1926444](https://doi.org/10.1145/1926385.1926444)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Verifies large array equations and indexed multi-dimensional components in Modelica without unrolling every array index into separate scalar variables. Partitions index sets into contiguous segments whose bounds and elements share uniform properties.

## 5. Delay Differential Equation (DDE) Method-of-Steps Flowpipes (`wasm_dde_flowpipe.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Bellman, R., & Cooke, K. L. (1963)**. _Differential-Difference Equations._  
  **Academic Press**.
- **Zou, L., Fränzle, M., Xue, B., & Zhan, N. (2015)**. _"orda: An Ode and Dde Reachability Analysis Tool."_  
  **SETTA 2015**, LNCS 9409, pp. 109–123. DOI: [10.1007/978-3-319-25942-0_8](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-319-25942-0_8)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

Physical transport delays, networked control loops, and Modelica `delay(x, tau)` operators yield infinite-dimensional Delay Differential Equations (DDEs):
$$\dot{x}(t) = f\big(t, x(t), x(t - \tau)\big), \qquad x(t) \in \Phi(t) \text{ for } t \in [-\tau, 0]$$
`DdeFlowpipeSolver` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_dde_flowpipe.ts`) implements **Method-of-Steps** reachability propagation across consecutive delay horizons $[0, \tau], [\tau, 2\tau], \dots$:

- **History Interval Buffering**: Maintains a timestamped ring buffer `historyMap` storing both nominal trajectories $\bar{x}(t)$ and interval/zonotope tube enclosures $\mathcal{X}(t) = [\underline{x}(t), \overline{x}(t)]$. For $t - \tau \le t_0$, queries evaluate the initial functional history enclosure $\Phi(t - \tau)$; for $t - \tau > t_0$, historical enclosures are interpolated from stored flowpipe steps.
- **Interval Picard Enclosure Step**: Advances the state tube across $[t_k, t_k + \Delta t]$ by combining current state bounds $\mathcal{X}(t_k)$ and delayed history bounds $\mathcal{X}(t_k - \tau)$:
  $$\mathcal{X}(t_{k+1}) = \mathcal{X}(t_k) + \Delta t \cdot \square f\big(t_k, \mathcal{X}(t_k), \mathcal{X}(t_k - \tau)\big)$$
- **Epistemic Soundness Tagging**: Explicitly tags the resulting `VerificationVerdict` with rigor metadata (`heuristic` vs. `certified`) so downstream safety monitors distinguish fast corner-sampled delay tube estimates from fully Taylor-enclosed flowpipes.

---

## 6. Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) PDE Level-Set Reachability (`wasm_hji_solver.ts`)

### Academic Citations

- **Mitchell, I. M., Bayen, A. M., & Tomlin, C. J. (2005)**. _"A time-dependent Hamilton-Jacobi formulation of reachable sets for continuous dynamic games."_  
  **IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control**, 50(7), pp. 947–957.  
  DOI: [10.1109/TAC.2005.851439](https://doi.org/10.1109/TAC.2005.851439)
- **Jiang, G. S., & Shu, C. W. (2000)**. _"Weighted ENO schemes for Hamilton-Jacobi equations."_  
  **SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing**, 21(6), pp. 2126–2143.  
  DOI: [10.1137/S106482759732455X](https://doi.org/10.1137/S106482759732455X)

### ModelScript Rationale & Modifications

When verifying safety of nonlinear control systems under worst-case adversarial disturbances $d \in \mathcal{D}$ and control authority $u \in \mathcal{U}$, convex set-propagation (zonotopes) can suffer from wrapping effects. `HjiLevelSetSolver` (`packages/runtime/src/analysis/wasm_hji_solver.ts`) computes the exact **Backward Reachable Tube (BRT)** by solving the zero-sum differential game **Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) PDE** viscosity solution on an Eulerian level-set grid:
$$\frac{\partial V}{\partial t} + \min \left\{ 0, \; \min_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \max_{d \in \mathcal{D}} \nabla V(x, t) \cdot f(x, u, d) \right\} = 0, \qquad V(x, 0) = \ell(x)$$
where the sub-zero level set $\mathcal{K}_{\text{unsafe}} = \{ x \mid \ell(x) \le 0 \}$ defines the target failure region and $\{ x \mid V(x, T) \le 0 \}$ captures all initial states from which the adversary $d$ can force the trajectory into $\mathcal{K}_{\text{unsafe}}$ within horizon $T$ despite optimal safety control $u$.

- **5th-Order WENO Upwind Spatial Reconstruction (`weno5Derivatives`)**: Approximates left and right spatial derivatives $(p^-, p^+)$ along each state axis using 3-stencil smoothness indicators ($s_1, s_2, s_3$) and nonlinear weights $a_k = \frac{\gamma_k}{(\epsilon + s_k)^2}$, eliminating spurious oscillations near non-smooth value-function kinks.
- **Lax-Friedrichs Numerical Hamiltonian**: Evaluates the saddle-point Hamiltonian $H(x, p) = \min_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \max_{d \in \mathcal{D}} p \cdot f(x, u, d)$ at central gradients $p = \frac{1}{2}(p^- + p^+)$ augmented by artificial viscosity dissipation:
  $$\hat{H}(x, p^-, p^+) = H\left(x, \frac{p^- + p^+}{2}\right) - \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i} \alpha_i (p_i^+ - p_i^-), \qquad \alpha_i = \max_{u, d} |f_i(x, u, d)|$$
- **Monotone BRT Accumulation**: Steps the level-set array backward in time with `nextV[idx] = Math.min(V[idx], V[idx] - dt * dVdt)` and reports the exact unsafe volume fraction across the state space.

---

## Upstream & Downstream Pipeline Connections

- **Upstream Inputs**:
  - Control-flow graphs, `delay(x, tau)` equations, and continuous vector fields from `ModelicaFlattener`.
  - Adversarial disturbance bounds $\mathcal{D}$ and safety level-set specifications $\ell(x) \le 0$ from SysML v2 verification cases.
- **Downstream Consumers**:
  - Feeds numeric intervals into [`HC4 Contractor`](./theory-coordinator.md) and [`Nelson-Oppen Coordinator`](./theory-coordinator.md).
  - Certifies backward reachable tubes and delay flowpipes in `UnifiedVerifier` (`msx verify`).
  - Eliminates out-of-bounds array access and division-by-zero compiler warnings at compile time.

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

1. **Semidefinite Programming (SDP) for Verified Safety**: Formal continuous verification of non-linear physical models requires proving that state trajectories $\mathbf{x}(t)$ never breach unsafe operating envelopes. Synthesizing polynomial Lyapunov functions $V(\mathbf{x}) > 0$ and barrier certificates $B(\mathbf{x}) \le 0$ reduces to finding Sum-of-Squares (SOS) decompositions:
   $$p(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{z}(\mathbf{x})^T Q \, \mathbf{z}(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0 \iff Q \succeq 0$$
   By implementing a native primal-dual interior-point SDP solver in WebAssembly, ModelScript provides mathematically verified stability proofs directly in the browser and CLI without relying on external monolithic commercial solvers.
2. **Multiple Shooting BVP for Optimal Trajectories**: Boundary Value Problems (BVPs) govern optimal trajectory planning, model predictive control (MPC), and periodic limit cycle detection with split boundary conditions:
   $$g(\mathbf{y}(t_0), \mathbf{y}(t_{\text{end}}), \mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{0}$$
   Standard single shooting suffers from catastrophic numerical instability on stiff or chaotic dynamics. Multiple shooting subdivides the time horizon into $M$ subintervals, guaranteeing numerical stability and fast Newton-Raphson convergence.
3. **Constructive Solid Geometry (CSG) for Multi-Physics 3D Packaging**: Lumped-parameter 1D physical models (Modelica) rely on 3D geometric properties (mass, inertia tensor, aerodynamic drag area, hydraulic volume). ModelScript evaluates OpenSCAD models into normalized CSG solid trees (`@modelscript/cad`), auto-tagging boundary patches (`inlet`, `outlet`, `wall`, `symmetry`) for downstream OpenCascade B-Rep evaluation, STEP export, and SU2/OpenFOAM CFD meshing.

---

## Mathematical Formulation & Execution Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SOS["Polynomial Barrier / Lyapunov Inequalities"] --> SDP_SOLVER["WASM Primal-Dual Interior-Point SDP<br/>Minimize tr(C X) s.t. A(X) = b, X ⪰ 0<br/>Cholesky Factorization & Central Path"]
    SDP_SOLVER --> CERT["Formal SOS Witness Certificate"]

    BVP_REQ["BVP Problem & Split Boundary Conditions"] --> BVP_SOLVER["Multiple Shooting Solver<br/>1. Subdivide Horizon [t_0, t_M]<br/>2. Tsit5 Parallel Forward Steps<br/>3. Continuity & Boundary Residuals<br/>4. WASM LU Factorization"]
    BVP_SOLVER --> TRAJ["Converged Optimal State Trajectory"]

    SCAD_CODE["OpenSCAD / STEP Geometry"] --> CSG_EVAL["CSG & StepMesher (@modelscript/cad & simulate)<br/>Tet4/Tet10 Meshing & Prismatic Boundary Inflation"]
    CSG_EVAL --> CONTINUUM["WebGPU D3Q19 LBM CFD & Corotational PCG FEA"]
    CSG_EVAL --> MECH_VERIFY["Swept-Volume Clearance, GD&T Stack-Up & Inverse CAD"]
```

### 1. Primal-Dual Interior Point SDP Solver

Solves standard primal and dual semidefinite programs:
$$\text{Primal: } \min_{X \in \mathbb{S}^n} \text{tr}(C X) \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \text{tr}(A_i X) = b_i, \; X \succeq 0$$
$$\text{Dual: } \max_{y \in \mathbb{R}^m, S \in \mathbb{S}^n} b^T y \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \sum_{i=1}^m y_i A_i + S = C, \; S \succeq 0$$

- **Central Path Following**: Enforces the perturbed complementarity condition $X S = \mu I$ with barrier parameter $\mu = \frac{\text{tr}(X S)}{n}$.
- **WASM Linear Algebra**: Predictor-corrector search directions $(\Delta X, \Delta y, \Delta S)$ are computed using fast in-memory Cholesky factorizations (`wasm_gaussian.ts`), with backtracking line search to ensure $X + \alpha \Delta X \succ 0$ and $S + \alpha \Delta S \succ 0$.

### 2. Multiple Shooting BVP Solver

Subdivides the horizon $[t_0, t_{\text{end}}]$ into $M$ subintervals with mesh points $t_0 < t_1 < \dots < t_M = t_{\text{end}}$:

- **State Trajectory Variables**: Introduces free initial conditions $\mathbf{s}_m$ at each node $t_m$.
- **Subinterval Integration**: Integrates forward from $t_m$ to $t_{m+1}$ using adaptive `tsit5`:
  $$\mathbf{y}(t_{m+1}; \mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{p})$$
- **Matching Residual System**: Solves the $(M \cdot n + k) \times (M \cdot n + k)$ simultaneous nonlinear system:
  $$F_m(\mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{s}_{m+1}) = \mathbf{y}(t_{m+1}; \mathbf{s}_m, \mathbf{p}) - \mathbf{s}_{m+1} = \mathbf{0}, \quad m = 0, \dots, M-1$$
  $$g(\mathbf{s}_0, \mathbf{s}_M, \mathbf{p}) = \mathbf{0}$$
- **Newton-Raphson Update**: Evaluates sensitivity Jacobians along trajectories and solves the block-banded linear system via WASM Gaussian LU elimination.

### 3. OpenSCAD CSG Engine & CFD Boundary Tagging

Transforms procedural CSG trees into boundary-tagged solid geometries:

- Evaluates transformations (`translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, `mirror`) and regularized Boolean operators (`union`, `difference`, `intersection`).
- Decorates faces with CFD boundary tags (`tagPatch`, `BoundaryPatchType`: `inlet`, `outlet`, `wall`, `symmetry`), for handoff to automated SU2 mesh generators.

### 4. 3D Continuum Physics & B-Rep Meshing (`packages/simulate`)

ModelScript embeds native 3D continuum fluid, structural, and volumetric meshing engines that couple directly to 1D DAE simulations:

1. **WebGPU D3Q19 Lattice Boltzmann Method (LBM) CFD Solver (`webgpu-lbm-runner.ts`)**:
   - Discretizes the Boltzmann transport equation over a 19-velocity 3D lattice (`D3Q19`) stored in a zero-copy Structure-of-Arrays arena (`CfdFieldArena`) with ping-pong distribution buffers (`f0`, `f1`) and WGSL compute shader execution (`LBM_D3Q19_WGSL`, workgroups $8 \times 8 \times 4$):
     $$f_i^{\text{post}}(\mathbf{x}, t) = f_i(\mathbf{x}, t) - \omega_{\text{loc}}\!\left(f_i(\mathbf{x}, t) - f_i^{\text{eq}}(\rho, \mathbf{u})\right), \qquad f_i^{\text{eq}} = w_i \rho \!\left(1 + 3(\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u}) + \frac{9}{2}(\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u})^2 - \frac{3}{2}\|\mathbf{u}\|^2\right)$$
   - **Smagorinsky Subgrid LES Turbulence**: Dynamically adapts the local relaxation frequency $\omega_{\text{loc}} = (\tau_0 + \Delta\tau_{\text{LES}})^{-1}$ from the non-equilibrium momentum flux tensor $\Pi_{\alpha\beta}^{\text{neq}} = \sum_i c_{i\alpha} c_{i\beta} (f_i - f_i^{\text{eq}})$.
   - **Bouzidi Curved Boundaries & Moving-Wall FSI**: Applies sub-cell linear interpolation for curved solid obstacles ($\delta_{\text{wall}} < 0.5$ vs. $\delta_{\text{wall}} \ge 0.5$), injects moving-wall momentum $\Delta f_i = 6 w_i \rho (\mathbf{c}_i \cdot \mathbf{u}_{\text{wall}})$ for two-way aeroelastic FSI, and integrates surface drag forces via momentum exchange.
2. **3D Tet4/Tet10 Linear/Nonlinear Corotational Elasticity & Thermal FEA Solver (`fea-solver.ts`)**:
   - Assembles global sparse stiffness $K$ and consistent mass $M$ matrices in Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format for 4-node linear (`Tet4Element`) and 10-node quadratic (`Tet10Element`) tetrahedra.
   - **Corotational Large-Rotation Kinematics**: Extracts element rigid-body rotation $R_e \in \text{SO}(3)$ from the deformation gradient $F = e_0 E_0^{-1}$ via 6-step Higham polar decomposition iterations $R_{k+1} = \frac{1}{2}(R_k + R_k^{-T})$, rotating local element stiffness blocks $K_{\text{rot}} = R_e K_e R_e^T$ for geometric nonlinearity invariance.
   - **Jacobi-Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG) & Newmark-$\beta$ Dynamics**: Solves static equilibrium $K u = f$ and Rayleigh-damped transient elastodynamics $M \ddot{u} + (\alpha_M M + \beta_K K)\dot{u} + K u = f$ using unconditional-stability Newmark-$\beta$ ($\beta = 0.25, \gamma = 0.5$) time stepping, outputting nodal/element von Mises stresses and yield safety factors.
3. **STEP B-Rep Tetrahedral Mesher & Prismatic Boundary-Layer Extrusion (`step-mesher.ts`)**:
   - `StepMesher` converts ISO 10303-21 STEP B-Rep entities and watertight surface triangulations into volumetric `Tet4` / `Tet10` meshes (`Tet4Mesher`), classifies exterior boundary patches (`PatchClassifier`), extrudes viscous prismatic inflation layers along `WALL_BODY` surfaces (`BoundaryLayerExtruder`), evaluates Jacobian/aspect-ratio quality (`MeshQualityAnalyzer`), and exports ready-to-run CalculiX (`*.inp`) and SU2 (`*.su2`) decks.

### 5. Mechanical Swept-Volume, GD&T Stack-Up & Inverse CAD (`packages/cad`)

1. **Dynamic Swept-Volume Collision & Clearance Envelopes (`dynamic-clearance.ts`)**:
   - `DynamicClearanceVerifier` bridges continuous reachability flowpipes (`TrajectoryStepEnclosure[]`) into 3D CAD assemblies (`Assembly`). At each time step, it propagates interval state enclosures $[x_i^{\text{lo}}, x_i^{\text{hi}}]$ through translational Minkowski sums, rotational corner-envelope expansions, and soft-tissue/compliant cavity morphing (`volume_radial` $s = (V/V_0)^{1/3}$, `anisotropic`, and `modal` skinning).
   - Evaluates exact pairwise AABB separation distances (`computeAABBDistance`) and closest witness points (`computeAABBClosestPoints`), automatically synthesizing a 3D counterexample CAD assembly at the worst-case collision timestamp $t^*$ if any clearance rule is violated.
2. **Worst-Case, Statistical RSS & Coupled Thermal-Elastic GD&T Stack-Up (`tolerance-stack.ts`)**:
   - `ToleranceStackVerifier` verifies 1D/3D kinematic assembly gap loops across directional contributors ($d_i \in \{+1, -1\}$) combining bilateral manufacturing tolerances $[t_i^L, t_i^U]$, thermal expansion over $[T_{\min}, T_{\max}]$ ($\Delta L_{\text{th}} = L_0 \alpha_{\text{CTE}} \Delta T$), and axial elastic deflection under dynamic loads $[F_{\min}, F_{\max}]$ ($\Delta L_{\text{el}} = \frac{F L_0}{E A}$):
     $$g_{\text{min, WC}} = \sum_{i} d_i L_{0,i} + \sum_{i} \min(d_i t_i^L, d_i t_i^U) + \Delta g_{\text{th, min}} + \Delta g_{\text{el, min}}, \qquad \sigma_{\text{RSS}} = \sqrt{\sum_{i} \left(\frac{t_i^U - t_i^L}{6}\right)^2}$$
3. **Certified Bi-Directional CAD Parameter Inversion (`parameter-inversion.ts`)**:
   - `ParameterInversionEngine` closes the loop from 1D system optimization back to 3D MCAD source code. Given target mass/inertia constraints (`solveLengthForMass`, `scaleDimensionsForMass`) or optimized Modelica parameters, `patchMcadSourceCertified` verifies candidate dimensions against a multidisciplinary `SafeRegionGuard` ($\mathcal{P}_{\text{safe}}$ box bounds and buckling/stress/clearance predicates) before rewriting the parametric MCAD AST and regenerating STEP geometry.
4. **3D Spatial Formal Verification Overlays (`verification-overlay.ts`)**:
   - Projects mathematical proof artifacts from `@modelscript/runtime` and `@modelscript/simulate` directly onto 3D CAD assemblies (`Three.js`, glTF 2.0, and OpenUSD `.usda`):
     - **Reachability Tube Envelopes (`buildReachabilityTubeOverlay`)**: Extrudes interval Taylor-Model state flowpipes ($[x_i^{\text{lo}}(t), x_i^{\text{hi}}(t)]$) into semi-transparent 3D swept bounding-tube meshes colored by temporal progression or safety margin.
     - **SOS Barrier & Lyapunov Iso-Surface Shells (`buildBarrierShellOverlay`)**: Evaluates the zero-level set $B(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ (or level surface $V(\mathbf{x}) = c$) of a synthesized Sum-of-Squares polynomial certificate over a 3D spatial grid to render invariant safety shells around robotic manipulators and aerospace vehicles.
     - **Dynamic Clearance Witness Vectors (`buildDynamicClearanceOverlay`)**: Renders minimum-distance witness arrows and crimson collision capsules between nearest B-Rep faces at the critical timestamp $t^*$.

### 6. ECAD / PCB Geometry, Autorouting & DRC (`packages/cad/src/ecad/`)

1. **RS-274X Gerber Aperture Evaluation & Excellon Drill Synthesis (`gerber.ts`)**:
   - `generateManufacturingFiles` compiles multi-layer `PCBLayout` models (`TopCopper`, `BottomCopper`, `InnerCopper1/2`, `Top/BottomSilkscreen`, `Top/BottomSolderMask`, `BoardOutline`) into IPC-compliant **RS-274X Gerber** (`%FSLAX46Y46*%`, $10^{-6}\text{ mm}$ integer precision) with deduplicated aperture macros (`%ADD10C,...*%`, circle/rect/oval pads, $0.1\text{ mm}$ negative-polarity solder mask expansion `%IPNEG*%`) and **Excellon** NC drill programs (`drill.xln`, `METRIC,TZ`).
2. **Multi-Layer Interactive & Constrained PCB Trace Router (`engine/router.ts`)**:
   - `PCBRouter` (`pcb-router.ts` / `engine/router.ts`) implements a multi-layer trace routing engine supporting pad snap-targeting (`snapToPad`), $90^\circ$ Manhattan (`manhattanRoute`) and $45^\circ$ octilinear (`diagonal45Route`: $\text{diag} = \min(|\Delta x|, |\Delta y|)$) segment constraints, and automatic plated through-hole via insertion (`insertVia`) on layer transitions.
3. **Euclidean Trace/Pad Clearance Design Rule Checking (`engine/drc.ts`)**:
   - `runDRC` (`pcb-drc.ts` / `engine/drc.ts`) executes non-blocking geometric verification across copper layers, checking minimum trace widths, trace-to-trace, trace-to-pad, and pad-to-pad Euclidean clearances ($d(\mathbf{p}_1, \mathbf{p}_2) - \frac{w_1 + w_2}{2} \ge c_{\min}$), via drill and annular ring minimums ($r_{\text{outer}} - r_{\text{drill}} \ge a_{\min}$), point-to-segment board-outline polygon distances (`minDistToPolygon`), and unconnected ratsnest net completeness.

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

Physical engineering schematics (such as Modelica connection diagrams, SysML v2 Internal Block Diagrams, and hydraulic/piping schematics) require strict geometric conventions:

- **Orthogonal Edges**: Connections must run strictly along horizontal and vertical channels with clean $90^\circ$ bends.
- **Port-Constraint Preservation**: High-degree engineering components have physical boundary pins (e.g. electrical resistors have pins $p$ and $n$ on opposite faces; hydraulic valves have ports $A$, $B$, $P$, $T$). Layout engines must place connection points on explicit component boundaries rather than abstract node centers.
- **Zero-Obstacle Penetration**: Wires must never traverse component bounding boxes.
- **Bus Disambiguation**: Multi-variable connections between blocks must not collapse onto identical collinear segments.

ModelScript implements the **Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM)** pipeline augmented with a **Global Port ILP Solver** and **Dogleg Channel Router** natively in the browser and CLI.

---

## Three-Phase Layout & Routing Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    INPUT["Modelica Connects / SysML v2 Item Flows"] --> PORT_OPT["Phase 1: Port Constraint Optimization<br/>(Face Assignment & Cross-Free Ordering)"]
    PORT_OPT --> TSM["Phase 2: Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM)<br/>1. Planarization & Crossing Minimization<br/>2. Orthogonal Shape via Network Flow<br/>3. Metric Coordinate Compaction"]
    TSM --> ROUTER["Phase 3: Orthogonal Channel Routing<br/>1. Normal Outward Port Stubs<br/>2. Obstacle-Avoiding Bend-Penalized A*<br/>3. Staggered Parallel Dogleg Offsets"]
    ROUTER --> RENDER["SVG / Canvas / Studio Viewport"]
```

### 1. Port Constraint & Continuous Alignment Solver

Resolves port assignment along component perimeters ($x, y \in \partial \text{Node}$):

- **Discrete Face Selection**: Assigns ports to Cardinal sides (`top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`) minimizing Manhattan connection distance:
  $$\min \sum_{e = (u_i, v_j) \in E} \| \mathbf{p}(u_i) - \mathbf{p}(v_j) \|_1$$
- **Causality Biasing**: Automatically places `input` ports on the left face and `output` ports on the right face for signal-flow blocks.
- **Collinear Port Snapping**: Enforces 0-bend straight lines whenever two connected ports are horizontally or vertically aligned within a configurable tolerance `straightTolerance`.

### 2. Topology-Shape-Metrics (TSM) Engine

Extends Tamassia's Kandinsky model for high-degree engineering vertices:

1. **Planarization**: Replaces unavoidable edge crossings with dummy vertices of degree 4.
2. **Orthogonalization (Minimum Bend Flow)**: Formulates bend minimization as a minimum-cost network flow problem over the dual graph, assigning angles $\alpha \in \{90^\circ, 180^\circ, 270^\circ, 360^\circ\}$ to faces.
3. **Compaction**: Solves two independent 1D longest path problems on horizontal and vertical constraint DAGs to compute minimal integer grid coordinates.

### 3. Obstacle-Avoiding Dogleg Channel Router

Renders clean multi-segment connection polylines:

- **Perpendicular Port Stubs**: Edge paths extend outward along the port normal vector by a distance `stubLength` before turning.
- **A\* Grid Search with Bend Penalty**: Avoids component AABB bounding boxes using fast `segmentIntersectsRect` intersection tests while penalizing unnecessary turns:
  $$\text{Cost}(p \to q) = \text{dist}(p, q) + \lambda_{\text{bend}} \cdot [\text{isTurn}(p, q)]$$
- **Staggered Parallel Channels**: Multi-wire bus connections share a common corridor but are offset by `parallelIndex * channelSpacing`, preventing overlapping lines.

### 4. Specialized Engineering Diagram Layouts

Beyond acausal block schematics, ModelScript provides domain-specific geometric layout engines tailored to safety, behavioral, and power-systems engineering notations:

1. **Fault Tree Gate Hierarchy Layout (`fault-tree.ts` / `fault-tree-layout.ts`)**:
   - `synthesizeFaultTreeDiagram` transforms Minimal Cut Sets ($\text{MCS} = \{ C_1, \dots, C_m \}$) into four-tier standardized Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) diagrams:
     - **Tier 1 ($y = 40$)**: Top Hazard Event rect node centered at $x_{\text{center}} = W / 2$.
     - **Tier 2 ($y = 160$)**: Root Boolean `OR` gate (`createGateMarkup("OR")` SVG bezier shield) aggregating cut-set branches.
     - **Tier 3 ($y = 280$)**: Intermediate `AND` gates for multi-point failure cut sets ($\text{order} > 1$), while order-1 Single Points of Failure (SPOFs) route directly in high-visibility crimson (`#dc2626`) to basic events.
     - **Tier 4 ($y = 420$)**: Deduplicated circular Basic Event leaf nodes (`basicEventNodesMap`) distributed symmetrically across the horizontal span.
2. **UML / SysML v2 Sequence & Activity Swimlane Layouts (`sequence-layout.ts`, `swimlane-layout.ts`)**:
   - **Dual-Axis Sequence Layout (`computeSequenceLayout` / `applySequenceLayout`)**: Orders participant lifelines left-to-right ($x_i = x_{\text{left}} + i \cdot \Delta x_{\text{lifeline}} + W_{\text{hdr}}/2$), renders dashed vertical lifeline stems (`__seq_stem_*`), and stacks temporal messages top-to-bottom ($y_{k+1} = y_k + \Delta y_{\text{msg}}$) with distinct styling for synchronous (`sync`), asynchronous (`async`), dashed `reply`, and self-loop (`isSelf`, $1.5\times$ vertical spacing) messages.
   - **2D Activity Swimlane Partitioning (`applySwimlaneLayout`)**: Groups SysML v2 action nodes into vertical or horizontal allocation partitions (`SwimlanePartition`), sizing uniform lane containers (`swimlane_<id>`) to the maximum member stack height and routing cross-lane object/control flows via `port-orthogonal-astar`.
3. **PSCAD & PowerFactory Power-System Single-Line Diagram (SLD) & Block Schematics (`pscad-diagram-builder.ts`, `powerfactory-diagram-builder.ts`)**:
   - `buildPscadDiagram` and `buildPowerFactoryDiagram` render `.pscx`/`.pslx` and DIgSILENT PowerFactory `.dsl`/`.dgs` models into IEEE-standard Single-Line Diagrams and AVR/Gov/PSS composite block diagrams with voltage-coded busbar glyphs ($\ge 200\text{ kV}$ red `#ff5252`, $\ge 69\text{ kV}$ amber `#ffab40`, $< 69\text{ kV}$ cyan `#40c4ff`), specialized IEEE apparatus vector glyphs (`transformerGlyph`, `generatorGlyph`, `inverterIbrGlyph`, `breakerGlyph`, `surgeArresterGlyph`, `faultGlyph`, `converterBridgeGlyph`), solder-dot wire T-junctions, and orthogonal feeder routing.
4. **Protection Relay Log-Log TCC, Distance R-X Plane & Generator P-Q Capability Plots (`tcc-diagram-builder.ts`, `rx-diagram-builder.ts`, `pq-diagram-builder.ts`)**:
   - **Time-Current Characteristic (TCC) Log-Log Plots (`buildTccDiagram`)**: Renders multi-decade log-log ($10^0\dots 10^5\text{ A}$ vs. $10^{-2}\dots 10^3\text{ s}$) overcurrent relay (`IEEE Moderately/Very/Extremely Inverse`, `IEC Standard/Very/Extremely Inverse`, `Definite Time`) and fuse melting/clearing curves alongside annotated Coordination Time Interval (CTI) margin arrows.
   - **Distance Protection R-X Impedance Plane (`buildRxDiagram`)**: Plots Zone 1, Zone 2, and Zone 3 Mho circles and quadrilateral reach polygons, transmission line impedance vectors $Z_L \angle \theta_L$, load encroachment blinders, and apparent fault impedance trajectories $Z_{\text{app}}(t)$ in the complex $R + jX$ plane.
   - **Synchronous Generator P-Q Capability Envelopes (`buildPqDiagram`)**: Synthesizes active-vs-reactive ($P\text{–}Q$) operating envelopes bounded by armature current heatingCircles, field current rotor heating arcs, stator end-region core heating limits, prime-mover MW limits, and Under-Excitation Limiter (UEL) / steady-state stability boundaries.
5. **Hydraulic & Stormwater Pipe Network Topological Diffs (`water-network-diff.ts`)**:
   - `diffWaterNetworks` and `renderWaterNetworkDiffSvg` compare baseline and proposed EPANET / SWMM `.inp` pipe networks, highlighting added/removed/resized conduits, junction pressure deltas $\Delta p$, and flow reversals on spatially anchored municipal layouts.

### 5. Semantic Visual Diffing, CST 3-Way Merge & Collaborative Presence

1. **AST-Aware Structural Graph Diffing & Mental-Map Stabilization (`visual-diff-graph.ts`, `visual-diff-renderer.ts` / `visual-diff.ts`)**:
   - `buildVisualDiffGraph` computes a semantic delta between `Base` and `Head` diagram revisions, classifying nodes and edges into `added`, `deleted`, `modified`, and `unchanged` states (`DiffStatus`).
   - **Breaking Interface Detection**: Inspects property and port changes (`diffProperties`) against architectural breaking keys (`direction`, `isAbstract`, `typeName`, `multiplicity`, `causality`, `variability`, `flowDirection`) and flags deleted components or port-count mutations as `MODIFIED (BREAKING)`.
   - **Anchor-Preserving Layout Stabilization (`computeIncrementalStabilization`)**: Locks `Base` node coordinates as immutable spatial anchors while iteratively relaxing newly added/modified `Head` nodes to eliminate bounding-box overlaps without destroying the reviewer's spatial mental map.
2. **Tree-Edit-Distance CST Semantic Diff & 3-Way Merge Engine (`semantic_diff.ts` in `@modelscript/dsl`)**:
   - `diffEntities` and `mergeEntities3Way` (`msx merge`) match declarations across `base`, `ours`, and `theirs` revisions by stable semantic key (`kind::name`) and dice-coefficient structural similarity ($\ge 0.55$) to detect renames, equations, and parameter modifications while ignoring formatting whitespace.
   - Automatically merges non-overlapping edits and isolates true concurrent collisions (`modify-modify`, `delete-modify`, `add-add`) with line/column spans.
3. **CRDT / WebSocket Cursor, Selection Lock & Spatial Delta Synchronization (`collab-manager.ts`)**:
   - `CollabManager` coordinates real-time multi-user diagramming over WebSocket and VS Code Live Share transports:
     - **60 FPS Spatial Delta Streaming (`broadcastSpatialDelta`)**: Streams live component drag transformations (`PlacementItem`) with Last-Write-Wins (`LWW`) timestamp conflict resolution (`d.timestamp >= existing.timestamp`).
     - **Component Selection Locks (`SelectionLock`)**: Broadcasts per-peer component locks with distinct peer colors and automatic stale-peer heartbeat eviction (`purgeStalePeers`).
     - **Anchored Visual Review Comments (`DiagramComment`)**: Synchronizes spatially pinned sticky-note threads (`addComment`, `resolveComment`) directly on the schematic canvas.

## ModelScript Architectural Rationale

ModelScript compiles and indexes multi-million-element engineering workspaces, including the complete Modelica Standard Library (MSL), SysML v2 standard libraries (KerML), ISO 10303 STEP schemata, and OWL2 domain ontologies.

Representing these vast semantic graphs using standard JavaScript object heaps incurs:

- Extreme memory bloat (JavaScript objects typically consume 40–80 bytes of overhead per node).
- Heavy Garbage Collector (GC) pressure and unpredictable pause times during interactive IDE editing.
- Slow pointer chasing across cache lines.

To solve this, ModelScript implements **compact, zero-GC data structures** operating directly inside WebAssembly 64-bit linear memory.

---

## Architecture of Core WASM Structures

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    WORKSPACE["Workspace Indexer & AST Symbols"] --> ROARING["Roaring Bitmaps<br/>12-byte Chunk Descriptors<br/>Array / Dense Bitset"]
    WORKSPACE --> TRIE["Front-Coded Dictionary<br/>Shared Prefixes (8-entry blocks)<br/>+ Robin Hood Hash Map"]
    WORKSPACE --> BTREE["Paged B+ Tree (4KB Slotted Pages)<br/>Subject-Predicate-Object (SPO)<br/>Predicate-Object-Subject (POS)"]
    ROARING --> SALSA["Salsa Query Dependency Tracking"]
    TRIE --> INTERN["Symbol & IRI ID Interning"]
    BTREE --> SPARQL["WCOJ Pattern Matching & SPARQL Engine"]
```

### 1. Unmanaged Roaring Bitmaps

Partitions the 32-bit integer space into $2^{16} = 65{,}536$ chunks based on the upper 16 bits:

- **12-Byte Chunk Descriptor**:
  ```
  Offset 0..3:   [key: u16] | [containerType: u16]
  Offset 4..7:   [containerPtr: u32]
  Offset 8..9:   [cardinality: u16]
  Offset 10..11: [capacity: u16]
  ```
- **Adaptive Containers**:
  - **Array Container**: Used when cardinality $< 4{,}096$. Elements are stored as sorted `u16` integers in linear memory.
  - **Bitmap Container**: When cardinality reaches $4{,}096$, the container automatically converts to a dense 8,192-byte bitset ($1{,}024 \times \text{u64}$ words), allowing bitwise `AND`, `OR`, `XOR` operations at hardware SIMD speeds.

### 2. Front-Coded String & IRI Dictionary

Engineering identifiers and semantic URIs often share massive common prefixes:

```
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#PartDefinition
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#ItemDefinition
http://modelscript.io/sysml2/core#ActionDefinition
```

The front-coded dictionary partitions sorted strings into blocks of size $K = 8$:

- **Header String**: Stored uncompressed at the beginning of each block.
- **Suffix Entries**: Encoded as `[commonPrefixLen: u8, suffixLen: u8, suffixBytes]`.
- **Hybrid Lookups**: Combines front-coding (achieving 75–85% memory compression) with a zero-cost 64-bit Robin Hood hash map (`UnmanagedMap64`) for $O(1)$ string-to-ID interning.

### 3. Paged 4KB Slotted B+ Tree

Stores billions of semantic assertions and relational tuples:

- **4KB Slotted Page Layout (32-byte header + 254 entries)**:
  ```
  [0..3]   pageId: u32
  [4..5]   pageType: u16 (1 = Leaf, 2 = Internal)
  [6..7]   itemCount: u16
  [8..11]  prevPage: u32 (doubly-linked leaf chain for range scans)
  [12..15] nextPage: u32
  [16..19] parentPage: u32
  [20..23] flags: u32
  [24..31] lsn: u64 (Log Sequence Number for crash consistency)
  ```
- **RDF-3X Triples**: Triples $(S, P, O)$ are indexed in clustered B+ tree leaf chains. Full index permutations (`SPO`, `POS`, `OSP`) permit fast range scans for multi-way graph joins without intermediate hash joins.

---

## Upstream & Downstream Integration

| Data Structure           | Upstream Dependencies                      | Downstream Consumers                                     |
| :----------------------- | :----------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------- |
| **RoaringBitmap**        | Symbol IDs from `SymbolIndexer`            | Invalidation sets in `QueryEngine`, type sets            |
| **FrontCodedDictionary** | AST string literals, Qualified names, URIs | Inter-file symbol resolution, memory-mapped LSP indexing |
| **PagedBTree**           | AST semantic relationships, OWL2 axioms    | Leapfrog Triejoin (WCOJ), graph query evaluators, SPARQL |

# CLI Overview

The `@modelscript/cli` package provides two identical binary executables: `modelscript` and its shorthand alias `msx`. The command-line interface serves as the primary headless automation driver for compiling, simulating, verifying, linting, rendering, and orchestrating polyglot engineering systems across local workspaces, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud HPC clusters.

## Installation

You can run the CLI directly from the monorepo workspace using `npx`, or install it globally for system-wide access:

```bash
# Run directly via npx
npx msx --help

# Install globally
npm install -g @modelscript/cli
msx --version
```

## Global Options & Environment Variables

The CLI parser (`apps/cli/src/main.ts`) intercepts global execution flags prior to command dispatch and respects standard environment variables for headless CI/CD and enterprise hub integration:

### Global Flags

| Flag        | Type      | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
| :---------- | :-------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--daemon`  | `boolean` | Route command execution through the persistent background compiler daemon (`~/.modelscript/daemon.sock`) to bypass cold-start WASM initialization and reuse warm Salsa caches. |
| `--help`    | `boolean` | Display usage information and command-specific options.                                                                                                                        |
| `--version` | `boolean` | Print the installed `@modelscript/cli` semantic version.                                                                                                                       |

### Environment Variables

| Variable                                     | Default                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| :------------------------------------------- | :----------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `NO_COLOR`                                   | Unset                    | When set to any non-empty value, disables ANSI color sequences in terminal diagnostics, tables, and diff output.                                                                               |
| `ANSATZ_API_URL` / `MODELSCRIPT_API_URL`     | `http://localhost:3000`  | Base URL for the Ansatz Platform, Package Registry, and Cloud HPC dispatch API (`~/.ansatzrc` / `~/.modelscriptrc` fallback).                                                                  |
| `ANSATZ_API_TOKEN` / `MODELSCRIPT_API_TOKEN` | Unset                    | Bearer token (`JWT` or `ms_bot_*` service token) used for non-interactive authentication against the Registry, Cloud HPC, and Hub APIs (also accepts `ANSATZ_TOKEN` or `MODELSCRIPT_TOKEN`).   |
| `MSX_EDITION`                                | `ee`                     | Runtime edition selector (`ee` for Enterprise Edition, `ce` for pure `AGPL-3.0-or-later` Community Edition). Setting `MSX_EDITION=ce` disables all `@modelscript/ee` commands and subsystems.  |
| `MSX_LICENSE_KEY`                            | Unset                    | Offline Ed25519-signed Enterprise license token (`msx_lic_<payload>.<sig>`) unlocking Enterprise CLI commands (`cloud`, `hil`, `attest`, `digital-twin`, `compliance`, `oslc`, `sysmlv2-api`). |
| `MSX_LICENSE_ENFORCE`                        | `false` (`true` in prod) | When `true`, strictly requires a valid `MSX_LICENSE_KEY` before executing Enterprise CLI commands (otherwise runs in 30-day local evaluation mode).                                            |

## Persistent Compiler Daemon (`--daemon`)

Standard CLI invocations spin up an isolated Node.js process, compile or load `.wasm` parser binaries, and index workspace dependencies from disk. When iterating rapidly or running hundreds of checks in a pre-commit hook, pass `--daemon` to any command:

```bash
# Start or auto-spawn the background daemon and run lint with warm Salsa caches
msx lint model.mo --daemon

# Explicitly manage the daemon lifecycle
msx daemon status
msx daemon restart
msx daemon stop
```

When `--daemon` is passed, `msx` connects to the local Unix domain socket (`~/.modelscript/daemon.sock` on Linux/macOS or named pipe `\\.\pipe\modelscript-daemon` on Windows). If no daemon is running, the CLI automatically spawns one in the background, waits for readiness, and streams the command's `stdout`, `stderr`, and exit code back to the terminal.

## Return Codes & CI/CD Integration

All `msx` commands return POSIX-compliant exit codes suitable for gating GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or Jenkins pipelines:

| Exit Code | Meaning                                                                                                             |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `0`       | Command succeeded with zero errors (or all verification obligations proved `SAFE`).                                 |
| `1`       | Compilation error, static lint error (`severity: "error"`), counterexample falsification found, or runtime failure. |
| `2`       | Invalid CLI arguments, missing required flags, or unreadable input paths.                                           |

DOCUMENT: CLI Commands Reference

# CLI Commands Reference

This reference documents the core and domain-specific commands, subcommands, and flags registered in `@modelscript/cli` (`apps/cli/src/main.ts` and `apps/cli/src/commands/`). All **157 commands** (126 primary commands + 31 aliases) across **81 supported languages** can be invoked via `modelscript` or its shorthand alias `msx`, and any command can be accelerated with the global `--daemon` flag.

---

## Compilation, Simulation & Optimization

### `compile` / `flatten`

Compiles and flattens a hierarchical Modelica class into a canonical Differential-Algebraic Equation (DAE) representation in linear WebAssembly memory (`DAEBuilder`). `flatten` is an exact alias for `compile`.

### CLI Command: `compile <name> [paths..]`
Flatten or lower a Modelica, SysML v2, or domain engineering model to DAE, Modelica, SysML v2, SSP, or FMU

Options:
  - `--output, -o, --out <string>`: output file path for compiled representation
  - `--to, -t <string>`: target output representation (dae, modelica, sysml2, ssp, fmu) (default: "dae")
  - `--model, -m <string>`: explicit class/system name when first positional argument is a file
  - `--language, -l, --lang <string>`: explicit language ID override
  - `--modelica-path, -L <string>`: directories to search for Modelica libraries (colon-separated)
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--memory-profile <boolean>`: profile memory usage across phases and report as JSON to stderr (default: false)

```bash
# Flatten a model using the hybrid WASM kernel with timing breakdowns
msx flatten Modelica.Electrical.Analog.Examples.ChuaCircuit -L ./libraries --timing
```

---

### `instantiate`

Instantiates a Modelica class via the Salsa `QueryEngine` and prints the resolved component hierarchy, inherited modifications, and bindings prior to DAE index reduction.

### CLI Command: `instantiate <name> <paths...>`
Instantiate and query AST structure of a Modelica model

---

### `simulate`

Compiles a model, performs Block Lower Triangular (BLT) Pantelides index reduction and tearing, and executes a numerical time-domain or steady-state simulation locally or on a remote Slurm HPC cluster.

### CLI Command: `simulate <name> [paths..]`
Simulate a Modelica model, SysML v2 system, FMU archive, or domain engineering deck

Options:
  - `--output, -o, --out <string>`: output file path for simulation results
  - `--model, -m <string>`: explicit class/system name when first positional argument is a file
  - `--language, -l, --lang <string>`: explicit language ID override
  - `--start-time <number>`: override experiment start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override experiment stop time
  - `--tolerance <number>`: override experiment tolerance
  - `--interval, --step-size, --output-interval <number>`: override experiment output interval / step size
  - `--format, -f <string>`: output format (default: "csv")
  - `--solver <string>`: ODE/DAE/Symplectic/QSS solver to use (default: "dopri5")
  - `--linear-solver <string>`: Linear system solver for implicit/stiff steps (default: "klu")
  - `--interface-type <string>`: FMI interface type when simulating an FMU: 'cs', 'me', or 'auto'
  - `--start-value <string>`: override FMU variable start value as name=value (repeatable)
  - `--input-file <string>`: CSV file providing time-varying input trajectories (time,u1,u2,...)
  - `--output-variable <string>`: variable name(s) to record in FMU simulation output (repeatable)
  - `--initial-fmu-state-file <string>`: restore serialized FMU state from file before stepping
  - `--final-fmu-state-file <string>`: save serialized FMU state to file after simulation finishes
  - `--log-fmi-calls <boolean>`: log all FMI C API calls and logger callbacks to stderr (default: false)
  - `--realtime <number>`: run simulation in real-time mode with given scale factor (e.g., 1.0 for 1x)
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: js (pure JavaScript), arena (arena-native DoD), wasm (WebAssembly via emcc), c (native compiled), jit (in-memory JIT) (default: "js")
  - `--jit <boolean>`: enable in-memory JIT compilation engine (sub-15ms execution) (default: false)
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--memory-profile <boolean>`: profile memory usage across phases and report as JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--jacobian`: Jacobian calculation method (default: "sparse")
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--steady-state <boolean>`: Solve steady-state initial equilibrium only without time integration (default: false)
  - `--cloud <boolean>`: dispatch simulation to ModelScript Cloud HPC cluster (default: false)
  - `--profile <string>`: cloud compute profile (standard, high-memory, gpu-a100, hpc-mpi-64) (default: "standard")
  - `--async <boolean>`: submit cloud job asynchronously and return immediately with Job ID (default: false)
  - `--poll-interval <number>`: polling interval in milliseconds for cloud simulation status (default: 1500)
  - `--output-dir <string>`: directory to write downloaded simulation result file (default: "./results")
  - `--api-url <string>`: override ModelScript API base URL

```bash
# Run a stiff DAE simulation using the 4th-order Rosenbrock solver and sparse symbolic Jacobians
msx simulate RLC_Circuit circuit.mo --stop-time 10.0 --solver rodas4p --engine arena --jacobian sparse --format csv > trajectory.csv

# Dispatch a heavy multi-domain simulation to the Cloud HPC cluster
msx simulate ThermalGrid plant.mo --cloud --profile high-cpu --stop-time 3600 --output-dir ./runs/thermal
```

### `optimize`

Formulates and solves a nonlinear Dynamic Optimization / Optimal Control Problem (OCP) over a flattened DAE using direct collocation and sequential quadratic programming (SQP).

### CLI Command: `optimize <name> <paths..>`
Solve an optimal control problem for a Modelica model

Options:
  - `--objective <string>`: cost integrand expression (e.g. "u^2")
  - `--controls <string>`: control variable names (comma-separated)
  - `--control-bounds <string>`: control bounds as var:min:max (comma-separated)
  - `--start-time <number>`: override start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override stop time
  - `--num-intervals <number>`: number of collocation intervals (default: 50)
  - `--tolerance <number>`: NLP convergence tolerance (default: 0.000001)
  - `--max-iterations <number>`: maximum SQP iterations (default: 200)
  - `--format`: output format (default: "csv")

```bash
msx optimize EV_BatteryPack vehicle.mo \
  --objective energyLoss \
  --controls currentCommand \
  --control-bounds "currentCommand:-200:200" \
  --stop-time 600 \
  --num-intervals 100 \
  --format json > optimal_profile.json
```

### `bifurcation`

### CLI Command: `bifurcation <name>`

  - `--param, -p <string>`: Continuation parameter name (default: "mu")
  - `--p0 <number>`: Initial continuation parameter value (default: -1)
  - `--p-min <number>`: Minimum continuation parameter bound (default: -2)
  - `--p-max <number>`: Maximum continuation parameter bound (default: 2)
  - `--ds <number>`: Initial pseudo-arclength step size (default: 0.05)
  - `--max-steps <number>`: Maximum continuation steps along the branch (default: 150)
  - `--x0 <number>`: Initial equilibrium state guess vector
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Output serialization format (default: "json")
  - `--output, -o <string>`: Output file path

### `surrogate`

Executes a Design of Experiments (DoE) campaign over a physics model, trains a Reduced-Order Model (ROM) surrogate, attaches convex-hull/bounding-box extrapolation guardrails, and exports standalone C, ONNX, or Modelica `.mo` blocks.

### CLI Command: `surrogate <name> [paths..]`
Train or import an AI surrogate model (ROM) and generate C, ONNX, or Modelica code

Options:
  - `--inputs <string>`: input parameter names (comma-separated)
  - `--input-bounds <string>`: input bounds as var:min:max (comma-separated)
  - `--outputs <string>`: output variable names (comma-separated)
  - `--strategy`: Design of Experiments (DoE) sampling strategy (default: "latin-hypercube")
  - `--num-samples <number>`: number of samples to generate (default: 50)
  - `--architecture`: Reduced Order Model (ROM) architecture (default: "mlp")
  - `--start-time <number>`: override start time
  - `--stop-time <number>`: override stop time
  - `--format`: target export format: C/WASM ('c'), ONNX graph ('onnx'), Modelica block ('mo'), or all ('all') (default: "c")
  - `--from-onnx <string>`: path to external ONNX JSON model file to import instead of training from Modelica source
  - `--extrapolation-guardrails <boolean>`: embed Modelica assertion guardrails for input bounds (default: true)
  - `--extrapolation-level`: severity level of Modelica extrapolation assertions (default: "warning")
  - `--extrapolation-flag <boolean>`: emit Boolean isExtrapolating output variable in Modelica (default: true)
  - `--out-file <string>`: output file name (defaults to <model>_surrogate.<ext>)
  - `--replace-component <string>`: name of component declaration in Modelica model to replace with surrogate
  - `--replace-out <string>`: output path for modified Modelica model with replaced component
  - `--report <string>`: output report JSON file (default: "report.json")

```bash
msx surrogate HeatExchanger thermal.mo \
  --inputs "massFlow,inletTemp" \
  --input-bounds "massFlow:0.1:5.0,inletTemp:280:380" \
  --outputs "outletTemp,pressureDrop" \
  --strategy sobol \
  --num-samples 128 \
  --architecture mlp \
  --format all \
  --out-file build/hx_rom
```

### `mc`

Runs high-throughput Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation across stochastic parameter distributions using worker threads and the linear-memory WASM evaluator.

### CLI Command: `mc <name> <paths..>`
Run Monte Carlo simulation

Options:
  - `--runs <number>`: Number of Monte Carlo runs (default: 1000)
  - `--threads <number>`: Number of parallel threads (default: 1)
  - `--params <string>`: Random variables in format name:dist:arg1:arg2 (comma-separated)
  - `--seed <number>`: PRNG seed
  - `--lhs <boolean>`: Use Latin Hypercube Sampling (default: false)
  - `--format`: Output format (default: "json")
  - `--output <string>`: Output file path (defaults to stdout if not provided)
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: wasm or js (default: "wasm")

```bash
msx mc RLC_Filter filter.mo \
  --params "R:gaussian:100:5,C:uniform:1e-6:1.2e-6" \
  --runs 5000 \
  --lhs \
  --threads 8 \
  --seed 42 \
  --output mc_summary.json
```

### `diff`

Compute an AST-aware semantic diff between two model files (supports any registered DSL)

  - `--format, -f`: Output format (default: "text")

  - `--output, -o <string>`: Write merged output to specified file path

## Formal Verification, Safety & Test Synthesis

### `verify`

Unified formal verification and simulation validation for SysML v2 and Modelica: decision tables, assume-guarantee contracts, state machines, and optional flowpipe reachability. Results can be emitted as terminal output or as JSON, CTRF, JUnit, SARIF, HTML, or DHF reports for CI/CD and compliance workflows.

### CLI Command: `verify [target] [paths..]`
Unified formal verification and simulation validation for SysML v2 and Modelica

Options:
  - `--all <boolean>`: execute all applicable formal verification stages (default: false)
  - `--decisions <boolean>`: verify decision table exhaustiveness and determinism (default: true)
  - `--contracts <boolean>`: verify assume-guarantee contract compatibility and refinement (default: true)
  - `--state-machines <boolean>`: verify state machine and activity workflow soundness/deadlock-freedom (default: true)
  - `--flowpipe <boolean>`: enable validated continuous/hybrid reachability flowpipes (default: false)
  - `--order <number>`: Taylor model flowpipe expansion order (default: 4)
  - `--dt <number>`: time step size in seconds for flowpipe reachability
  - `--horizon <number>`: time horizon (stop time) in seconds for flowpipe reachability
  - `--initial-set <string>`: initial state set bounds (e.g. 'x=[0.9,1.1],y=[-0.1,0.1]')
  - `--barriers <boolean>`: enable sum-of-squares barrier certificate synthesis (default: false)
  - `--falsify <boolean>`: enable adversarial requirement falsification (default: false)
  - `--simulation <boolean>`: verify dynamic simulation trajectory requirements (default: true)
  - `--clearance <boolean>`: enable 3D CAD clearance and physical collision verification (default: false)
  - `--mcdc <boolean>`: synthesize 100% MC/DC independent condition test pairs (default: false)
  - `--b2b <boolean>`: verify Back-to-Back MiL-vs-SiL equivalence against standalone C99 (default: false)
  - `--b2b-tol <number>`: maximum allowable numerical tolerance between MiL and SiL (default: 0.0001)
  - `--b2b-compiler <string>`: host/target C compiler for SiL compilation (default: "gcc")
  - `--b2b-dt <number>`: fixed integration step size in seconds for SiL RK4
  - `--algorithms <boolean>`: execute sound algorithmic abstract interpretation for zero RTEs (default: true)
  - `--format <string>`: output report format: terminal, json, ctrf, junit, sarif, html, or dhf (default: "terminal")
  - `--report <string>`: write test report to specified file path
  - `--export <string>`: comma-separated list of formal spec export formats: smt2, nuxmv, ocra, mos
  - `--export-dir <string>`: target directory for exported formal specifications (default: ".")
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts', 'wasm', 'hybrid', or 'diff' (default: "hybrid")
  - `--engine <string>`: simulation backend: wasm or js (default: "wasm")
  - `--timing <boolean>`: output timing JSON to stderr (default: false)
  - `--update-hypergraph <boolean>`: synchronize verification verdicts directly into digital thread hypergraph (default: false)
  - `--coordinator <boolean>`: execute 4-language SemanticTheoryCoordinator & DigitalThreadHypergraph verification across SysML v2, Modelica, OpenSCAD/URDF, and FEA/CFD/STEP (default: false)

```bash
# Verify a controller and emit a GitHub Code Scanning SARIF report
msx verify BrakingController brake.mo --format sarif --report results.sarif
```

### `falsify`

Performs optimization-guided falsification of Signal Temporal Logic (STL) safety properties ($\square_{[a,b]} \phi$, $\lozenge_{[a,b]} \phi$, $\phi_1 \mathcal{U}_{[a,b]} \phi_2$) by searching disturbance and parameter spaces to minimize quantitative robustness $\rho(\phi, \mathbf{x}, t) < 0$.

### CLI Command: `falsify`
Run adversarial multi-domain requirement falsification across SysML, Modelica, and CAD

Options:
  - `--property <string>`: Name of the target SysML requirement or property
  - `--sysml <string>`: Path to SysML v2 model file (.sysml)
  - `--modelica <string>`: Path to Modelica DAE model file (.mo)
  - `--cad <string>`: Path to CAD procedural file (.scad or .ts)
  - `--params <string>`: JSON array or file path containing parameter bounds
  - `--formula <string>`: STL formula JSON or predicate shorthand (e.g. 'stress <= 200')
  - `--algorithm`: Falsification global optimization algorithm (default: "de")
  - `--generations <number>`: Maximum optimization generations (default: 10)
  - `--population <number>`: Population size per generation (default: 12)
  - `--outTrace <string>`: Path to output CanonicalTraceRecord JSON
  - `--outCad <string>`: Path to output counterexample CAD model file

### `fmu`

### CLI Command: `fmu <name> [paths..]`
Export, validate, inspect, build, or simulate an FMU archive

  - `--description <string>`: model description string

  - `--tolerance <number>`: solver relative tolerance
  - `--xml-only <boolean>`: output only the modelDescription.xml (no archive) (default: false)
  - `--type <string>`: FMU type: 'me' (Model Exchange), 'cs' (Co-Simulation), 'both' (default) (default: "both")
  - `--interface-type <string>`: FMI interface type when simulating an FMU: 'cs', 'me', or 'auto'
  - `--solver <string>`: ODE solver when simulating an FMU in Model Exchange mode ('euler', 'rk4', 'cvode') (default: "rk4")
  - `--start-value <string>`: override FMU variable start value as name=value (repeatable)
  - `--input-file <string>`: CSV file providing time-varying input trajectories (time,u1,u2,...)
  - `--output-variable <string>`: variable name(s) to record in simulation output (repeatable)
  - `--initial-fmu-state-file <string>`: restore serialized FMU state from file before stepping
  - `--final-fmu-state-file <string>`: save serialized FMU state to file after simulation finishes
  - `--log-fmi-calls <boolean>`: log all FMI C API calls and logger callbacks to stderr (default: false)
  - `--format <string>`: simulation output format ('csv', 'json', 'none') (default: "csv")
  - `--target <string>`: export target: 'wasm' (WebAssembly), 'c' (C sources), 'js' (JavaScript), or 'all' (multi-target) (default: "all")
  - `--source <boolean>`: include C source files in the FMU archive (default: true)
  - `--compile <boolean>`: compile C sources into a shared library using the system C compiler (default: false)
  - `--fmi-version <string>`: FMI version to include: '2', '3', or 'both' (default: "both")
  - `--wasm <boolean>`: compile model to WebAssembly and include in the FMU archive (default: false)
  - `--flattener, -F <string>`: Flattener backend: 'ts' (reference TS), 'wasm' (zero-GC kernel), 'hybrid' (WASM with TS fallback), or 'diff' (parity comparison) (default: "hybrid")
  - `--golden <string>`: path to golden CSV trajectory for 'verify' subcommand
  - `--timing <boolean>`: report timing information for each stage as JSON to stderr (default: false)

```bash
# Export an FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU with embedded C sources and WebAssembly binary
msx fmu DC_Motor motor.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs --wasm --output build/DC_Motor.fmu
```

### `cosim`

Co-simulation management (sessions, participants, FMUs, replay)

### `pscad`

Provides full lifecycle tooling for Manitoba Hydro **PSCAD** electromagnetic transient (EMT) workspaces (`.pscx` cases and `.pswx` workspaces), including domain-specific electrical linting, Single-Line Diagram (SLD) generation, EMT simulation, **IEEE Std 2800-2022** grid interconnection verification, and conversion to Modelica/SSP.

### CLI Command: `pscad <action> [files..]`
Inspect, lint, diff, and simulate PSCAD-compatible projects (.pscx, .pslx)

Options:
  - `--out, -o, --output <string>`: Output file path (for diagram SVG, Modelica, SSD, CSV, or COMTRADE export)
  - `--tstop, --stop-time, --duration <number>`: Simulation duration in seconds (default: 1)
  - `--step, --step-size, --dt <string>`: Simulation fixed time step (e.g. '20us' or 20e-6) (default: "20us")
  - `--format, -f <string>`: Result format for 'sim' with --out (base path): pscad (.out/.inf), psout (.psout), comtrade, comtrade-bin, cff (default: "pscad")

| `diff`            | Compute a topological and parameter diff between two `.pscx` revisions.                                                                                                                                          |
| `sim`             | Execute a fixed-step nodal admittance ($\mathbf{G}\mathbf{v}(t) = \mathbf{i}_{\text{hist}}(t - \Delta t)$) EMT simulation.                                                                                       |
| `verify-ieee2800` | Run automated **IEEE Std 2800-2022** Inverter-Based Resource (IBR) compliance checks (Low/High Voltage Ride-Through LVRT/HVRT, frequency ride-through, and reactive current injection step response).            |
| `export-modelica` | Translate a `.pscx` schematic into an equivalent Modelica `.mo` model using `Modelica.Electrical`.                                                                                                               |
| `export-ssp`      | Package a `.pswx` multi-project workspace into an SSP 1.0 `.ssp` architecture container.                                                                                                                         |

