# EPA SWMM Stormwater & Urban Hydrology (`.inp`)

`@modelscript/swmm` (`languages/swmm`) provides zero-regex parsing, 1D Saint-Venant dynamic wave hydraulic routing, DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **US EPA Stormwater Management Model (SWMM 5.x)** urban drainage, sewer collection, and flood mitigation networks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format              | Description                                                                                                      |
| :-------- | :------------------ | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.inp`    | EPA SWMM Input File | Industry-standard stormwater network deck (junctions, conduits, outfalls, subcatchments, pumps, weirs, orifices) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 1D Saint-Venant Dynamic Wave Routing

- Models open-channel and pressurized sewer hydraulics via the one-dimensional **Saint-Venant equations of unsteady flow**:
  - **Conservation of Mass (Continuity)**:
    $$\frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = q_{\text{lateral}}$$
  - **Conservation of Momentum**:
    $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial x} \left( \frac{Q^2}{A} \right) + g A \frac{\partial H}{\partial x} + g A S_f = 0$$
    where $H = z + d$ is hydraulic head, $S_f$ is friction slope, and $S_0$ is conduit bed slope.
- Uses **Manning's open-channel equation** for friction slope:
  $$Q = \frac{k_m}{n} A R_h^{2/3} S_f^{1/2} \quad \implies \quad S_f = \frac{n^2 Q |Q|}{k_m^2 A^2 R_h^{4/3}}$$
  where $n$ is Manning roughness, $A$ is flow cross-sectional area, and $R_h = A / P_{\text{wetted}}$ is hydraulic radius.

### 2. Node & Link Hydraulic Structures

- **Junctions & Storage Units**: Continuous water stage mass conservation:
  $$A_{\text{node}} \frac{dH_i}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{in}} - \sum Q_{\text{out}} + Q_{\text{inflow}} - Q_{\text{flood}}$$
- **Conduits**: Circular, rectangular, trapezoidal, and irregular natural river cross-sections with entrance/exit minor head loss coefficients.
- **Outfalls**: Free, normal, tidal, and fixed water elevation boundary conditions.
- **Regulators**: Orifices, transverse/side-flow weirs, and variable-speed lift pumps.

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Compiles the entire stormwater collection network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` struct-of-arrays linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation of municipal drinking water networks ([`@modelscript/epanet`](./epanet.md)) and drainage networks within the same computational arena.

### 4. Real-Time Control (RTC), Pollutant Washoff, GIS Ingestion & EPA NetDMR

- **Real-Time Control (`rtc`) & Pollutant Washoff (`quality`)**: Simulates dynamic weir/orifice/pump PID and rule-based flood gates alongside exponential land-use pollutant buildup and runoff washoff (TSS, TP, TN).
- **GIS Ingestion (`from-gis`), Network Diff (`diff`) & EPA NetDMR Export**: Ingests GeoJSON conduits, manholes, and subcatchments (`gis-ingestor.ts`), computes topological stormwater diffs, and exports US EPA NPDES NetDMR CSO/SSO overflow monitoring tables (`netdmr-exporter.ts`).

### 5. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects SWMM nodes and channels into `Modelica.Fluid` open-channel tanks, flow conduits, and boundary reservoirs.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The SWMM linter verifies network graph integrity and hydraulic feasibility before simulation:

### Diagnostics for EPA SWMM (13 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8201` | error | `dangling-node-reference` | Link '<linkId>' references undefined <role> node '<nodeId>'. |
| `M8202` | warning | `adverse-conduit-slope` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has adverse slope: inlet elevation (<value>) is lower than outlet elevation (<value>). |
| `M8203` | error | `missing-cross-section` | Conduit '<conduitId>' has no hydraulic cross-section definition in '[XSECTIONS]'. |
| `M8204` | error | `unsupported-outfall-type` | Outfall '<outfallId>' specifies unsupported boundary condition type '<type>'. |
| `M8205` | warning | `surcharge-overflow-risk` | Junction '<junctionId>' rim elevation (<value>) is lower than connected conduit crown (<value>), creating surcharge overflow risk. |
| `M8206` | error | `duplicate-node-id` | Duplicate node identifier '<nodeId>' declared in network. |
| `M8207` | error | `duplicate-link-id` | Duplicate link identifier '<linkId>' declared in network. |
| `M8208` | error | `negative-roughness` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive Manning's roughness coefficient (n = <n>). |
| `M8209` | error | `zero-length-conduit` | Conduit '<conduitId>' specifies non-positive length (<len>). |
| `M8210` | warning | `isolated-network-node` | Junction '<nodeId>' has no connected conduits or hydraulic links (isolated node). |
| `M8211` | error | `subcatchment-outlet-not-found` | Subcatchment '<subId>' references non-existent discharge outlet '<outletId>'. |
| `M8212` | error | `weir-offset-negative` | Weir '<weirId>' specifies negative crest height offset (<offset>). |
| `M8213` | error | `invalid-discharge-coefficient` | Link '<linkId>' specifies non-positive discharge coefficient (Cd = <cd>). |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect junctions, conduits, outfalls, and subcatchments
msx swmm inspect UrbanDrainage.inp
msx swmm summary UrbanDrainage.inp

# Run pre-flight semantic diagnostics
msx swmm lint UrbanDrainage.inp

# Route hydraulic flow, simulate Real-Time Control (RTC), and evaluate pollutant water quality
msx swmm route-flow UrbanDrainage.inp
msx swmm rtc UrbanDrainage.inp
msx swmm quality UrbanDrainage.inp

# Compare two SWMM network revisions or build a SWMM .inp deck from GeoJSON GIS layers

msx swmm from-gis conduits.geojson --manholes=manholes.geojson --out=UrbanDrainage.inp

# Lower network topology into ModelScript linear DAE arena or Modelica 3.x
msx swmm to-dae UrbanDrainage.inp
msx swmm to-modelica UrbanDrainage.inp -o StormwaterNetwork.mo
```

================================================================================
DOCUMENT: USACE HEC-RAS (.g01, .g02, .rasgeo) Language Reference
CANONICAL URL: https://modelscript.org/languages/hec-ras

# USACE HEC-RAS River Hydraulics (`.g01`, `.g02`, `.rasgeo`)

`@modelscript/hec-ras` (`languages/hec-ras`) provides native parsing, 1D steady backwater profile solution, dynamic wave Saint-Venant DAE lowering, and cross-section validation for **US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) HEC-RAS** river geometries and steady/unsteady flow decks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `.g01`, `.g02`, `.g03` | HEC-RAS Geometry File | River reach coordinates, cross-section station-elevations, Manning's $n$, and weir structures |
| `.rasgeo`, `.geo` | Modern HEC-RAS ASCII Geometry | Unified multi-reach geometry exchange format |
| `.f01`, `.f02` | HEC-RAS Steady Flow File | Boundary conditions (known WS, critical depth, normal depth, rating curves) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Standard Step Method 1D Backwater Solver

- Solves the energy conservation equation between adjacent cross-sections:
  $$WSE_2 + \alpha_2 \frac{V_2^2}{2g} = WSE_1 + \alpha_1 \frac{V_1^2}{2g} + h_e$$
  where the head loss $h_e$ incorporates friction loss and expansion/contraction eddy losses:
  $$h_e = L \bar{S}_f + C \left| \alpha_2 \frac{V_2^2}{2g} - \alpha_1 \frac{V_1^2}{2g} \right|$$
- Friction slope evaluated via Manning's formula:
  $$\bar{S}_f = \left( \frac{Q}{\sum K_i} \right)^2, \quad K_i = \frac{1}{n_i} A_i R_i^{2/3}$$
- Supports subcritical, supercritical, and mixed flow regimes with hydraulic jump detection.

### 2. Multi-Zone Cross-Section Hydrodynamics

- Segmented cross-sections with distinct left overbank (LOB), main channel, and right overbank (ROB) roughness coefficients.
- Automated wetted perimeter $P(y)$, flow area $A(y)$, and hydraulic radius $R_h(y)$ quadrature across irregular surveyed station-elevation slices.
- Inline structures: broad-crested and ogee weirs with standard discharge coefficient formulations ($Q = C_d L H^{3/2}$).

### 3. Zero-GC Saint-Venant DAE Lowering

- Lowers 1D shallow water equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena:
  $$\frac{\partial A}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = q_L$$
  $$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial t} + \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left(\frac{\beta Q^2}{A}\right) + g A \frac{\partial h}{\partial x} + g A (S_f - S_0) = 0$$
- Enables direct co-simulation with urban drainage (`@modelscript/swmm`), drinking water networks (`@modelscript/epanet`), and regional aquifers (`@modelscript/modflow`).

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for USACE HEC-RAS (8 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `hecras-parse-error` | Syntax error in HEC-RAS deck: <err>. |
| `M2001` | error | `hecras-reach-not-found` | River '<river>', reach '<reach>' was referenced but not defined in geometry. |
| `M3001` | error | `hecras-station-inversion` | Cross-section at station '<station>' has inverted station offsets: <currSta> <= <prevSta>. Offsets must be strictly monotonically increasing. |
| `M3002` | warning | `hecras-manning-out-of-bounds` | Manning roughness coefficient <n> at station '<station>' is outside typical physical bounds (0.01 - 0.20). |
| `M3003` | error | `hecras-bank-station-out-of-bounds` | Bank station <bank> at station '<station>' is outside cross-section limits [<minSta>, <maxSta>]. |
| `M4001` | error | `hecras-disconnected-reach` | River reach '<river>, <reach>' has fewer than 2 cross-sections and cannot form a valid conveyance profile. |
| `M5001` | warning | `hecras-adverse-slope` | Adverse bed slope detected between upstream station '<usStation>' (invert <usBed> m) and downstream station '<dsStation>' (invert <dsBed> m). |
| `M5002` | error | `hecras-missing-downstream-boundary` | Reach '<river>, <reach>' is missing a downstream boundary condition (Normal Depth, Known WS, or Rating Curve). |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Lint an existing HEC-RAS geometry file for non-monotonic bank stations or invalid roughness
msx hec-ras lint ColumbiaRiver.g01

# Solve 1D backwater surface profile and print water surface elevations (WSE) and Froude numbers
msx hec-ras profile ColumbiaRiver.g01 --discharge=250.0 --slope=0.0015

# Lower river geometry and reach dynamics into ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx hec-ras to-dae ColumbiaRiver.g01 --out=river.dae
```

# USGS MODFLOW 6 Groundwater Aquifers (`.dis`, `.dis6`, `.npf`, `.wel`)

`@modelscript/modflow` (`languages/modflow`) provides native structured block parsing, 3D Darcy cell conductance evaluation, aquifer mass balance solution, and DAE lowering for **US Geological Survey (USGS) MODFLOW 6** regional groundwater flow models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `.dis`, `.dis6` | MODFLOW Discretization Package | 3D layered regular grid dimensions ($\Delta r, \Delta c$, top, bottom elevations) |
| `.npf` | Node Property Flow Package | Horizontal/vertical hydraulic conductivities ($K_{xx}, K_{33}$) and storage properties |
| `.wel` | Well Package | Extraction and injection well pumping rates per grid cell |
| `.riv` | River Package | Surface water-groundwater hydraulic exchange conductance and river stage |
| `.chd` | Constant-Head Package | Fixed piezometric head boundary conditions |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. 3D Darcy Inter-Cell Hydraulic Conductance

- Calculates harmonic-mean directional conductances between adjacent cells $(i, j)$:
  $$C_{ij} = \frac{2 K_i K_j}{K_i \Delta x_j + K_j \Delta x_i} \cdot A_{ij}$$
- Steady-state mass conservation at each cell:
  $$\sum_{j \in \text{neighbors}(i)} C_{ij} (h_j - h_i) + Q_{\text{wel}, i} + Q_{\text{riv}, i} + Q_{\text{chd}, i} = 0$$

### 2. Riverbed Seepage & Groundwater Interaction

- Simulates bidirectional surface-groundwater flux coupled to river stage:
  $$Q_{\text{riv}} = \begin{cases} C_{\text{riv}} (h_{\text{stage}} - h_{\text{cell}}), & h_{\text{cell}} > z_{\text{rbot}} \\ C_{\text{riv}} (h_{\text{stage}} - z_{\text{rbot}}), & h_{\text{cell}} \le z_{\text{rbot}} \end{cases}$$
- Coupled directly to river hydraulics (`@modelscript/hec-ras`) and urban stormwater runoff (`@modelscript/swmm`).

### 3. DAE Formulation for Aquifer Storage Dynamics

- Lowers unconfined/confined transient head equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder`:
  $$S_s \Delta V \frac{dh}{dt} = \sum Q_{\text{flux}}$$
- Allows municipal water planners to evaluate sustained well yield against drinking water demand profiles (`@modelscript/epanet`).

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for USGS MODFLOW (6 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `modflow-parse-error` | Syntax or structure error in MODFLOW deck: <err>. |
| `M2001` | error | `modflow-cell-out-of-bounds` | Grid cell (<layer>, <row>, <col>) is out of bounds for grid dimensions (<maxL>, <maxR>, <maxC>). |
| `M3001` | error | `modflow-invalid-conductivity` | Hydraulic conductivity K = <k> is invalid. K must be strictly positive (K > 0). |
| `M3002` | error | `modflow-invalid-storage` | Aquifer storage parameter <param> = <val> is invalid. Value must be non-negative. |
| `M4001` | error | `modflow-river-stage-below-bottom` | River stage <stage> m is lower than river bed bottom elevation <rbot> m. |
| `M4002` | error | `modflow-layer-elevation-inversion` | Layer <layer> has bottom elevation (<botm>) higher than or equal to its top elevation (<top>). |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect and summarize MODFLOW 6 grid discretization, conductivity, and boundary packages
msx modflow inspect CentralValley.dis6
msx modflow summary CentralValley.dis6

# Lint MODFLOW package files for negative thicknesses or invalid conductivity
msx modflow lint CentralValley.dis6

# Compute 3D cell mass balance, hydraulic heads, and water table drawdown
msx modflow balance CentralValley.dis6
msx modflow heads CentralValley.dis6
msx modflow solve CentralValley.dis6

# Lower aquifer cell conductance matrix to ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx modflow to-dae CentralValley.dis6 --out=aquifer.dae
```

# EPA LandGEM Biogas & Landfill Gas (`.landgem`, `.lfg`, `.biogas`)

`@modelscript/landgem` (`languages/landgem`) provides native parsing, first-order methane decay kinetics, continuous stirred-tank anaerobic digestion (ADM1), and Combined Heat & Power (CHP) DAE lowering for **US EPA LandGEM** and industrial organic waste-to-energy models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `.landgem`, `.lfg` | EPA LandGEM Model | Annual solid waste acceptance cohorts, methane capacity $L_0$, and decay rates $k$ |
| `.biogas` | Biogas / ADM1 Digester Deck | CSTR reactor parameters, hydraulic retention times (HRT), and influent COD loads |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. First-Order Decay Methane Generation Kinetics

- Evaluates the canonical US EPA LandGEM equation summing over all historical waste cohorts $i$:
  $$Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} 2 k L_0 M_i e^{-k t_{i}}$$
  where $k$ is the methane generation rate constant ($\text{yr}^{-1}$), $L_0$ is the potential methane generation capacity ($\text{m}^3/\text{Mg}$), and $M_i$ is the mass of waste accepted in year $i$.
- Evaluates landfill gas (LFG) collection efficiency and non-methane organic compound (NMOC) emissions.

### 2. ADM1 Continuous Anaerobic Digestion Engine

- Models mesophilic ($37^\circ\text{C}$) and thermophilic ($55^\circ\text{C}$) anaerobic CSTR digesters with chemical oxygen demand (COD) destruction:
  $$r_{\text{COD}} = \eta_{\text{removal}} \cdot \frac{S_{\text{COD,in}}}{HRT}$$
  $$Q_{\text{CH}_4,\text{dig}} = r_{\text{COD}} \cdot V_{\text{reactor}} \cdot Y_{\text{CH}_4/\text{COD}}$$
  where theoretical methane yield $Y_{\text{CH}_4/\text{COD}} \approx 0.35 \, \text{m}^3 \, \text{CH}_4 / \text{kg COD}_{\text{removed}}$ at STP.
- Monitors Volatile Fatty Acid (VFA) accumulation and digester souring risk based on pH.

### 3. Combined Heat & Power (CHP) DAE Lowering

- Couples gas production directly into electrical and thermal energy output equations in `DAEBuilder`:
  $$P_{\text{elec}}(t) = Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) \cdot \text{LHV}_{\text{CH}_4} \cdot \eta_{\text{elec}}$$
  $$P_{\text{thermal}}(t) = Q_{\text{CH}_4}(t) \cdot \text{LHV}_{\text{CH}_4} \cdot \eta_{\text{thermal}}$$
- Direct integration into electrical power networks (`@modelscript/opendss`) and district heating networks.

---

## Static Analysis & Pre-Flight Linter Rules

### Diagnostics for EPA LandGEM (6 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M1001` | error | `landgem-parse-error` | Syntax or structure error in LandGEM / Biogas deck: <err>. |
| `M2001` | error | `landgem-missing-waste-data` | Landfill site '<site>' has no historical or projected waste acceptance cohorts. |
| `M3001` | error | `landgem-invalid-kinetic-parameter` | Kinetic parameter <param> = <val> is invalid. Value must be strictly positive (<param> > 0). |
| `M3002` | error | `landgem-digester-ph-inhibition` | Digester '<digester>' operating pH (<ph>) causes severe methanogenic inhibition. Optimum pH is 6.8 - 7.6. |
| `M4001` | error | `landgem-invalid-year-range` | Landfill site '<site>' closing year (<close>) must be greater than or equal to opening year (<open>). |
| `M4002` | error | `landgem-negative-waste-mass` | Waste acceptance in year <year> has negative mass (<mass> Mg). Waste mass must be non-negative. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Lint landfill cohorts and digester parameters
msx landgem lint MetroLandfill.landgem

# Compute 50-year methane generation trajectory and CHP electrical output
msx landgem biogas MetroLandfill.landgem

# Lower methane decay dynamics into ModelScript DAE arena
msx landgem to-dae MetroLandfill.landgem --out=biogas.dae
```

# Aspen-Compatible Chemical Process Modeling (`.in`, `.inp`, `.bkp`)

`@modelscript/aspen` (`languages/aspen`) provides zero-regex parsing, vapor-liquid equilibrium (VLE) flash computation, distillation column MESH equations, DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **Aspen Plus- and Aspen HYSYS-compatible** chemical flowsheet input decks.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension      | Format                | Description                                                                          |
| :------------- | :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.in` / `.inp` | Aspen Plus Input File | Keyword-sectioned chemical process flowsheet, unit operations, stream thermodynamics |
| `.bkp`         | Aspen Backup Deck     | Serialized ASCII Aspen model topology and stream definitions                         |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Rachford-Rice Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium (VLE) Flash Solver

- Solves isothermal ($T$-$P$) and adiabatic ($P$-$H$) flash equilibrium via the **Rachford-Rice equation**:
  $$f(\psi) = \sum_{i=1}^{C} \frac{z_i (K_i - 1)}{1 + \psi (K_i - 1)} = 0$$
  where $\psi = V/F$ is the vapor fraction, $z_i$ is the feed mole fraction, and $K_i(T, P)$ is the equilibrium ratio:
  $$K_i = \frac{y_i}{x_i} = \frac{\gamma_i P_i^{\text{sat}}(T)}{\phi_i P}$$
- Uses modified **Antoine vapor pressure** equations:
  $$\ln P_i^{\text{sat}} = A_i - \frac{B_i}{T + C_i}$$
- Implements subcooled liquid ($\sum z_i K_i < 1$) and superheated vapor ($\sum z_i / K_i < 1$) state identification with monotonic Newton-Raphson bracket solving.

### 2. Unit Operations & Distillation Columns

- **Mixers & Splitters**: Rigorous material balance ($\sum F_{\text{in}} = \sum F_{\text{out}}$) and energy conservation ($\sum \dot{H}_{\text{in}} = \sum \dot{H}_{\text{out}}$).
- **Heaters & Coolers**: Specified duty ($Q$) or target outlet temperature/vapor fraction.
- **Flash Separators**: Multi-component 2-phase and 3-phase phase separation vessels.
- **RadFrac Equilibrium Distillation Columns**: Rigorous stage-by-stage **MESH equations** (Material balance, Equilibrium, Summation, Heat/enthalpy balance).

### 3. Direct Linear-Memory DAE Lowering

- Compiles flowsheet topology, stream molar balances, and component enthalpies directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` struct-of-arrays linear memory arena without intermediary AST allocations.
- Emits continuous DAE systems with algebraic stream constraints for joint dynamic simulation with pipeline networks ([`@modelscript/lps`](./lps.md)) and multiphase transient pipelines ([`@modelscript/olga`](./olga.md)).

### 4. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Translates unit operations into standardized `Modelica.Fluid` or OpenIPSL thermal-fluid models with acausal fluid ports (`m_flow`, `p`, `h`, `Xi`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The Aspen analyzer inspects flowsheet connectivity, phase equilibria, and thermodynamic consistency:

### Diagnostics for Aspen Plus / HYSYS (18 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8101` | error | `unconnected-stream-port` | Stream '<streamName>' connected to block '<blockName>' inlet has no producing source block outlet. |
| `M8102` | error | `tear-stream-unconverged` | Circular flowsheet loop detected involving block '<blockName>' without designated tear stream. |
| `M8103` | error | `invalid-eos-parameter` | Component '<compName>' lacks critical properties for property method '<propertyMethod>'. |
| `M8104` | error | `negative-component-fraction` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies negative component molar fraction for '<compName>' (<val>). |
| `M8105` | warning | `column-reboiler-heat-deficit` | Column '<blockName>' duty results in non-positive reboiler boil-up. |
| `M8106` | error | `duplicate-block-id` | Duplicate block ID '<blockId>' declared in flowsheet. |
| `M8107` | error | `duplicate-component-id` | Duplicate component ID '<compId>' declared in COMPONENTS. |
| `M8108` | warning | `fractions-sum-invalid` | Component mole fractions in stream '<streamName>' sum to <value>, expected 1.0. |
| `M8109` | error | `feed-stage-out-of-range` | Column '<blockName>' feed stage <stage> is out of bounds (1..<nStages>). |
| `M8110` | error | `product-stage-out-of-range` | Column '<blockName>' product stage <stage> is out of bounds (1..<nStages>). |
| `M8111` | warning | `missing-flowsheet-entry` | Block '<blockName>' has parameter declarations but is not connected in FLOWSHEET. |
| `M8112` | error | `stream-temperature-negative` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies non-physical absolute temperature <temp> K. |
| `M8113` | error | `stream-pressure-negative` | Stream '<streamName>' specifies non-positive pressure <pres> bar. |
| `M8114` | error | `radfrac-stages-too-few` | RadFrac column '<blockName>' has fewer than 2 stages (<nStages>). |
| `M8115` | error | `reflux-ratio-negative` | Column '<blockName>' reflux ratio (<rr>) must be non-negative. |
| `M8116` | error | `mixer-mass-balance-deficit` | Mixer '<blockName>' total inlet mass flow does not equal outlet mass flow. |
| `M8117` | warning | `heat-exchanger-temperature-cross` | Heat exchanger '<blockName>' has temperature cross: cold stream outlet exceeds hot stream inlet. |
| `M8118` | error | `compressor-pressure-ratio-subunity` | Compressor '<blockName>' specifies outlet pressure below inlet pressure. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash

msx aspen inspect MethanolWaterPlant.inp

# Run pre-flight semantic diagnostics
msx aspen lint MethanolWaterPlant.inp

# Solve isothermal flash VLE for a feed stream

# Lower flowsheet to ModelScript linear DAE arena

```

# gPROMS / PML-Compatible Dynamic Process Modeling (`.gproms`, `.pml`)

`@modelscript/gproms` (`languages/gproms`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, Method-of-Lines (MOL) spatial finite-difference discretization for distributed-parameter partial differential-algebraic equations (PDAEs), 4th-order Runge-Kutta dynamic simulation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **gPROMS / PML-compatible** chemical, pharmaceutical, and crystallization process models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                    | Description                                                                                                                 |
| :-------- | :------------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gproms` | gPROMS Model File         | Equation-oriented process model defining `PARAMETER`, `DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN`, `VARIABLE`, `EQUATION`, and `PROCESS` entities |
| `.pml`    | Process Modeling Language | Modular PML entity and flowsheet specification                                                                              |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Equation-Oriented & Distributed-Parameter Modeling (`PDAE`)

`@modelscript/gproms` parses hierarchical `VARIABLE_TYPE`, `MODEL`, and `PROCESS` entities:

- **`DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN`**: Axial, radial, or crystal-size spatial domains (e.g., `Axial AS [0 : L]`) for tubular plug-flow reactors (PFR), pressure-swing adsorption (PSA) beds, and population-balance crystallizers.
- **`PARTIAL(u, z)` & `INTEGRAL`**: First- and second-order spatial derivatives $\frac{\partial u}{\partial z}$ and $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial z^2}$ alongside time derivatives `$u` ($\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$):
  $$\frac{\partial C_i}{\partial t} = -v_z \frac{\partial C_i}{\partial z} + D_{\text{ax}} \frac{\partial^2 C_i}{\partial z^2} + \sum_r \nu_{i,r} R_r(\mathbf{C}, T)$$
- **`BOUNDARY` & `EQUATION`**: Danckwerts inlet/outlet boundary conditions ($v_z C_{i,\text{in}} = v_z C_i(0^+) - D_{\text{ax}} \frac{\partial C_i}{\partial z}\big|_{0^+}$) and coupled algebraic thermodynamic equilibrium relations.
- **`ASSIGN`, `INITIAL`, & `SCHEDULE`**: Structural degrees-of-freedom specifications, differential initial conditions, and sequential operating procedures (`CONTINUE FOR`, `SWITCH`, `RESET`, `PARALLEL`).

### 2. Method-of-Lines (MOL) Discretization & Dynamic Solver

For every distributed variable $u(z, t)$ defined over a `DISTRIBUTION_DOMAIN` $[z_0, z_N]$ with $N$ uniform grid intervals $\Delta z = (z_N - z_0)/N$, `@modelscript/gproms` discretizes spatial operators into node-indexed ODE/DAE equations:

$$\left.\frac{\partial u}{\partial z}\right|_{z_k} \approx \frac{u_k - u_{k-1}}{\Delta z} \quad (\text{1st-order upwind}), \qquad \left.\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial z^2}\right|_{z_k} \approx \frac{u_{k+1} - 2u_k + u_{k-1}}{\Delta z^2} \quad (\text{2nd-order central})$$

This transforms the PDAE system into a semi-discrete index-1 DAE system over node variables $u_0(t), \dots, u_N(t)$, which is integrated in time and lowered directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena.

### 3. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects gPROMS `MODEL` and `PROCESS` definitions into equation-based **Modelica 3.x** models (`gpromsToModelica`) with explicit `der(...)` equations, discretized array variables, and `initial equation` blocks.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for gPROMS / PML (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9451` | error | `undeclared-variable-type` | Variable '<varName>' in model '<modelName>' references undeclared DECLARE TYPE '<typeName>'. |
| `M9452` | error | `invalid-variable-bounds` | Variable type '<typeName>' specifies invalid bounds or default value (default=<defaultVal>, lower=<lower>, upper=<upper>); requires lower < upper and lower <= default <= upper. |
| `M9453` | error | `invalid-distribution-domain` | Distribution domain '<domainName>' in model '<modelName>' specifies invalid domain [<lower> : <upper>] or grid points (<gridPoints>); requires lower < upper and gridPoints >= 2. |
| `M9454` | error | `undeclared-equation-identifier` | Equation in model '<modelName>' references undeclared identifier '<identifier>'. |
| `M9455` | warning | `structural-dof-mismatch` | Model '<modelName>' has a structural degrees-of-freedom mismatch: <eqCount> equations + <assignCount> ASSIGNed variables != <varCount> unknown variables. |
| `M9456` | warning | `uninitialized-differential-state` | Differential state variable '$<varName>' lacks an INITIAL condition in PROCESS '<processName>'. |
| `M9457` | error | `partial-on-non-distributed-variable` | Spatial derivative 'PARTIAL(<varName>, <domainName>)' in model '<modelName>' is applied to variable '<varName>' which is not distributed over domain '<domainName>'. |
| `M9458` | error | `overassigned-parameter-or-variable` | Entity '<entityName>' in PROCESS '<processName>' is overassigned or misused: <detail>. |
| `M9459` | error | `empty-gproms-model` | gPROMS model '<modelName>' is empty and defines no variables or equations. |
| `M9460` | error | `duplicate-entity-declaration` | Duplicate <kind> declaration '<name>' in '<scope>'. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Run pre-flight linting on a gPROMS / PML model (structural DOF, boundaries, domains)
msx lint TubularReactor.gproms

# Parse and inspect the CST / symbol table
msx parse TubularReactor.gproms

# Dispatch domain inspection or Method-of-Lines simulation via the polyglot router
msx domain gproms inspect TubularReactor.gproms
```

## Programmatic TypeScript SDK

```typescript
import { parseGpromsModel, simulateGpromsProcess, lowerGpromsToDae, gpromsToModelica } from "@modelscript/gproms";
import { DAEBuilder } from "@modelscript/runtime";

const model = parseGpromsModel(gpromsSource);
const sim = simulateGpromsProcess(model, { steps: 200 });

const builder = new DAEBuilder();
lowerGpromsToDae(model, builder);
const modelicaCode = gpromsToModelica(model);
```

# Cantera Chemical Kinetics & Thermochemistry (`.yaml`, `.cti`)

`@modelscript/cantera` (`languages/cantera`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, NASA-7 polynomial thermodynamic evaluation ($C_p^\circ(T)$, $H^\circ(T)$, $S^\circ(T)$, $G^\circ(T)$), modified Arrhenius and Troe falloff reaction rate calculation, non-isothermal batch reactor ODE integration, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and SBML / Modelica projections for **Cantera** gas-phase combustion, catalysis, and chemical kinetics mechanisms.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format             | Description                                                                                         |
| :-------- | :----------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.yaml`   | Cantera YAML       | Modern Cantera 2.5+ / 3.x YAML mechanism format (`phases`, `species`, `reactions`, `thermo: NASA7`) |
| `.cti`    | Legacy Cantera CTI | Classic Cantera `ideal_gas`, `species`, and `reaction` mechanism definitions                        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. NASA-7 Thermochemical Polynomials

- Evaluates two-range (low-$T$ $[T_{\min}, T_{\text{mid}}]$ and high-$T$ $[T_{\text{mid}}, T_{\max}]$) 7-coefficient NASA polynomials $(a_0, \dots, a_6)$ for every species $k$:
  $$\frac{C_{p,k}^\circ(T)}{R} = a_0 + a_1 T + a_2 T^2 + a_3 T^3 + a_4 T^4$$
  $$\frac{H_k^\circ(T)}{RT} = a_0 + \frac{a_1}{2}T + \frac{a_2}{3}T^2 + \frac{a_3}{4}T^3 + \frac{a_4}{5}T^4 + \frac{a_5}{T}$$
  $$\frac{S_k^\circ(T)}{R} = a_0 \ln T + a_1 T + \frac{a_2}{2}T^2 + \frac{a_3}{3}T^3 + \frac{a_4}{4}T^4 + a_6$$
- Verifies continuity of $C_{p,k}^\circ$, $H_k^\circ$, and $S_k^\circ$ across the midpoint splitting temperature $T_{\text{mid}}$ and checks atomic elemental conservation across all elementary reactions.

### 2. Elementary, Three-Body & Troe Falloff Kinetics

- Computes forward rate constants via the 3-parameter modified Arrhenius expression and reverse rate constants via microscopic reversibility from the concentration equilibrium constant $K_{c,j}(T)$:
  $$k_{f,j}(T) = A_j \, T^{\beta_j} \exp\!\left(-\frac{E_{a,j}}{RT}\right), \qquad k_{r,j}(T) = \frac{k_{f,j}(T)}{K_{p,j}(T)} \left(\frac{P^\circ}{RT}\right)^{\sum_k \nu_{k,j}}$$
- Supports third-body collision efficiencies $[M]_j = \sum_k \alpha_{j,k} [X_k]$ (`+ M`) and pressure-dependent **Lindemann / Troe falloff** blending between low-pressure ($k_0$) and high-pressure ($k_\infty$) limits via the reduced pressure $P_r = k_0 [M] / k_\infty$ and broadening factor $\log_{10} F_{\text{cent}}(T)$.

### 3. Non-Isothermal Reactor ODE Solver & DAE Lowering

- Integrates coupled species molar concentrations $\dot{\omega}_k = \sum_j (\nu_{k,j}'' - \nu_{k,j}') q_j$ and adiabatic energy balance equations:
  $$\rho \bar{c}_p \frac{dT}{dt} = -\sum_{k=1}^{N_s} H_k^\circ(T) \, \dot{\omega}_k$$
- Lowers the full chemical kinetics and thermochemical network into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena and projects mechanisms into **Modelica 3.x** (`canteraToModelica`) and **SBML** (`canteraToSbml`).

---

# USGS PHREEQC Aqueous Geochemistry & Speciation (`.pqi`, `.dat`)

`@modelscript/phreeqc` (`languages/phreeqc`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, ionic strength and Davies / Extended Debye-Hückel activity coefficient calculation, aqueous carbonate/redox speciation, mineral Saturation Index ($\text{SI}$) evaluation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **USGS PHREEQC** hydrogeochemical, brine scaling, carbon mineralization, and water treatment models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                 | Description                                                                                                              |
| :-------- | :--------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.pqi`    | PHREEQC Input Deck     | Keyword data blocks (`TITLE`, `SOLUTION`, `EQUILIBRIUM_PHASES`, `REACTION`, `KINETICS`, `MIX`, `SELECTED_OUTPUT`, `END`) |
| `.dat`    | Thermodynamic Database | Aqueous species (`SOLUTION_SPECIES`) and mineral solubility (`PHASES`) database definitions                              |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Ionic Strength, Electrical Charge Balance & Activity Coefficients

For an aqueous solution containing $N_s$ dissolved ionic species with molalities $m_i\text{ [mol/kgw]}$ and formal charges $z_i$, the molal ionic strength $I$ and electrical Charge Balance Error ($\text{CBE}$) are:

$$
I = \frac{1}{2} \sum_{i=1}^{N_s} m_i z_i^2, \qquad
\text{CBE (\%)} = 100 \times \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N_s} m_i z_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{N_s} m_i |z_i|}
$$

Single-ion activity coefficients $\gamma_i$ ($a_i = \gamma_i m_i$) are evaluated using the **WATEQ Extended Debye-Hückel** equation (when ion-size parameters $\mathring{a}_i, b_i$ are specified in `.dat`) or the **Davies** equation ($I \lesssim 0.5\text{ mol/kgw}$):

$$
\log_{10} \gamma_i = \begin{cases}
  -\dfrac{A(T)\, z_i^2 \sqrt{I}}{1 + B(T)\,\mathring{a}_i \sqrt{I}} + b_i I & \text{(Extended Debye-Hückel)}, \\[10pt]
  -A(T)\, z_i^2 \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{I}}{1 + \sqrt{I}} - 0.3\, I\right) & \text{(Davies)}.
\end{cases}
$$

### 2. Mineral Saturation Indices ($\text{SI}$) & Transition-State Theory (TST) Kinetics

For a mineral dissolution reaction $M \rightleftharpoons \sum_i \nu_{im} S_i$ with temperature-corrected solubility product $K_{\text{sp},m}(T)$ (Van 't Hoff $\Delta H_r^\circ$ or 6-term analytical $\log_{10} K(T)$ polynomial), the **Ion Activity Product ($\text{IAP}_m$)** and **Saturation Index ($\text{SI}_m$)** are:

$$
\text{IAP}_m = \prod_{i=1}^{N_s} a_i^{\nu_{im}}, \qquad
\text{SI}_m = \log_{10}\!\left(\frac{\text{IAP}_m}{K_{\text{sp},m}(T)}\right), \qquad
\Omega_m = 10^{\text{SI}_m}
$$

In `KINETICS` blocks, Palandri-Kharaka / Lasaga Transition-State Theory (TST) mineral dissolution/precipitation rates $R_m\text{ [mol/(kgw}\cdot\text{s)]}$ combine acid, neutral, and carbonate/base mechanisms over reactive surface area $A_m$:

$$
R_m = A_m \left(k_{\text{acid}} a_{\text{H}^+}^{n_{\text{H}}} + k_{\text{neutral}} + k_{\text{base}} a_{\text{OH}^-}^{n_{\text{OH}}}\right) \left(1 - \Omega_m^{p_m}\right)^{q_m}
$$

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Direct `DAEBuilder` Lowering (`lowerPhreeqcToDae`)**: Lowers aqueous mass-action equilibria, electroneutrality algebraic constraints ($\sum m_i z_i = 0$), and kinetic mineral dissolution ODEs ($dm_m/dt = -R_m$) into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.
- **Modelica 3.x Projection (`phreeqcToModelica`)**: Generates acausal hydrochemical speciation and scaling blocks compatible with [EPANET](./epanet.md) water distribution and [OLGA](./olga.md) / [ECLIPSE](./eclipse.md) oilfield brine flowassurance workflows.

---

# SMILES & MDL Molfile Molecular Graphs (`.smi`, `.smarts`, `.mol`, `.sdf`)

`@modelscript/smiles` (`languages/smiles`) provides zero-regex native WebAssembly GLR parsing, organic valence and Hückel $4n+2$ aromaticity verification, **Joback & Reid (1987)** group-contribution thermodynamic and critical property estimation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Aspen Plus / Modelica projections for **OpenSMILES**, **SMARTS**, and **MDL Molfile V2000 / Structure-Data File (`.sdf`)** molecular specifications.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension         | Format          | Description                                                                                                      |
| :---------------- | :-------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.smi`, `.smiles` | OpenSMILES      | Line notation encoding molecular graphs, ring closures, branches, stereochemistry (`@`/`@@`), and aromatic atoms |
| `.smarts`         | SMARTS          | Substructure query patterns for functional-group matching                                                        |
| `.mol`, `.sdf`    | MDL V2000 / SDF | 2D/3D atomic coordinate tables, bond orders, and associated structure-data property tags (`> <Property>`)        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Molecular Graph Topology, Valence & Hückel Aromaticity

- Constructs typed molecular graphs $G = (V, E)$ with implicit/explicit hydrogen counting, ring-closure matching (single-digit `1`–`9` and two-digit `%nn` closures), disconnected ionic salts/mixtures (`.`), formal charges, isotopes, tetrahedral chirality (`@`/`@@`), and cis/trans alkene stereochemistry (`/` and `\`).
- Evaluates cycle bases over conjugated $\pi$-systems to verify **Hückel's rule** ($N_\pi = 4n + 2$ delocalized $\pi$-electrons) and checks every atom against allowed organic/inorganic valence shells ($\text{B}: 3$, $\text{C}: 4$, $\text{N}: \{3,5\}$, $\text{O}: 2$, $\text{P}: \{3,5\}$, $\text{S}: \{2,4,6\}$, halogens: $1$).

### 2. Joback & Reid (1987) Group-Contribution Property Estimator

`@modelscript/smiles` decomposes molecular graphs into functional group frequencies $N_k$ (`-CH3`, `-CH2-`, `>CH-`, `>C<`, `=CH2`, `>C=O`, `-OH`, `-COOH`, `-COO-`, `-NH2`, aromatic ring carbons, and halogens) and evaluates the **Joback & Reid** group-contribution correlations for pure-component thermophysical properties:

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_b &= 198.2 + \sum_k N_k \, \Delta T_{b,k} \quad [\text{K}] \\[4pt]
T_m &= 122.5 + \sum_k N_k \, \Delta T_{m,k} \quad [\text{K}] \\[4pt]
T_c &= T_b \left[0.584 + 0.965 \sum_k N_k \, \Delta T_{c,k} - \left(\sum_k N_k \, \Delta T_{c,k}\right)^2\right]^{-1} \quad [\text{K}] \\[4pt]
P_c &= \left(0.113 + 0.0032 \, N_{\text{atoms}} - \sum_k N_k \, \Delta P_{c,k}\right)^{-2} \quad [\text{bar}] \\[4pt]
V_c &= 17.5 + \sum_k N_k \, \Delta V_{c,k} \quad [\text{cm}^3/\text{mol}]
\end{aligned}
$$

Along with standard enthalpy of formation $\Delta H_{f,298}^\circ$, standard Gibbs energy of formation $\Delta G_{f,298}^\circ$ ($\text{kJ/mol}$), ideal-gas heat capacity polynomial $C_p^\circ(T) = A + BT + CT^2 + DT^3$, and the Lee-Kesler acentric factor $\omega$.

### 3. Aspen Plus, Modelica & DAE Lowering

- **Aspen Plus & Modelica Media Projection**: Projects estimated critical constants ($T_c, P_c, V_c, \omega$), molecular weights, and NASA/ideal-gas $C_p^\circ(T)$ polynomials directly into **Aspen Plus** pure-component property cards (`smilesToAspen`) and **Modelica** media records (`smilesToModelica`).
- **`DAEBuilder` Lowering**: Emits pure-component thermophysical parameters and temperature-dependent $C_p^\circ(T)$, $H^\circ(T)$, and vapor-pressure saturation equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

| `M9302` | error | `unbalanced-branch-parenthesis` | Branch parenthesis in '<moleculeName>' is unbalanced. |
| `M9303` | error | `valence-exceeded` | Atom '<element>' (index '<atomIndex>') in '<moleculeName>' has bond order sum '<actualValence>' exceeding maximum allowed valence '<maxValence>'. |

# SBML Systems Biology & Biochemical Kinetics (`.sbml`, `.xml`)

`@modelscript/sbml` (`languages/sbml`) provides zero-regex streaming XML parsing, biochemical reaction network kinetics solving, 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE simulation, linear DAE lowering, and Modelica 3.x projection for **Systems Biology Markup Language (SBML Level 2 & 3 Core)** cellular, metabolic, and signaling network models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format            | Description                                                                               |
| :-------- | :---------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sbml`   | SBML Model File   | Standard biochemical XML schema encoding compartments, species, parameters, and reactions |
| `.xml`    | SBML XML Document | General XML format containing standard SBML Level 2/3 definitions                         |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Biochemical Reaction Networks & Stoichiometry

- Parses hierarchical multi-compartment biochemical reaction networks:
  - **Compartments**: Cellular volumes (cytosol, mitochondria, extracellular space) with spatial dimensions (0D, 2D membrane, 3D volume).
  - **Species**: Chemical and protein concentrations or particle amounts ($[S_i] \ge 0$).
  - **Parameters**: Kinetic rate constants ($k_{\text{fwd}}, k_{\text{rev}}$), Michaelis constants ($K_m$), and Hill coefficients ($n$).
  - **Reactions**: Reversible and irreversible reaction fluxes ($v_j$) with stoichiometric coefficient matrices $N = [\nu_{ij}]$:
    $$\sum_{i} s_{ij} S_i \xrightarrow{v_j} \sum_{k} p_{kj} P_k$$

### 2. Kinetic Law Formulations & ODE Solver

- Evaluates dynamic reaction velocities across standard enzyme kinetics:
  - **Mass-Action Kinetics**:
    $$v = k_{\text{fwd}} \prod [R_i]^{s_i} - k_{\text{rev}} \prod [P_j]^{p_j}$$
  - **Michaelis-Menten Enzymatic Saturation**:
    $$v = \frac{V_{\text{max}} [S]}{K_m + [S]}$$
  - **Hill Cooperativity**:
    $$v = \frac{V_{\text{max}} [S]^n}{K_{0.5}^n + [S]^n}$$
- Solves the resulting non-linear **ordinary differential equations (ODEs)**:
  $$\frac{d[S_i]}{dt} = \frac{1}{V_{\text{comp}}} \sum_{j=1}^{R} \nu_{ij} \cdot v_j([S], p)$$
  using embedded 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) integration or stiff SUNDIALS CVODE solvers.

### 3. Direct DAE Lowering

- Lowers reaction stoichiometric matrices and flux equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` linear memory arena.
- Enables co-simulation between cellular metabolic networks and pharmacokinetics / drug delivery fluid pipelines ([`@modelscript/aspen`](./aspen.md)).

### 4. Bidirectional Modelica 3.x Projection

- Projects SBML reaction systems into Modelica biochemical components and acausal substance substance-flow models.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

The SBML analyzer validates stoichiometric consistency, undefined references, and physical rate bounds:

### Diagnostics for SBML (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M8801` | error | `missing-model-id` | SBML <model> element is missing required 'id' attribute. |
| `M8802` | error | `undefined-compartment-reference` | Species '<speciesId>' references undefined compartment '<compartmentId>'. |
| `M8803` | error | `undefined-species-reference` | Reaction '<reactionId>' references undefined <role> species '<speciesId>'. |
| `M8804` | error | `negative-compartment-size` | Compartment '<compartmentId>' defines non-positive size (<size>). |
| `M8805` | error | `negative-initial-amount-concentration` | Species '<speciesId>' specifies negative initial amount/concentration (<val>). |
| `M8806` | error | `empty-reaction` | Reaction '<reactionId>' must define at least one reactant or product. |
| `M8807` | warning | `missing-kinetic-law` | Reaction '<reactionId>' does not define a kineticLaw rate law equation. |
| `M8808` | error | `negative-stoichiometry` | Species reference for '<speciesId>' in reaction '<reactionId>' specifies non-positive stoichiometry (<stoich>). |
| `M8809` | warning | `undefined-kinetic-parameter` | Kinetic law formula in reaction '<reactionId>' references identifier '<id>' not found in parameters or species. |
| `M8810` | info | `circular-species-assignment` | Reaction '<reactionId>' lists '<speciesId>' as both reactant and product with identical stoichiometry; consider defining as modifier. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect compartments, species, parameters, and reactions
msx sbml inspect GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Run pre-flight linting and stoichiometric validation
msx sbml lint GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Simulate biochemical reaction kinetics ODEs with RK4
msx sbml simulate GlycolyticPathway.sbml --duration=20.0

# Lower biochemical reaction network to ModelScript linear DAE arena
msx sbml to-dae GlycolyticPathway.sbml

# Project into Modelica 3.x biochemical network model
msx sbml to-modelica GlycolyticPathway.sbml -o GlycolysisModel.mo
```

# Antimony Modular Systems Biology (`.ant`)

`@modelscript/antimony` (`languages/antimony`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, hierarchical submodel composition and port aliasing (`is`), rate and assignment rule evaluation, state-triggered event handling, 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE integration, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and bidirectional SBML Level 3 / Modelica 3.x projection for **Antimony** human-readable systems biology models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format         | Description                                                                                                            |
| :-------- | :------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.ant`    | Antimony Model | Modular text language (`model ... end`) for biochemical reactions, compartments, species, events, and submodel imports |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Multi-Compartment Stoichiometric Balance & Boundary Species

Given $M$ dynamic floating species $\mathbf{S} = (S_1, \dots, S_M)^\top$ residing in compartments of volume $V_{\text{comp}(i)}$, $B$ fixed boundary species (`$S_b`, where $dS_b/dt = 0$), and $R$ biochemical reactions $J_r$ with net stoichiometry matrix $\mathbf{N} \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times R}$ ($\nu_{ir} = \nu_{ir}^+ - \nu_{ir}^-$) and kinetic rate laws $\mathbf{v}(\mathbf{S}, \mathbf{p}, t) \in \mathbb{R}^R$:

$$
\frac{d[S_i]}{dt} = \frac{1}{V_{\text{comp}(i)}} \sum_{r=1}^R \nu_{ir}\, v_r\bigl([\mathbf{S}], \mathbf{p}, t\bigr)
$$

Explicit rate rules (`x' = f(x, S, p)`), algebraic assignment rules (`y := g(x, S, p)`), and Hill / Michaelis-Menten regulatory kinetics combine with reaction fluxes into a coupled semi-explicit DAE system:

$$
\dot{\mathbf{x}} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}, \mathbf{p}, t), \qquad \mathbf{y} = \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{p}, t)
$$

### 2. Hybrid State-Event Zero-Crossing Semantics (`at (...)`)

An Antimony event `E_k: at (phi(x, t) > 0): x_i = h_i(x^-), p_j = c_j;` defines a zero-crossing guard predicate $\phi_k(\mathbf{x}, t)$ monitored during numerical integration. At the root time $t^*$ where $\phi_k(\mathbf{x}(t^{*-}), t^{*-}) = 0$ and $\dot{\phi}_k > 0$, discrete state and parameter reinitializations $\mathbf{x}(t^{*+}) = \mathbf{h}_k(\mathbf{x}(t^{*-}))$ are applied atomically.

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Hierarchical Submodel Flattening & `is` Aliasing**: Submodel instances (`A: SubModel();`) and shared port/species alias declarations (`A.S1 is Cytosol_S1;`) are resolved into equivalence classes prior to emitting variables into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerAntimonyToDae`).
- **Bidirectional SBML Level 3 Core Interop (`antimonyToSbml`)**: Translates compartments, species, reactions, rate/assignment rules, and events directly into [SBML](./sbml.md) Level 3 XML.
- **Modelica 3.x Projection (`antimonyToModelica`)**: Emits Modelica `model` blocks with `der(...)` equations and `when ... then reinit(...)` clauses.

# BioNetGen Rule-Based Biochemical Networks (`.bngl`)

`@modelscript/bngl` (`languages/bngl`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, rule-based site-specific biochemical network expansion, observable pattern aggregation, 4th-order Runge-Kutta ODE integration, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and SBML / Modelica projections for **BioNetGen Language (BNGL)** multiprotein signaling, receptor oligomerization, and post-translational modification models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format          | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| :-------- | :-------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.bngl`   | BioNetGen Model | Block-structured rule-based biochemical specification (`parameters`, `molecule types`, `seed species`, `observables`, `reaction rules`, `actions`) |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Site-Graph Rewriting & Combinatorial Network Generation

A receptor or scaffold protein with $M$ independent phosphorylation/binding sites generates $2^M$ or more distinct chemical micro-states. Instead of enumerating all micro-species manually, a BNGL reaction rule $R_r: \mathcal{P}_{\text{react}} \xrightarrow{k_r} \mathcal{P}_{\text{prod}}$ is a **typed site-graph rewrite rule** matching subgraph embeddings $\phi: \mathcal{P}_{\text{react}} \hookrightarrow G_s$ into reachable chemical species graphs $G_s \in \mathcal{S}$:

- **Internal State Transition**: `EGFR(Y1068~U) -> EGFR(Y1068~P) k_phos`
- **Reversible Site Binding (`!n`)**: `L(r) + EGFR(l) <-> L(r!1).EGFR(l!1) kp1, km1`
- **Wildcard Bonds**: `!+` (bound to any partner), `!?` (bound or unbound), and empty site (explicitly unbound).

### 2. Mass-Action ODE System & Observable Pattern Aggregation

Once iterative rule application reaches fixed-point closure (or `max_iter`) over $\mathcal{S} = \{S_1, \dots, S_N\}$ and elementary reactions $\mathcal{R} = \{1, \dots, R\}$, the concentration vector $\mathbf{x}(t) \in \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}^N$ evolves according to stoichiometric mass-action kinetics with statistical symmetry multiplicities $\sigma_r$:

$$
\frac{dx_i}{dt} = \sum_{r=1}^R \nu_{ir}\, \sigma_r k_r \prod_{j=1}^N x_j^{\nu_{jr}^-}, \qquad \nu_{ir} = \nu_{ir}^+ - \nu_{ir}^-
$$

Each declared `Molecules` or `Species` observable $O_q(t)$ computes a weighted linear combination over all generated species $S_i$ matching pattern $\Pi_q$ with subgraph match multiplicity $w_{qi} = |\text{Emb}(\Pi_q, S_i)|$:

$$
O_q(t) = \sum_{i=1}^N w_{qi}\, x_i(t)
$$

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Direct `DAEBuilder` Lowering (`lowerBnglToDae`)**: Kinetic rate parameters, expanded species state variables (`Variability.Continuous`), elementary reaction flux expressions, mass-balance ODEs (`der(x_i)`), and pattern observable equations (`O_q`) are emitted directly into `DAEBuilder`.
- **SBML Level 3 Export (`bnglToSbml`)**: Serializes the expanded species and reaction network into standards-compliant [SBML](./sbml.md) XML for downstream pathway tools.
- **Modelica 3.x Projection (`bnglToModelica`)**: Generates acausal Modelica biochemical models ready for multi-scale coupling with physiological [CellML](./cellml.md) or pharmacokinetic [NONMEM](./nmtran.md) models.

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for BioNetGen (BNGL) (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| `M9052` | error | `component-site-undeclared` | Component site '<siteName>' is not declared on molecule type '<moleculeName>'. |
| `M9053` | error | `invalid-internal-state` | Internal state '~<stateName>' is not allowed for component '<siteName>' of molecule type '<moleculeName>'. |

| `M9055` | warning | `undefined-rate-parameter` | Reaction rule '<ruleId>' references undeclared rate parameter '<parameterName>'. |

# SBOL3 Synthetic Biology Genetic Circuits (`.sbol`, `.ttl`, `.rdf`)

`@modelscript/sbol` (`languages/sbol`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, Sequence Ontology (`SO`) and Systems Biology Ontology (`SBO`) genetic circuit verification, Hill-function transcriptional activation/repression ODE simulation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and SBML / Modelica projections for **Synthetic Biology Open Language (SBOL 3.x)** genetic designs.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension               | Format       | Description                                                                                                      |
| :---------------------- | :----------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sbol`, `.rdf`, `.xml` | SBOL RDF/XML | Standard RDF/XML serialization of `sbol:Component`, `sbol:Sequence`, `sbol:SubComponent`, and `sbol:Interaction` |
| `.ttl`                  | SBOL3 Turtle | Compact RDF Turtle representation of SBOL3 genetic circuits and sequence constraints                             |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Genetic Parts, Sequence Constraints & Interactions

`@modelscript/sbol` parses hierarchical `sbol:Component` definitions, `sbol:SubComponent` instances, `sbol:SequenceConstraint` ordering rules (`precedes`, `sameOrientationAs`, `oppositeOrientationAs`), and regulatory `sbol:Interaction` graphs:

| Ontology Term         | Identifier    | Biological Role                                                    | Mathematical Lowering                                            |
| :-------------------- | :------------ | :----------------------------------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Promoter              | `SO:0000167`  | Transcriptional initiation site regulated by transcription factors | Basal rate $\alpha_{0,i}$ + inducible Hill fractional activation |
| Ribosome Binding Site | `SO:0000139`  | Translational initiation sequence (Shine-Dalgarno / Kozak)         | Translational gain multiplier on mRNA expression                 |
| Coding Sequence (CDS) | `SO:0000316`  | Open reading frame encoding a protein or reporter species $P_i$    | Continuous state variable $[P_i](t)$ in `DAEBuilder`             |
| Terminator            | `SO:0000141`  | Hairpin transcriptional termination boundary                       | Transcriptional unit boundary verification                       |
| Stimulation           | `SBO:0000170` | Transcriptional activation by activator $A$ (`SBO:0000459`)        | Cooperative activation term $[A]^n / (K_A^n + [A]^n)$            |
| Inhibition            | `SBO:0000169` | Transcriptional repression by repressor $R$ (`SBO:0000020`)        | Cooperative repression term $K_R^m / (K_R^m + [R]^m)$            |

### 2. Hill-Function Genetic Circuit ODE Solver

For every transcriptional unit ending in a coding sequence $P_i$ regulated by a set of transcriptional activators $\mathcal{A}_i$ and repressors $\mathcal{R}_i$, `@modelscript/sbol` synthesizes coupled mRNA and protein concentration ODEs using cooperative Hill kinetics:

$$\frac{d[P_i]}{dt} = \alpha_{0,i} + \alpha_i \left(\prod_{A \in \mathcal{A}_i} \frac{[A]^{n_A}}{K_A^{n_A} + [A]^{n_A}}\right) \left(\prod_{R \in \mathcal{R}_i} \frac{K_R^{m_R}}{K_R^{m_R} + [R]^{m_R}}\right) - \gamma_i [P_i]$$

where:

- $\alpha_{0,i}$ is the basal (leaky) promoter expression rate ($\text{nM}\cdot\text{min}^{-1}$),
- $\alpha_i$ is the maximum regulated synthesis rate ($\text{nM}\cdot\text{min}^{-1}$),
- $K_A, K_R$ are the half-maximal dissociation constants ($\text{nM}$),
- $n_A, m_R$ are the Hill cooperativity coefficients, and
- $\gamma_i = \gamma_{\text{deg},i} + \mu$ is the combined proteolytic degradation and cell-growth dilution rate ($\text{min}^{-1}$).

This formulation directly supports multistable genetic toggle switches (Gardner et al.), three-node repressilator ring oscillators (Elowitz & Leibler), and AND/NAND logic gates.

### 3. DAE Lowering & SBML / Modelica Projection

- **`DAEBuilder` Linear Memory Lowering**: Registers each expressed protein/RNA species as a continuous state variable (`VarType.Real`, `Variability.Continuous`) and lowers its basal, Hill-activation, Hill-repression, and dilution parameters (`Variability.Parameter`) and rate equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.
- **SBML Level 3 & Modelica 3.x Export**: Projects genetic circuits into SBML Level 3 Core (`sbolToSbml`) with `SBO` annotations and into equation-based Modelica 3.x models (`sbolToModelica`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9501` | error | `invalid-nucleotide-sequence` | Sequence '<seqId>' contains characters outside the IUPAC nucleic acid alphabet ('<invalidChar>'). |
| `M9502` | error | `sequence-range-out-of-bounds` | Feature '<featureId>' location '[<start>..<end>]' exceeds sequence '<seqId>' length '<seqLength>'. |
| `M9503` | warning | `cds-length-not-multiple-of-three` | Coding sequence (CDS) '<cdsId>' nucleotide length ('<length>') is not divisible by 3 or lacks a valid start/stop codon. |
| `M9504` | error | `unresolved-subcomponent-reference` | SubComponent '<subId>' in '<compId>' references undefined Component '<instanceOf>'. |

# COMBINE SED-ML Simulation Experiments (`.sedml`)

`@modelscript/sedml` (`languages/sedml`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, KiSAO solver algorithm validation, multi-task simulation protocol execution (`UniformTimeCourse`, `OneStep`, `SteadyState`, `RepeatedTask`), `DataGenerator` post-processing, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Modelica experiment projection for **Simulation Experiment Description Markup Language (SED-ML Level 1 Version 3/4)** reproducible simulation studies.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension        | Format         | Description                                                                                                          |
| :--------------- | :------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.sedml`, `.xml` | COMBINE SED-ML | XML specification of `listOfModels`, `listOfSimulations`, `listOfTasks`, `listOfDataGenerators`, and `listOfOutputs` |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Uniform Time-Course Discretization & KiSAO Solver Mapping

A SED-ML `uniformTimeCourse` specifies an initial integration start time $t_0 = t_{\text{initial}}$, an output recording window $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$ with $t_0 \le t_{\text{start}} < t_{\text{end}}$, and $N_{\text{pts}} = \text{numberOfPoints}$ uniform sampling intervals of step size:

$$
\Delta t = \frac{t_{\text{end}} - t_{\text{start}}}{N_{\text{pts}}}, \qquad t_k = t_{\text{start}} + k\,\Delta t \quad (k = 0, 1, \dots, N_{\text{pts}})
$$

Each `algorithm` element references an ontology term from the **Kinetic Simulation Algorithm Ontology (KiSAO)**alongside `algorithmParameter` tolerances (`KISAO:0000209` relative tolerance $\varepsilon_{\text{rel}}$, `KISAO:0000211` absolute tolerance $\varepsilon_{\text{abs}}$):

| KiSAO Term      | Algorithm Name                               | `@modelscript/simulate` Target |
| :-------------- | :------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------- |
| `KISAO:0000019` | CVODE (Variable-order BDF / Adams-Moulton)   | `cvode` / `bdf`                |
| `KISAO:0000283` | IDA (Implicit Differential-Algebraic solver) | `ida`                          |
| `KISAO:0000032` | Explicit 4th-order Runge-Kutta (RK4)         | `rk4`                          |
| `KISAO:0000086` | Fehlberg / Dormand-Prince adaptive RK45      | `dopri5`                       |
| `KISAO:0000304` | Radau IIA 5th-order implicit Runge-Kutta     | `radau5`                       |
| `KISAO:0000029` | Gillespie Direct Stochastic Simulation (SSA) | Stochastic ensemble kernel     |

### 2. Model Pre-Processing (`changeAttribute` & `computeChange`) and `DataGenerator` Normalization

Before task execution, `computeChange` evaluates a functional parameter override $p_{\text{new}} = g(\mathbf{p}_0)$ over XPath/SBML target identifiers. After trajectory integration $\mathbf{x}(t_k)$, each `dataGenerator` $d_j$ evaluates a post-processing functional over raw model variables $v_i(t_k)$:

$$
y_j(t_k) = f_j\!\left(v_1(t_k), \dots, v_m(t_k), \mathbf{c}_j\right), \qquad \tilde{y}_j(t_k) = \frac{y_j(t_k) - \min_k y_j(t_k)}{\max_k y_j(t_k) - \min_k y_j(t_k)}
$$

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Direct `DAEBuilder` Lowering (`lowerSedmlToDae`)**: Simulation horizon parameters (`tInitial`, `outputStartTime`, `outputEndTime`, `numberOfPoints`), model attribute overrides (`changeAttribute`), and algebraic `dataGenerator` observable equations are lowered directly into contiguous `DAEBuilder` parameter and equation slots.
- **Modelica Experiment Projection (`sedmlToModelica`)**: Translates SED-ML tasks and parameter sweeps into executable Modelica 3.x models carrying standard `annotation(experiment(StartTime = ..., StopTime = ..., Interval = ..., Tolerance = ...))` metadata.
- **SBML / CellML / COMBINE Archive Coupling**: Resolves `model[@source]` URIs against companion [SBML](./sbml.md) and [CellML](./cellml.md) models in the unified `WorkspaceIndex`.

---

# NMTRAN / NONMEM-Compatible Pharmacometrics & PK/PD (`.ctl`, `.mod`)

`@modelscript/nmtran` (`languages/nmtran`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, `ADVAN1`–`ADVAN13` compartmental pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) solving, multi-dose (`AMT`, `RATE`, `II`, `ADDL`) exposure calculation ($\text{AUC}$, $C_{\max}$, $T_{\max}$, $t_{1/2}$), `DAEBuilder` lowering, and SBML / Modelica projections for **NMTRAN / NONMEM-compatible** clinical trial and population pharmacometrics control streams.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format                | Description                                                                                                                                          |
| :-------- | :-------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.ctl`    | NMTRAN Control Stream | NONMEM-compatible control file (`$PROBLEM`, `$INPUT`, `$DATA`, `$SUBROUTINES`, `$PK`, `$DES`, `$ERROR`, `$THETA`, `$OMEGA`, `$SIGMA`, `$ESTIMATION`) |
| `.mod`    | PsN / NONMEM Model    | PsN- and Pirana-compatible pharmacometric model file                                                                                                 |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Standard PREDPP Compartmental Library (`ADVAN`) & General ODEs (`$DES`)

`@modelscript/nmtran` parses `$SUBROUTINES` declarations (`ADVAN` + `TRANS` parameterizations) and general differential equations (`$DES`):

| Subroutine            | Compartments                  | Route & Kinetics                                            | Governing System                                                                                                   |
| :-------------------- | :---------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ADVAN1`              | 1 (Central)                   | IV Bolus / Infusion (`TRANS1`: $K$, `TRANS2`: $CL, V$)      | $\frac{dA_1}{dt} = R_{\text{inf}}(t) - \frac{CL}{V} A_1$                                                           |
| `ADVAN2`              | 2 (Depot + Central)           | Extravascular 1st-Order Absorption ($K_a, CL, V$)           | $\frac{dA_1}{dt} = -K_a A_1, \quad \frac{dA_2}{dt} = K_a A_1 - \frac{CL}{V} A_2$                                   |
| `ADVAN3` / `ADVAN4`   | 2–3 (Central + Peripheral)    | Two-compartment IV / Oral ($CL, V_1, Q, V_2, K_a$)          | Coupled central-peripheral distribution exchange $Q(A_1/V_1 - A_2/V_2)$                                            |
| `ADVAN11` / `ADVAN12` | 3–4 (Central + 2 Peripherals) | Three-compartment IV / Oral ($CL, V_1, Q_2, V_2, Q_3, V_3$) | Deep-tissue distribution kinetics                                                                                  |
| `ADVAN6` / `ADVAN13`  | $N$ User-Defined              | General Non-Linear ODEs (`$DES` with `DADT(i)`)             | Target-Mediated Drug Disposition (TMDD), Michaelis-Menten clearance $V_{\max} C / (K_m + C)$, indirect response PD |

### 2. Population Mixed-Effects (`$THETA`, `$OMEGA`, `$SIGMA`) & Exposure Metrics

- Evaluates non-linear mixed-effects (NLME) individual parameter relationships in `$PK` and residual error structures in `$ERROR`:
  $$\theta_{i,k} = \theta_{\text{pop},k} \cdot \exp(\eta_{i,k}), \qquad \boldsymbol{\eta}_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Omega}), \qquad Y_{ij} = F_{ij}(1 + \varepsilon_{1,ij}) + \varepsilon_{2,ij}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_{ij} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$$
- Simulates single-dose and steady-state multi-dose regimens (`AMT`, zero-order infusion `RATE`, inter-dose interval `II`, additional doses `ADDL`) and computes non-compartmental clinical exposure metrics via trapezoidal integration:
  $$\text{AUC}_{0\to t} = \int_0^t C_p(\tau)\,d\tau, \qquad t_{1/2,\beta} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda_z}, \qquad C_{\max} = \max_{t} C_p(t), \qquad T_{\max} = \arg\max_{t} C_p(t)$$

### 3. DAE Lowering & Modelica / SBML Projection

- Lowers PK/PD compartmental differential equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena and projects them into **Modelica 3.x** (`nmtranToModelica`) and **SBML** (`nmtranToSbml`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for NMTRAN (NONMEM) (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9401` | error | `missing-problem-record` | NMTRAN control stream is missing the required '$PROBLEM' record. |
| `M9402` | error | `theta-bounds-violation` | $THETA parameter 'THETA(<thetaIndex>)' violates bounds (lower=<lower>, init=<init>, upper=<upper>). |
| `M9403` | error | `missing-des-block-for-general-advan` | Subroutine '<advan>' requires a '$DES' differential equation block. |
| `M9404` | error | `undefined-theta-reference` | Block references 'THETA(<thetaIndex>)' beyond the number of declared '$THETA' parameters ('<maxTheta>'). |
| `M9405` | error | `undefined-eta-reference` | Block references 'ETA(<etaIndex>)' beyond the dimension of declared '$OMEGA' variance entries ('<maxOmega>'). |
| `M9406` | error | `non-positive-omega-variance` | $OMEGA diagonal variance entry 'OMEGA(<omegaIndex>)' must be positive (> 0) unless FIXED to 0 (got '<variance>'). |
| `M9407` | error | `compartment-index-out-of-bounds` | Compartment reference '<cmtIndex>' exceeds declared compartment count ('<maxCmt>'). |
| `M9408` | error | `missing-error-prediction-y` | $ERROR block does not define the required dependent prediction variable 'Y'. |
| `M9409` | error | `missing-required-trans-parameter` | Subroutine '<advan>' with '<trans>' requires pharmacokinetic parameter '<paramName>' in '$PK'. |
| `M9410` | error | `negative-dosing-amount` | Dosing record specifies a negative '<field>' value ('<value>'). |

# PDB & mmCIF 3D Macromolecular Structure (`.pdb`, `.cif`, `.mmcif`)

`@modelscript/pdb` (`languages/pdb`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, backbone Ramachandran $(\phi, \psi)$ dihedral angle and steric clash verification, radius of gyration ($R_g$) calculation, **Gaussian Network Model (GNM)** elastic normal-mode fluctuation analysis, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and OpenSCAD / Modelica projections for **Protein Data Bank (`.pdb`)** and **PDBx/mmCIF (`.cif`)** 3D macromolecular structures.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension        | Format            | Description                                                                                                       |
| :--------------- | :---------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.pdb`, `.ent`   | Legacy PDB Format | Fixed-column records (`HEADER`, `TITLE`, `SEQRES`, `HELIX`, `SHEET`, `SSBOND`, `ATOM`, `HETATM`, `CONECT`, `END`) |
| `.cif`, `.mmcif` | PDBx / mmCIF      | Macromolecular Crystallographic Information File (`data_`, `loop_`, `_atom_site.*`)                               |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. Backbone Dihedral Angles $(\phi, \psi, \omega)$ & Radius of Gyration ($R_g$)

Given consecutive backbone atomic coordinates $\mathbf{r}_{\text{C}_{i-1}}, \mathbf{r}_{\text{N}_i}, \mathbf{r}_{\text{C}\alpha_i}, \mathbf{r}_{\text{C}_i}, \mathbf{r}_{\text{N}_{i+1}} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, bond vectors $\mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3$ define the peptide torsion angle via the four-quadrant normal projection:

$$
\theta(\mathbf{b}_1, \mathbf{b}_2, \mathbf{b}_3) = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(
  \bigl((\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2) \times (\mathbf{b}_2 \times \mathbf{b}_3)\bigr) \cdot \frac{\mathbf{b}_2}{\|\mathbf{b}_2\|},\;
  (\mathbf{b}_1 \times \mathbf{b}_2) \cdot (\mathbf{b}_2 \times \mathbf{b}_3)
\right)
$$

yielding $\phi_i = \theta(\text{C}_{i-1}, \text{N}_i, \text{C}_{\alpha,i}, \text{C}_i)$ and $\psi_i = \theta(\text{N}_i, \text{C}_{\alpha,i}, \text{C}_i, \text{N}_{i+1})$. The mass-weighted center of mass $\mathbf{R}_{\text{cm}}$ and radius of gyration $R_g$ over $N$ atoms with atomic masses $m_k$ are:

$$
\mathbf{R}_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum_{k=1}^N m_k \mathbf{r}_k}{\sum_{k=1}^N m_k}, \qquad R_g = \sqrt{\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N m_k \|\mathbf{r}_k - \mathbf{R}_{\text{cm}}\|^2}{\sum_{k=1}^N m_k}}
$$

### 2. Gaussian Network Model (GNM) & Crystallographic $B$-Factors

In the coarse-grained Tirion / Bahar **Gaussian Network Model (GNM)**, each residue is represented by its $\text{C}_\alpha$ node ($i = 1, \dots, n$) connected by uniform harmonic springs $\gamma$ within a cutoff radius $r_c = 7.0\text{ \AA}$. The $n \times n$ Kirchhoff contact matrix $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}$ is defined by:

$$
\Gamma_{ij} = \begin{cases}
  -1 & \text{if } i \ne j \text{ and } \|\mathbf{r}_{\text{C}\alpha,i} - \mathbf{r}_{\text{C}\alpha,j}\| \le r_c, \\
  0  & \text{if } i \ne j \text{ and } \|\mathbf{r}_{\text{C}\alpha,i} - \mathbf{r}_{\text{C}\alpha,j}\| > r_c, \\
  -\sum_{k \ne i} \Gamma_{ik} & \text{if } i = j.
\end{cases}
$$

Using the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^+$ (excluding the trivial zero translational eigenmode $\lambda_1 = 0$), theoretical equilibrium mean-square residue fluctuations and isotropic X-ray Debye-Waller $B$-factors are:

$$
\langle (\Delta \mathbf{R}_i)^2 \rangle = \frac{3 k_B T}{\gamma} \left[\boldsymbol{\Gamma}^+\right]_{ii}, \qquad B_i^{\text{calc}} = \frac{8 \pi^2}{3} \langle (\Delta \mathbf{R}_i)^2 \rangle
$$

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Direct `DAEBuilder` Lowering (`lowerPdbToDae`)**: Lowers the coarse-grained $\text{C}_\alpha$ elastic network $M_i \ddot{\mathbf{u}}_i + \eta \dot{\mathbf{u}}_i + \gamma \sum_j \Gamma_{ij} \mathbf{u}_j = \mathbf{0}$ into continuous state and derivative equations in `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.
- **OpenSCAD 3D CSG Projection (`pdbToScad`)**: Exports secondary-structure ribbons, $\text{C}_\alpha$ elastic contact networks, and ball-and-stick atomic spheres/cylinders to [OpenSCAD](./scad.md) (`.scad`).
- **Modelica Multibody Projection (`pdbToModelica`)**: Generates acausal harmonic spring-damper macromolecular models in [Modelica](./modelica.md).

---

# GenBank & FASTA Nucleotide Sequences (`.gb`, `.gbk`, `.fasta`, `.fa`)

`@modelscript/genbank` (`languages/genbank`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, NCBI genetic code translation verification, 6-frame Open Reading Frame (ORF) discovery, restriction endonuclease digestion mapping, Codon Adaptation Index ($\text{CAI}$) calculation, `DAEBuilder` transcriptional/translational lowering, and SBOL3 / Modelica projections for **NCBI GenBank** and **FASTA** plasmid, viral, and genomic sequence files.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension                 | Format                 | Description                                                                                           |
| :------------------------ | :--------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.gb`, `.gbk`, `.genbank` | NCBI GenBank Flat File | Annotated nucleotide sequence record (`LOCUS`, `DEFINITION`, `ACCESSION`, `FEATURES`, `ORIGIN`, `//`) |
| `.fasta`, `.fa`, `.fna`   | FASTA Sequence         | Multi-sequence nucleotide or peptide FASTA records (`>header`)                                        |

---

## Governing Mathematical Formulation

### 1. GC Content, Primer Melting Temperature ($T_m$) & Codon Adaptation Index ($\text{CAI}$)

Given a nucleotide sequence $S = s_1 s_2 \dots s_L \in \{\text{A}, \text{C}, \text{G}, \text{T/U}\}^L$, the GC fraction $f_{\text{GC}}$ and salt-adjusted Marmur-Doty / SantaLucia melting temperature $T_m$ ($[\text{Na}^+] = 50\text{ mM}$) are:

$$
f_{\text{GC}} = \frac{N_{\text{G}} + N_{\text{C}}}{L}, \qquad
T_m = \begin{cases}
  2(N_{\text{A}} + N_{\text{T}}) + 4(N_{\text{G}} + N_{\text{C}}) & \text{if } L < 14, \\
  64.9 + 41.0 \left(\dfrac{N_{\text{G}} + N_{\text{C}} - 16.4}{L}\right) & \text{if } L \ge 14.
\end{cases}
$$

For a coding sequence (`CDS`) of $K$ sense codons $c_1, \dots, c_K$, let $f(c_k)$ be the reference frequency of codon $c_k$ in highly expressed host genes and $\max_{c \in \text{Syn}(a_k)} f(c)$ be the maximum frequency among synonymous codons encoding amino acid $a_k$. Sharp & Li's **Codon Adaptation Index ($\text{CAI}$)** is the geometric mean of relative adaptiveness weights $w_k$:

$$
w_k = \frac{f(c_k)}{\max_{c \in \text{Syn}(a_k)} f(c)}, \qquad \text{CAI} = \left(\prod_{k=1}^K w_k\right)^{1/K} = \exp\!\left(\frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^K \ln w_k\right) \in (0, 1]
$$

### 2. Transcriptional & Translational Gene Expression ODEs

Each annotated `CDS` $i$ driven by an upstream `promoter` and ribosome binding site (`RBS`) is lowered into coupled mRNA ($m_i$) and protein ($p_i$) dynamical equations with Hill regulatory activation/repression and ribosome elongation rate scaled by $\text{CAI}_i$:

$$
\frac{dm_i}{dt} = \alpha_{0,i} + \alpha_i \frac{u_i^{n_i}}{K_i^{n_i} + u_i^{n_i}} - \gamma_{m,i}\, m_i, \qquad
\frac{dp_i}{dt} = k_{\text{tl},i}(\text{CAI}_i)\, m_i - (\gamma_{p,i} + \mu)\, p_i
$$

---

## `DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering & Cross-Language Projections

- **Direct `DAEBuilder` Lowering (`lowerGenbankToDae`)**: Emits mRNA and protein concentrations, promoter Hill kinetics, and $\text{CAI}$-weighted translation rates directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena.
- **SBOL3 Genetic Circuit Projection (`genbankToSbol`)**: Maps GenBank `FEATURES` (`promoter`, `RBS`, `CDS`, `terminator`, `rep_origin`) to Sequence Ontology (`SO:0000167`, `SO:0000139`, `SO:0000316`, `SO:0000141`) `SubComponent` hierarchies in [SBOL3](./sbol.md).
- **Modelica 3.x Projection (`genbankToModelica`)**: Generates synthetic biology ODE blocks in [Modelica](./modelica.md).

---

# CellML Cellular Electrophysiology & Physiome Modeling (`.cellml`)

`@modelscript/cellml` (`languages/cellml`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, 7-base SI dimensional unit consistency and component port directionality verification, Hodgkin-Huxley / cardiac action-potential and 0D microvascular Windkessel ODE integration, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Modelica 3.x / SBML projections for **IUPS Physiome Project CellML (1.0 / 1.1 / 2.0)** physiological models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension         | Format                 | Description                                                                                                          |
| :---------------- | :--------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.cellml`, `.xml` | CellML 1.0 / 1.1 / 2.0 | Modular XML specification of `units`, `component`, `variable`, MathML `math` ODEs, `connection`, and `encapsulation` |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Modular Components, Encapsulation & 7-Base SI Dimensional Vector Algebra

- Parses `<units>` definitions (`prefix`, `multiplier`, `exponent`, `offset`) and reduces every custom physiological unit (e.g., $\text{mV}$, $\mu\text{A}/\text{cm}^2$, $\text{mS}/\text{cm}^2$, $\text{mmHg}$, $\text{mM}$) to its canonical 7-base SI dimensional exponent vector $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{Q}^7$ and scalar scale factor $s$:
  $$\mathbf{d}(u) = \begin{bmatrix} d_{\text{m}} & d_{\text{kg}} & d_{\text{s}} & d_{\text{A}} & d_{\text{K}} & d_{\text{mol}} & d_{\text{cd}} \end{bmatrix}^\top$$
- Verifies dimensional homogeneity ($\mathbf{d}(v_1) = \mathbf{d}(v_2)$) across all `<map_variables>` connections and enforces `public_interface` / `private_interface` (`in` / `out` / `none`) encapsulation hierarchy rules so no variable is driven by multiple `in` ports simultaneously.

### 2. Cardiac Action Potential & Microvascular Hemodynamics Solver

- Integrates membrane transmembrane potential $V_m(t)$ and voltage-dependent Hodgkin-Huxley / Noble / ten Tusscher ionic channel gating states $y_i(t) \in \{m, h, j, n, d, f, x_{r1}, x_{r2}, x_s\}$:
  $$C_m \frac{dV_m}{dt} = -\left(I_{\text{Na}} + I_{\text{K1}} + I_{\text{Kr}} + I_{\text{Ks}} + I_{\text{CaL}} + I_{\text{leak}} - I_{\text{stim}}(t)\right)$$
  $$I_{\text{Na}} = \bar{g}_{\text{Na}} m^3 h j (V_m - E_{\text{Na}}), \qquad \frac{dy_i}{dt} = \alpha_{y_i}(V_m)(1 - y_i) - \beta_{y_i}(V_m)y_i = \frac{y_{i,\infty}(V_m) - y_i}{\tau_{y_i}(V_m)}$$
- Supports coupled 0D 3-element Windkessel arterial/venous hemodynamic compliance loops ($C_{\text{art}} \frac{dP_{\text{art}}}{dt} = Q_{\text{in}}(t) - \frac{P_{\text{art}} - P_{\text{ven}}}{R_{\text{periph}}}$).

### 3. DAE Arena Lowering & Modelica / SBML Projection

- Lowers modular CellML component networks and MathML differential/algebraic equations into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerCellmlToDae`) and projects models into **Modelica 3.x** (`cellmlToModelica`) and **SBML Level 3** (`cellmlToSbml`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| `M9307` | error | `cellml-unresolved-connection-member` | Connection references unknown <memberKind> '<memberName>' in '<contextName>'. |
