# OpenSim Musculoskeletal Biomechanics (`.osim`)

`@modelscript/opensim` (`languages/opensim`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, musculoskeletal kinematic tree and mass/inertia validation, **Hill-type muscle-tendon activation and contraction dynamics** (`Thelen2003Muscle`, `Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle`), `DAEBuilder` lowering, and Modelica 3.x / ROS URDF projections for **OpenSim** biomechanical and orthopedic surgical planning models.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format           | Description                                                                                                                              |
| :-------- | :--------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.osim`   | OpenSim Document | XML specification of `BodySet`, `JointSet`, `ForceSet` (Hill muscles, ligaments, coordinate actuators), `MarkerSet`, and `WrapObjectSet` |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Multibody Skeletal Kinematics, Inertia & Wrapping Surfaces

- Parses `OpenSimDocument` (versions 3.x & 4.x) including rigid body segments (`Body` with mass $m_b > 0$ and 6-component inertia tensor $\mathbf{I}_b \succ 0$ satisfying triangle inequalities $I_{xx} + I_{yy} \ge I_{zz}$), anatomical joints (`PinJoint`, `SliderJoint`, `CustomJoint`, `WeldJoint`, `FreeJoint`, `BallJoint`, `UniversalJoint`), generalized coordinates (`Coordinate` with range-of-motion bounds $[q_{\min}, q_{\max}]$), motion-capture fiducial markers (`MarkerSet`), and muscle wrapping surfaces (`WrapCylinder`, `WrapSphere`, `WrapEllipsoid`).
- Formulates the articulated skeletal equations of motion driven by muscle-tendon forces $\mathbf{F}^T$ mapped through the moment-arm matrix $\mathbf{R}(\mathbf{q})$:
  $$\mathbf{M}(\mathbf{q})\ddot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{C}(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})\dot{\mathbf{q}} + \mathbf{G}(\mathbf{q}) = \mathbf{R}(\mathbf{q}) \, \mathbf{F}^T + \boldsymbol{\tau}_{\text{ext}}$$

### 2. Hill-Type Muscle-Tendon Activation & Contraction Solver

For every `Thelen2003Muscle` or `Millard2012EquilibriumMuscle` actuator, `@modelscript/opensim` integrates first-order neural excitation-to-activation dynamics ($u(t) \in [0, 1] \to a(t) \in [a_{\min}, 1]$) with asymmetric activation/deactivation time constants ($\tau_{\text{act}} \approx 10\text{ ms}$, $\tau_{\text{deact}} \approx 40\text{ ms}$):

$$\frac{da}{dt} = \frac{u - a}{\tau(a, u)}, \qquad \tau(a, u) = \begin{cases} \tau_{\text{act}}(0.5 + 1.5a) & u > a \\ \dfrac{\tau_{\text{deact}}}{0.5 + 1.5a} & u \le a \end{cases}$$

coupled with active force-length $f_L(\tilde{l}^M)$, concentric/eccentric force-velocity $f_V(\tilde{v}^M)$, passive parallel elastic $f_{PE}(\tilde{l}^M)$, and pennation angle $\alpha(\tilde{l}^M)$ tendon force equilibrium over total muscle-tendon path length $l^{MT} = l^M \cos\alpha + l^T$:

$$F^T = F_0^M \left(a \, f_L(\tilde{l}^M) f_V(\tilde{v}^M) + f_{PE}(\tilde{l}^M)\right)\cos\alpha = F_0^M \, f_{SE}(\tilde{l}^T)$$

### 3. DAE Lowering & Modelica / URDF Projection

- **`DAEBuilder` Linear Memory Lowering**: Emits generalized coordinates $(q_i, \omega_i)$, muscle activation states $a_m(t)$, normalized fiber lengths $\tilde{l}_m^M(t)$, and Hill-type force balance equations directly into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerOpenSimToDae`).
- **Modelica 3.x & ROS 2 URDF Export**: Projects musculoskeletal models into **Modelica** (`openSimToModelica`) and **ROS 2 URDF** (`openSimToUrdf`) for prosthetic/exoskeleton co-simulation.

---

# FEBio & SOFA Soft-Tissue Biomechanics (`.feb`, `.scn`)

`@modelscript/febio` (`languages/febio`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, hyperelastic and biphasic poroelastic material stability verification, element Jacobian volume positivity checking, non-linear strain-energy and Cauchy stress evaluation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and CalculiX `.inp` / Modelica projections for **FEBio (`febio_spec` 3.0 / 4.0)** soft-tissue biomechanics and **SOFA Framework (`.scn`)** real-time surgical simulation scenes.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format              | Description                                                                                                          |
| :-------- | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.feb`    | FEBio Specification | XML specification of `Material`, `Mesh` / `Geometry`, `Boundary`, `Loads`, `Contact`, and `Step` blocks              |
| `.scn`    | SOFA Scene Graph    | Simulation Open Framework Architecture (`Node`, `MechanicalObject`, `TetrahedronFEMForceField`, `CollisionPipeline`) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Hyperelastic, Viscoelastic & Biphasic Constitutive Models

`@modelscript/febio` parses and evaluates soft-tissue strain energy density functions $W(\mathbf{C})$ over the right Cauchy-Green deformation tensor $\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{F}^\top \mathbf{F}$, principal stretches $(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3)$, and volume ratio $J = \det \mathbf{F} = \lambda_1 \lambda_2 \lambda_3$:

| Constitutive Law        | Strain Energy Density $W(\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \lambda_3, J)$                                                                                                               | Stability & Physical Constraints                                              |
| :---------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Neo-Hookean**         | $W = \frac{\mu}{2}(I_1 - 3) - \mu \ln J + \frac{\lambda}{2}(\ln J)^2$                                                                                                       | $\mu > 0, \quad K = \lambda + \frac{2}{3}\mu > 0$                             |
| **Mooney-Rivlin**       | $W = C_1(\tilde{I}_1 - 3) + C_2(\tilde{I}_2 - 3) + \frac{K}{2}(\ln J)^2$                                                                                                    | $C_1 + C_2 > 0, \quad K > 0$                                                  |
| **Ogden ($N$-term)**    | $W = \sum_{p=1}^N \frac{\mu_p}{\alpha_p}\left(\tilde{\lambda}_1^{\alpha_p} + \tilde{\lambda}_2^{\alpha_p} + \tilde{\lambda}_3^{\alpha_p} - 3\right) + \frac{K}{2}(J - 1)^2$ | **Drucker stability**: $\sum_{p=1}^N \mu_p \alpha_p > 0$                      |
| **Holmes-Mow Biphasic** | $W_s(I_1, I_2, J) + \text{Darcy interstitial fluid flux } \mathbf{w} = -k(J) \nabla p$                                                                                      | Hydraulic permeability $k_0 > 0$, solid volume fraction $\phi_0^s \in (0, 1)$ |

### 2. Cauchy Stress Solver & Mesh Jacobian Verification

- Evaluates principal Cauchy stresses $\sigma_i = \frac{\lambda_i}{J} \frac{\partial W}{\partial \lambda_i}$ and verifies **3D tetrahedral/hexahedral element orientation** ($\det \mathbf{J}_e > 0$) across all mesh elements to prevent inverted or zero-volume elements prior to non-linear Newton-Raphson equilibrium iterations:
  $$\det \mathbf{J}_{\text{tet}} = \det \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{x}_2 - \mathbf{x}_1 & \mathbf{x}_3 - \mathbf{x}_1 & \mathbf{x}_4 - \mathbf{x}_1 \end{bmatrix} > 0$$

### 3. CalculiX FEA, Modelica & DAE Lowering

- **CalculiX / Abaqus `.inp` & Modelica Export**: Projects FEBio meshes, node/element sets, boundary conditions, and hyperelastic material cards directly into **CalculiX- / Abaqus-compatible `.inp`** decks (`febioToCalculixInp`) and **Modelica 3.x** Kelvin-Voigt viscoelastic compliance models (`febioToModelica`).
- **`DAEBuilder` Arena Lowering**: Lowers lumped viscoelastic deformation and biphasic interstitial pore-pressure relaxation ODEs into `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerFebioToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| `M9402` | error | `febio-inverted-element-jacobian` | Element '<elemId>' (<elemType>) has non-positive Jacobian determinant det(J) = '<detJ>'. |
| `M9403` | error | `febio-unresolved-node-or-set` | Unresolved <refKind> reference '<refId>' in '<contextName>'. |
| `M9404` | warning | `febio-unconstrained-rigid-body` | Model '<modelTitle>' has no fixed or prescribed displacement boundary conditions to prevent rigid-body motion. |
| `M9405` | error | `febio-invalid-biphasic-permeability` | Invalid biphasic/poroelastic parameter (<reason>) in material '<materialName>'. |
| `M9406` | error | `febio-invalid-time-stepper` | Invalid <Control> time-stepper configuration: time_steps='<timeSteps>', step_size='<stepSize>' (both must be > 0). |

# DICOM-RT Radiation Oncology & Clinical Dosimetry (`.rtplan`, `.rtstruct`, `.rtdose`)

`@modelscript/dicom-rt` (`languages/dicom-rt`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, **QUANTEC Organ-at-Risk (OAR)** dose constraint and Multi-Leaf Collimator (MLC) leaf/gantry kinematics verification, cumulative and differential **Dose-Volume Histogram (DVH)** integration, Linear-Quadratic **BED / EQD2** biological dose calculation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and OpenSCAD / SysML v2 projections for **DICOM Radiotherapy (`RTPLAN`, `RTSTRUCT`, `RTDOSE`)** treatment plans.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension   | Format                 | Description                                                                                                                 |
| :---------- | :--------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.rtplan`   | DICOM RT Plan          | External-beam photon/electron/proton beam geometry, gantry/couch/collimator angles, MLC control points, and fraction groups |
| `.rtstruct` | DICOM RT Structure Set | 3D anatomical contours for Planning Target Volumes (`PTV`, `CTV`, `GTV`) and Organs at Risk (`OAR`)                         |
| `.rtdose`   | DICOM RT Dose          | 3D dose grid arrays and cumulative/differential Dose-Volume Histogram (`DVH`) curves                                        |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Cumulative DVH, ICRU 83 Homogeneity & Paddick Conformity

`@modelscript/dicom-rt` integrates differential and cumulative Dose-Volume Histograms $V(D)$ across every Planning Target Volume (`PTV`) and Organ at Risk (`OAR`) to extract near-minimum dose $D_{98\%}$, prescription coverage $D_{95\%}$, median dose $D_{50\%}$, near-maximum hot-spot dose $D_{2\%}$, mean dose $D_{\text{mean}}$, and volume-at-dose $V_{x\text{Gy}}$:

$$\text{HI}_{\text{ICRU 83}} = \frac{D_{2\%} - D_{98\%}}{D_{50\%}}, \qquad \text{CI}_{\text{RTOG}} = \frac{PIV}{TV}, \qquad \text{CI}_{\text{Paddick}} = \frac{(TV_{\text{PIV}})^2}{TV \times PIV}$$

where $TV$ is the target volume, $PIV$ is the prescription isodose volume, and $TV_{\text{PIV}}$ is the target volume covered by the prescription isodose.

### 2. Linear-Quadratic Biological Dose ($\text{BED}$ & $\text{EQD2}$)

For a fractionation schedule of $n$ fractions at dose $d = D_{\text{total}}/n$ per fraction, `@modelscript/dicom-rt` evaluates the Linear-Quadratic (LQ) **Biologically Effective Dose ($\text{BED}$)** and **Equivalent Dose in $2\text{ Gy}$ Fractions ($\text{EQD2}$)**:

$$\text{BED} = n d \left(1 + \frac{d}{\alpha/\beta}\right), \qquad \text{EQD2} = \frac{\text{BED}}{1 + \frac{2}{\alpha/\beta}} = n d \left(\frac{d + \alpha/\beta}{2 + \alpha/\beta}\right)$$

using tissue-specific radiosensitivity ratios ($\alpha/\beta \approx 10\text{ Gy}$ for early-responding tumor targets, $\alpha/\beta \approx 2\text{ Gy}$ for late-responding CNS/spinal cord/optic pathways, and $\alpha/\beta \approx 3\text{ Gy}$ for lung, heart, rectum, and bladder).

### 3. QUANTEC Clinical OAR Constraints & MLC Delivery Kinematics

| Organ at Risk (`OAR`) | QUANTEC Metric                        | Clinical Threshold              | Endpoint Guarded                      |
| :-------------------- | :------------------------------------ | :------------------------------ | :------------------------------------ |
| Spinal Cord           | $D_{\max}$ ($D_{0.03\text{cc}}$)      | $\le 50\text{ Gy}$              | Radiation myelopathy ($< 0.2\%$ risk) |
| Brainstem             | $D_{\max}$                            | $\le 54\text{ Gy}$              | Cranial neuropathy / necrosis         |
| Optic Chiasm / Nerves | $D_{\max}$                            | $\le 55\text{ Gy}$              | Radiation-induced optic neuropathy    |
| Parotid Glands        | $D_{\text{mean}}$                     | $\le 25\text{ Gy}$              | Severe long-term xerostomia           |
| Bilateral Lungs       | $V_{20\text{Gy}}$ / $D_{\text{mean}}$ | $\le 30\%$ / $\le 20\text{ Gy}$ | Symptomatic radiation pneumonitis     |
| Heart / Pericardium   | $D_{\text{mean}}$                     | $\le 26\text{ Gy}$              | Pericarditis & late cardiac toxicity  |

Alongside dosimetric checks, `@modelscript/dicom-rt` audits Multi-Leaf Collimator (`MLCX`/`MLCY`) control points for leaf bank collisions ($x_{\text{B},i} - x_{\text{A},i} \ge \Delta_{\min}$), carriage overtravel, monotonic cumulative meterset weights ($w_0 = 0 \le w_k \le w_N = 1$), and non-coplanar gantry-couch collision clearance.

### 4. OpenSCAD, SysML v2 & DAE Projections

- Projects beam apertures and ROI structures into **OpenSCAD** 3D collimator blocks (`dicomRtToScad`), **OMG SysML v2** clinical safety requirement verification packages (`dicomRtToSysML2`), and `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerDicomRtToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for DICOM-RT (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9201` | error | `dicom-rt-missing-target-volume` | Treatment plan '<planLabel>' contains no clinical target volume ROI ('PTV', 'CTV', or 'GTV'). |
| `M9202` | error | `dicom-rt-mlc-leaf-overlap` | MLC leaf pair '<pairIndex>' on beam '<beamName>' control point '<cpIndex>' has bankA='<bankA> mm', bankB='<bankB> mm' (gap '<value> mm' < minimum '<MIN_MLC_LEAF_GAP_MM> mm'). |
| `M9203` | error | `dicom-rt-mlc-speed-exceeded` | MLC leaf pair '<pairIndex>' on beam '<beamName>' between control points '<cpFrom>' and '<cpTo>' travels at '<value> mm/s', exceeding physical motor limit '<value> mm/s'. |
| `M9204` | error | `dicom-rt-gantry-couch-collision` | Gantry angle '<gantryDeg> deg' and non-coplanar couch angle '<couchDeg> deg' on beam '<beamName>' control point '<cpIndex>' enter the gantry-couch collision hazard zone. |
| `M9205` | error | `dicom-rt-oar-dose-constraint-violated` | Organ-at-Risk '<roiName>' <metricKind> dose '<value> Gy' exceeds QUANTEC clinical constraint '<value> Gy'. |
| `M9206` | error | `dicom-rt-non-monotonic-cum-meterset` | Control point cumulativeMetersetWeight sequence on beam '<beamName>' is invalid: <detail>. |

| `M9208` | error | `dicom-rt-unresolved-frame-of-reference` | <modalitySource> FrameOfReferenceUID '<sourceUid>' does not match plan FrameOfReferenceUID '<planUid>'. |
| `M9209` | error | `dicom-rt-invalid-beam-meterset` | TREATMENT beam '<beamName>' has invalid delivery parameters (metersetMu='<metersetMu>', energyMeV='<energyMeV>'); both must be > 0. |
| `M9210` | warning | `dicom-rt-ptv-underdosage` | Target volume '<roiName>' D95% '<value> Gy' is below 95% of prescribed dose '<value> Gy' (minimum '<value> Gy'). |

---

# TOPAS & GATE Proton & Hadrontherapy Monte Carlo (`.topas`, `.mac`)

`@modelscript/topas` (`languages/topas`) provides native WebAssembly GLR parsing, Geant4 geometry hierarchy and parent-child bounding-box containment verification, **Bortfeld (1997) analytical Bragg peak depth-dose** and Spread-Out Bragg Peak (SOBP) evaluation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and OpenSCAD / Modelica projections for **TOPAS (Tool for Particle Simulation)** and **GATE** proton, carbon-ion, and flash radiotherapy beamline configurations.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension        | Format               | Description                                                                                                                                             |
| :--------------- | :------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `.topas`, `.txt` | TOPAS Parameter File | Typed Geant4 parameter system (`s:` string, `d:` double with units, `i:` integer, `b:` boolean, `dv:`/`sv:` vectors) for `Ge/`, `So/`, `Sc/`, and `Ph/` |
| `.mac`           | GATE / Geant4 Macro  | Command-stream macro (`/gate/world/daughters/...`, `/gate/source/...`, `/gate/actor/...`) for medical physics Monte Carlo                               |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Typed Geometry (`Ge/`), Beam Sources (`So/`) & Dose Scorers (`Sc/`)

- Parses hierarchical Geant4 CSG beamline components (`TsBox`, `TsCylinder`, `TsSphere`, `TsRangeModulator`, `TsPropeller`, `TsMultiLeafCollimator`, `TsAperture`, water phantoms, and patient CT volumes), particle sources (`Proton`, `Carbon12`, `Electron`, `Photon`), physics lists (`Ph/Default/Modules`), and `DoseToMedium` / `LETd` / `Fluence` scorers.
- Verifies parent-child spatial containment so every child component bounding box $[x_c \pm \Delta x_c, y_c \pm \Delta y_c, z_c \pm \Delta z_c]$ lies strictly inside its parent volume `Ge/<Comp>/Parent` without geometric overlap.

### 2. Analytical Bortfeld (1997) Bragg Peak & Range Calculation

`@modelscript/topas` evaluates the **Bragg-Kleeman range-energy relation** and **Bortfeld's (1997)** analytical depth-dose equation for proton and heavy-ion beams in water/tissue:

$$R_0 = \alpha \, E_0^p, \qquad \sigma_{\text{mono}}^2 = \alpha_{\sigma} R_0^{3 - 2/p}, \qquad \sigma^2 = \sigma_{\text{mono}}^2 + \sigma_E^2 \left(\alpha p E_0^{p-1}\right)^2$$

where $\alpha \approx 0.0022\text{ cm}\cdot\text{MeV}^{-p}$ and $p \approx 1.77$ for protons in water ($\rho = 1.0\text{ g/cm}^3$). Along depth $z$, the absorbed dose $D(z)$ is computed from the Gaussian range-straggling variable $\zeta = (R_0 - z)/\sigma$, computing:

- Continuous-slowing-down range $R_0$ ($\text{mm}$),
- Distal $80\%$ dose falloff depth $R_{80}$ and $90\%\text{–}10\%$ distal penumbra,
- Entrance-to-Bragg-peak dose ratio and dose-averaged Linear Energy Transfer ($\text{LET}_d$).

### 3. 3D Nozzle CSG, Modelica & DAE Lowering

- **OpenSCAD 3D Nozzle CSG (`topasToScad`)**: Projects treatment nozzle collimators, range modulators, ionization chambers, and water phantoms into parameterized 3D OpenSCAD CSG assemblies.
- **Modelica & `DAEBuilder` Lowering**: Projects beamline energy-degradation and target heating dynamics into **Modelica 3.x** (`topasToModelica`) and `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerTopasToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for TOPAS / GATE (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9601` | error | `topas-type-prefix-mismatch` | Parameter '<fullPath>' value '<rawVal>' does not match declared TOPAS type prefix '<typePrefix>:'. |
| `M9602` | error | `topas-unresolved-parent-component` | Geometry component '<compName>' references undeclared parent volume '<parentName>'. |
| `M9603` | error | `topas-non-positive-geometry-dimension` | Geometry component '<compName>' has invalid dimension: <detail>. |
| `M9604` | error | `topas-child-exceeds-parent-bounds` | Child geometry '<childName>' protrudes outside parent '<parentName>' along <axis>-axis ('<childExtent> mm' > '<parentHalfExtent> mm'). |
| `M9605` | error | `topas-undefined-material` | Component '<compName>' references unknown material '<materialName>' not found in Geant4/NIST materials or custom 'Ma/' definitions. |
| `M9606` | error | `topas-invalid-beam-energy` | Particle source '<sourceName>' has invalid beam energy specification: <detail>. |
| `M9607` | error | `topas-circular-include-file` | Circular or self-referential includeFile chain detected: '<cycleChain>'. |
| `M9608` | error | `topas-scorer-missing-component` | Scorer '<scorerName>' has invalid configuration: <detail>. |
| `M9609` | error | `topas-vector-length-mismatch` | Vector parameter '<fullPath>' declares length '<declaredCount>' but provides '<actualCount>' elements. |
| `M9610` | warning | `topas-duplicate-parameter-assignment` | Parameter '<fullPath>' is assigned multiple times in the same file without 'change' override prefix. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect TOPAS/GATE geometry components, beam sources, and scorers
msx topas inspect ProtonNozzle.topas

# Validate parent-child bounding box containment, materials, and beam energy
msx topas validate ProtonNozzle.topas

# Compute analytical Bortfeld Bragg peak range (R0, R80) and depth-dose curve
msx topas bragg-peak ProtonNozzle.topas

# Project treatment nozzle and phantom geometry to OpenSCAD, Modelica, or DAE
msx topas to-scad ProtonNozzle.topas > ProtonNozzle.scad
msx topas to-modelica ProtonNozzle.topas > ProtonNozzle.mo
msx topas to-dae ProtonNozzle.topas
```

```typescript
  parseTopasModel,

  topasToScad,
  topasToModelica,
} from "@modelscript/topas";
```

# NIfTI & NRRD Volumetric Medical Imaging (`.nii`, `.nrrd`, `.nhdr`)

`@modelscript/nifti` (`languages/nifti`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, $4 \times 4$ `qform` quaternion and `sform` affine **Right-Anterior-Superior (RAS)** coordinate transformation validation, anatomical segmentation labelmap volume calculation, **Marching Tetrahedra** 3D iso-surface mesh extraction, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and ISO 10303-21 STEP / OpenSCAD projections for **NIfTI-1 / NIfTI-2** and **NRRD (Nearly Raw Raster Data)** medical imaging volumes.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension        | Format                | Description                                                                                                              |
| :--------------- | :-------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.nii`           | NIfTI-1 / NIfTI-2     | Neuroimaging & clinical volumetric format encoding 3D/4D voxel grids, `pixdim` spacings, and `qform`/`sform` RAS affines |
| `.nrrd`, `.nhdr` | Teem / 3D Slicer NRRD | Nearly Raw Raster Data header/volume with `space directions`, `space origin`, and anatomical segmentation labelmaps      |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Voxel-to-RAS Affine Geometry & Orientation Auditing

`@modelscript/nifti` parses voxel dimensions $(N_i, N_j, N_k, N_t)$, millimeter spacings $(\Delta i, \Delta j, \Delta k) = (\text{pixdim}[1], \text{pixdim}[2], \text{pixdim}[3])$, unit quaternion parameters $(b, c, d)$ with $a = \sqrt{\max(0, 1 - (b^2 + c^2 + d^2))}$ and `qfac` $q \in \{-1, +1\}$, and $4 \times 4$ `sform` homogeneous transformation matrices:

$$\begin{bmatrix} x_{\text{RAS}} \\ y_{\text{RAS}} \\ z_{\text{RAS}} \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{R}(a, b, c, d) \begin{bmatrix} \Delta i \cdot i \\ \Delta j \cdot j \\ q \cdot \Delta k \cdot k \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} q_{\text{offset},x} \\ q_{\text{offset},y} \\ q_{\text{offset},z} \end{bmatrix}$$

Pre-flight diagnostics verify:

- Non-singular affine determinant ($\lvert \det(\mathbf{M}_{3\times 3}) \rvert > 10^{-9}$) so voxels map bijectively to physical space,
- Consistency of radiological vs. neurological left-right handedness ($\text{sign}(\det \mathbf{M}_{\text{qform}}) = \text{sign}(\det \mathbf{M}_{\text{sform}})$),
- Isotropic/sub-millimeter slice spacing limits for surgical navigation and stereotactic radiosurgery.

### 2. Segmentation Labelmaps & Marching Tetrahedra Iso-Surfacing

- Computes exact organ and tumor ROI volumes $V_{\text{ROI}} = N_{\text{voxels}} \cdot \lvert \det(\mathbf{M}_{3\times 3}) \rvert$ ($\text{mm}^3$ and $\text{cm}^3$), physical RAS centroids, and axis-aligned bounding boxes.
- Decomposes each cubic voxel into 6 Kuhn tetrahedra and extracts a watertight, manifold-consistent 3D triangular surface mesh at any threshold $I_{\text{iso}}$ via linear edge interpolation (`extractIsoSurfaceMesh`):
  $$\mathbf{p}_{ab} = \mathbf{p}_a + \frac{I_{\text{iso}} - I_a}{I_b - I_a}\left(\mathbf{p}_b - \mathbf{p}_a\right)$$

### 3. CAD Reconstruction (STEP AP242, OpenSCAD & DAE Lowering)

- Projects extracted anatomical iso-surfaces directly into **ISO 10303-21 STEP** B-Rep faceted shells (`niftiToStep`), **OpenSCAD** `polyhedron(...)` CSG modules (`niftiToScad`), and `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerNiftiToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for NIfTI / NRRD (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9501` | error | `nifti-invalid-dimensions` | Invalid NIfTI/NRRD volume dimensions: dim[0]='<ndim>', spatial size=(<nx>, <ny>, <nz>). |
| `M9502` | error | `nifti-non-positive-voxel-spacing` | Non-positive voxel spacing pixdim=(<dx>, <dy>, <dz>) mm (all spatial spacings must be > 0). |
| `M9503` | error | `nifti-singular-affine-transform` | 4x4 sform affine transformation matrix is singular or degenerate with det(A) = '<detA>'. |
| `M9504` | error | `nifti-invalid-quaternion-norm` | Invalid qform quaternion parameters (<b>, <c>, <d>): b^2 + c^2 + d^2 = '<normSq>' exceeds 1.0. |
| `M9505` | error | `nifti-qform-sform-handedness-mismatch` | Coordinate handedness mismatch between active qform (qfac sign '<qfacSign>') and sform (det sign '<sformDetSign>'). |
| `M9506` | error | `nifti-zero-intensity-scale-slope` | Intensity scaling has scl_slope='<sclSlope>' with active scaling (scl_inter='<sclInter>'), zeroing all voxel intensities. |
| `M9507` | error | `nifti-unsupported-datatype` | Unsupported or invalid NIfTI/NRRD voxel datatype '<datatypeName>' (code='<datatypeCode>'). |
| `M9508` | error | `nifti-voxel-data-size-mismatch` | Voxel payload count '<actualCount>' does not match expected '<expectedCount>' for dimensions <dimsDesc>. |
| `M9509` | warning | `nifti-empty-segmentation-mask` | Segmentation labelmap '<title>' contains zero foreground voxels across all anatomical labels. |
| `M9510` | warning | `nifti-anisotropic-slice-gap-warning` | Slice thickness dz='<dz>' mm exceeds in-plane resolution '<minInPlane>' mm by '<ratio>x' (> 5x threshold), risking severe 3D stair-step artifacts. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect NIfTI/NRRD dimensions, voxel spacings, and RAS affine transforms
msx nifti inspect BrainAtlas.nii

# Validate qform/sform affine non-singularity and handedness consistency
msx nifti validate BrainAtlas.nii

# Extract 3D iso-surface mesh and ROI volumes from segmentation volume
msx nifti mesh BrainAtlas.nii

# Export reconstructed anatomical geometry to ISO 10303-21 STEP, OpenSCAD, or DAE
msx nifti to-step BrainAtlas.nii > BrainAtlas.stp
msx nifti to-scad BrainAtlas.nii > BrainAtlas.scad
msx nifti to-dae BrainAtlas.nii
```

# 3MF Medical Surgical Guides & Implants (`.3mf`)

`@modelscript/three-mf` (`languages/three-mf`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, **half-edge 2-manifold watertightness** and Euler-Poincaré characteristic ($\chi = V - E + F$) verification, surgical guide minimum wall-thickness and drill-sleeve K-wire clearance auditing, osteotomy cutting-plane normal validation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and ISO 10303-21 STEP / OpenSCAD projections for **ISO/ASTM 52915 3MF Medical** patient-specific 3D-printed surgical guides and cranial/orthopedic implants.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension | Format             | Description                                                                                                                               |
| :-------- | :----------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.3mf`    | ISO/ASTM 52915 3MF | 3D Manufacturing Format (`<model>`, `<resources>`, `<mesh>`, `<vertices>`, `<triangles>`, `<build>`, and surgical guide/implant metadata) |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Watertight 2-Manifold Topology & Signed Divergence Volume

`@modelscript/three-mf` constructs the directed half-edge incidence graph over `<vertices>` and `<triangles>` (`analyzeMeshTopology`) to verify that every directed edge $(u \to v)$ is paired with exactly one opposite half-edge $(v \to u)$:

$$\chi = V - E + F = 2(S - g), \qquad V_{\text{signed}} = \frac{1}{6}\sum_{f=1}^{F} \mathbf{v}_{f,1} \cdot \left(\mathbf{v}_{f,2} \times \mathbf{v}_{f,3}\right)$$

where $S$ is the number of closed connected shells and $g$ is the topological genus (e.g., number of drill-guide holes through the template). Pre-flight checks flag open boundary edges ($N_{\text{boundary}} > 0$), non-manifold edges shared by $>2$ faces, inverted negative-volume shells, and zero-area degenerate triangles ($\|\left(\mathbf{v}_2 - \mathbf{v}_1\right) \times \left(\mathbf{v}_3 - \mathbf{v}_1\right)\| = 0$).

### 2. Surgical Cutting Guide & Drill-Sleeve Verification

- Validates patient-specific osteotomy cutting guides and pedicle/dental drill sleeves:
  - **Minimum Wall Thickness**: Enforces structural wall thickness $t_{\text{wall}} \ge 1.2\text{ mm}$ for biocompatible additive manufacturing (SLS PA12, SLA BioMed Clear/Amber, Ti6Al4V DMLS).
  - **Drill-Sleeve Annular Wall & K-Wire Clearance**: Checks radial wall thickness $r_{\text{outer}} - r_{\text{inner}} \ge 1.0\text{ mm}$ and positive diametral clearance between guide cylinder bore and surgical drill bit / Kirschner wire.
  - **Osteotomy Plane Normals**: Verifies unit-normalized cutting-plane normal vectors ($\lvert \|\mathbf{n}\|_2 - 1 \rvert < 10^{-4}$).

### 3. ISO 10303-21 STEP, OpenSCAD & DAE Lowering

- Exports verified surgical guides and implants to **ISO 10303-21 STEP** (`threeMfToStep`), **OpenSCAD** (`threeMfToScad`), and `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerThreeMfToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for 3MF Medical (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9701` | error | `three-mf-non-manifold-edge` | Mesh in object '<objId>' is not a closed 2-manifold ('<openEdges>' open boundary edges, '<nonManifoldEdges>' non-manifold edges). |
| `M9702` | error | `three-mf-degenerate-triangle` | Triangle #<triIndex> (<v1>, <v2>, <v3>) in object '<objId>' is degenerate (duplicate vertex indices or zero area). |
| `M9703` | error | `three-mf-negative-mesh-volume` | Mesh in object '<objId>' has non-positive signed volume '<signedVol> mm^3' (inverted outward face normals). |
| `M9704` | error | `three-mf-unresolved-build-object` | Build '<item>' references undefined resource '<object id="<objectId>">'. |
| `M9705` | error | `three-mf-wall-thickness-violation` | Surgical guide or cannula '<targetName>' has wall thickness '<actualMm> mm' below minimum additive manufacturing threshold '<minMm> mm'. |
| `M9706` | error | `three-mf-invalid-osteotomy-guide-axis` | Osteotomy plane or drill sleeve '<guideFeatureId>' on object '<objId>' has a zero-length normal/axis vector. |
| `M9707` | error | `three-mf-missing-biocompatible-material` | Medical object '<objId>' lacks an approved ISO 10993 / USP Class VI biocompatible material (found '<matName>'). |
| `M9708` | error | `three-mf-singular-item-transform` | Build '<item objectid="<objectId>">' has singular or reflection 4x3 affine transform with determinant '<det>'. |
| `M9709` | error | `three-mf-out-of-bounds-vertex-index` | Triangle #<triIndex> (<v1>, <v2>, <v3>) in object '<objId>' references vertex index outside [0, <value>]. |
| `M9710` | error | `three-mf-duplicate-object-id` | Duplicate '<object id="<objId>">' declared in '<resources>'. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect 3MF objects, build items, and surgical guide metadata
msx three-mf inspect MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf

# Validate 2-manifold watertightness, wall thickness, and osteotomy planes
msx three-mf validate MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf

# Compute mesh topology metrics (Euler characteristic, volume, surface area)
msx three-mf topology MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf

# Export surgical guide mesh to ISO 10303-21 STEP, OpenSCAD, or DAE arena
msx three-mf to-step MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf > MandibleOsteotomyGuide.stp
msx three-mf to-scad MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf > MandibleOsteotomyGuide.scad
msx three-mf to-dae MandibleOsteotomyGuide.3mf
```

# OpenIGTLink & PLUS Surgical Navigation (`.igtl`, `.plus.xml`)

`@modelscript/igtl` (`languages/igtl`) provides native WebAssembly parsing, $SE(3)$ homogeneous transform orthogonality ($\mathbf{R}^\top\mathbf{R} = \mathbf{I}$, $\det\mathbf{R} = +1$) and coordinate-frame graph connectivity verification, **stylus pivot calibration**, **Fitzpatrick (1998) Target Registration Error ($\text{TRE}$)** estimation, `DAEBuilder` lowering, and ROS 2 URDF / Modelica projections for **OpenIGTLink** and **PLUS Toolkit** image-guided surgical navigation systems.

---

## Supported Extensions & Standards

| Extension           | Format              | Description                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :------------------ | :------------------ | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.plus.xml`, `.xml` | PLUS Toolkit Config | `PlusConfiguration` XML defining optical/EM trackers (`DataCollection`), `<CoordinateDefinitions>` $SE(3)$ transforms, pivot/phantom calibration, and `<PlusOpenIGTLinkServer>` streams |
| `.igtl`             | OpenIGTLink Stream  | Surgical navigation `TRANSFORM`, `POSITION`, `TRACKING_DATA`, `IMAGE`, and `STATUS` message definitions                                                                                 |

---

## Key Capabilities

### 1. $SE(3)$ Coordinate Frame Graph & Matrix Orthogonality

`@modelscript/igtl` parses $4 \times 4$ homogeneous transformations $\mathbf{T}_{\text{From}\to\text{To}} \in SE(3)$ across surgical coordinate frames (`Tracker`, `Patient`, `Reference`, `Stylus`, `StylusTip`, `Probe`, `UltrasoundImage`, `RAS`) and verifies $SO(3)$ rotation matrix orthogonality ($\|\mathbf{R}^\top\mathbf{R} - \mathbf{I}\|_F < 10^{-4}$ and $\det\mathbf{R} = +1$):

$$^{A}\mathbf{T}_{C} = {}^{A}\mathbf{T}_{B} \, {}^{B}\mathbf{T}_{C}, \qquad \mathbf{T}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}^\top & -\mathbf{R}^\top\mathbf{t} \\ \mathbf{0}^\top & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

Breadth-first traversal over `<CoordinateDefinitions>` resolves arbitrary multi-hop kinematic chains (e.g., $\text{StylusTip} \to \text{Stylus} \to \text{Tracker} \to \text{Reference} \to \text{Patient} \to \text{RAS}$) and detects disconnected subgraphs or contradictory cycle transforms.

### 2. Stylus Pivot Calibration & Fitzpatrick Target Registration Error ($\text{TRE}$)

- **Spherical Stylus Pivot Calibration**: Given $M$ poses $\{(\mathbf{R}_i, \mathbf{t}_i)\}_{i=1}^M$ of a tracked surgical pointer pivoting around a stationary divot, `@modelscript/igtl` solves the overdetermined linear least-squares system (`solveTransformChainAndPivot`) for the local tip offset $\mathbf{p}_{\text{tip}}$ and global pivot position $\mathbf{p}_{\text{pivot}}$:
  $$\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}_1 & -\mathbf{I}_3 \\ \vdots & \vdots \\ \mathbf{R}_M & -\mathbf{I}_3 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{p}_{\text{tip}} \\ \mathbf{p}_{\text{pivot}} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} -\mathbf{t}_1 \\ \vdots \\ -\mathbf{t}_M \end{bmatrix}, \qquad e_{\text{RMS}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M \|\mathbf{R}_i \mathbf{p}_{\text{tip}} + \mathbf{t}_i - \mathbf{p}_{\text{pivot}}\|^2}$$
- **Fitzpatrick (1998) Target Registration Error**: Evaluates expected RMS registration error at surgical target $\mathbf{r}$ from $N$ anatomical/bone-screw fiducial markers with isotropic Fiducial Localization Error ($\text{FLE}$) and principal-axis RMS distances $f_k$:
  $$\langle \text{TRE}^2(\mathbf{r}) \rangle = \frac{\langle \text{FLE}^2 \rangle}{N}\left(1 + \frac{1}{3}\sum_{k=1}^{3}\frac{d_k^2}{f_k^2}\right)$$

### 3. ROS 2 URDF, Modelica & DAE Projections

- Projects surgical tracker coordinate trees into **ROS 2 URDF** (`igtlToUrdf`), **Modelica 3.x** (`igtlToModelica`), and `@modelscript/runtime`'s `DAEBuilder` arena (`lowerIgtlToDae`).

---

## Pre-Flight Diagnostics

### Diagnostics for OpenIGTLink / PLUS (10 rules)
| Code | Severity | Identifier | Summary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `M9801` | error | `igtl-non-orthogonal-rotation` | Transform '<from> -> <to>' has non-orthogonal or reflection 3x3 rotation block (\|\|R^T R - I\|\|_F = <frobErr>, det(R) = <det>). |
| `M9802` | error | `igtl-invalid-homogeneous-bottom-row` | Transform '<from> -> <to>' has invalid 4x4 homogeneous bottom row '[<rowStr>]' (expected '[0, 0, 0, 1]'). |
| `M9803` | error | `igtl-disconnected-coordinate-frame` | Coordinate frame graph is disconnected: <detail>. |
| `M9804` | error | `igtl-cyclic-transform-chain` | Directed cycle detected in coordinate transform definitions: '<cycleStr>'. |
| `M9805` | warning | `igtl-excessive-registration-error` | Registration or calibration RMS error '<errorMm> mm' on '<contextName>' exceeds clinical safety threshold '<thresholdMm> mm'. |
| `M9806` | error | `igtl-invalid-acquisition-rate` | Device '<deviceId>' has invalid AcquisitionRate '<rateHz> Hz' (must be > 0 Hz). |
| `M9807` | error | `igtl-unresolved-device-or-channel` | '<contextName>' references undeclared <refKind> '<refId>'. |
| `M9808` | error | `igtl-self-transform-identity-mismatch` | Self-transform '<frameName> -> <frameName>' must be the 4x4 identity matrix. |
| `M9809` | error | `igtl-invalid-server-port` | OpenIGTLink server '<serverId>' ListeningPort '<port>' is outside valid TCP port range [1024, 65535]. |
| `M9810` | error | `igtl-duplicate-transform-edge` | Duplicate '<Transform>' defined for coordinate frame pair '(<from>, <to>)'. |

---

## CLI Usage

```bash
# Inspect tracking devices, SE(3) transforms, and OpenIGTLink servers
msx igtl inspect LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml

# Validate SE(3) rotation orthogonality, frame connectivity, and TRE limits
msx igtl validate LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml

# Solve coordinate frame chains, stylus pivot calibration, and Fitzpatrick TRE
msx igtl calibrate LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml

# Project surgical navigation frame tree to ROS 2 URDF, Modelica, or DAE arena
msx igtl to-urdf LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml > SurgicalTracker.urdf
msx igtl to-modelica LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml > SurgicalTracker.mo
msx igtl to-dae LaparoscopicTracker.plus.xml
```

---

## Programmatic TypeScript SDK

```typescript
import {
  parseIgtlModel,
  solveTransformChainAndPivot,
  lowerIgtlToDae,
  igtlToUrdf,
  igtlToModelica,
} from "@modelscript/igtl";
import { DAEBuilder } from "@modelscript/runtime";

const model = parseIgtlModel(plusXmlSource);
const calibration = solveTransformChainAndPivot(model);

const builder = new DAEBuilder();
lowerIgtlToDae(model, builder);
const urdfXml = igtlToUrdf(model);
const modelicaCode = igtlToModelica(model);
```

# Aerospace & Aviation

**Tagline:** Flight dynamics, propulsion & mission telemetry
**Summary:** Connect SysML v2 architectures and ReqIF requirements to JSBSim flight models, NASA ROCETS propulsion decks, and CCSDS telemetry, then simulate, verify, and export FMUs without leaving one toolchain.
**Headline:** From requirements to flight dynamics in a single, verifiable thread

**Target Languages:** `jsbsim`, `rocets`, `ccsds`, `easy5`, `sysml2`, `reqif`, `oscal`, `step`, `qif`, `cfd`, `fea`, `fortran`
**Supported Standards:** SysML v2 / KerML, ReqIF, NIST OSCAL 1.1, CCSDS OEM / OPM / XTCE, STEP AP242, ISO 23952 QIF 3.0, FMI 2.0 / 3.0, SSP

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Requirements drift from analysis:** Requirements live in one tool, physics in another. Traceability is rebuilt by hand before every review.
- **Legacy Fortran & decks:** Decades of validated propulsion and flight code are locked in card decks and Fortran routines nobody wants to touch.
- **Certification evidence is manual:** Verification artifacts are assembled from screenshots and spreadsheets instead of generated from the models.

### Key Capabilities
- **6-DOF flight dynamics:** Parse JSBSim aircraft definitions and lower them to DAEs for simulation and linearization.
- **Propulsion transients:** Ingest ROCETS engine decks and turbomachinery maps, with a bridge for embedded Fortran user routines.
- **Mission telemetry:** Read CCSDS orbit and XTCE telemetry definitions and align them with simulated trajectories.
- **Formal verification:** Check SysML v2 constraints and requirement contracts with k-induction and SMT-backed proofs.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Capture:** SysML v2 architecture + ReqIF requirements
2. **Model:** JSBSim airframe, ROCETS engine, Modelica subsystems
3. **Simulate:** Stiff DAE solvers, Monte Carlo, surrogates
4. **Verify:** Requirement entailment & SARIF evidence

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx rocets simulate engine.roc
msx render SpacecraftPower spacecraft.sysml --view IBD -o ibd.svg
msx verify BrakingController brake.mo --format sarif
```

# Power Systems & Grid

**Tagline:** EMT, power flow & grid-code compliance
**Summary:** Run PSCAD/EMTDC electromagnetic transients, Siemens PSS/E, DIgSILENT PowerFactory, and GE PSLF transmission studies alongside OpenDSS distribution, OCPP EV charging, and OpenADR demand response — with IEEE 2800, NERC PRC-029, and ENTSO-E RfG verification built in.
**Headline:** Grid-code compliance, from PSCAD to IEEE 2800 in one pipeline

**Target Languages:** `pscad`, `psse`, `powerfactory`, `pslf`, `cgmes`, `opendss`, `ocpp`, `openadr`, `ampl`, `oscal`, `modelica`, `c`, `fortran`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** IEEE 2800-2022 & NERC PRC-029-1, ENTSO-E RfG & IEEE 1547-2018, DIgSILENT PowerFactory (.dsl / .dgs), GE PSLF (.epc / .dyd) & PSS/E RAW v30–35, OCPP 1.6J / 2.0.1 & OpenADR 2.0b, NIST OSCAL 1.1 (NERC CIP), IEEE C37.111 COMTRADE, CIGRE black-box DLLs

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Interconnection queues:** Inverter-based resources need extensive EMT and ride-through studies before they can connect.
- **Black-box vendor models:** OEM controller DLLs only run inside specific desktop tools on specific operating systems.
- **Fragmented studies:** Transmission, distribution, and EMT models are maintained separately and drift apart.

### Key Capabilities
- **EMT simulation:** Native PSCAD project ingestion and electromagnetic transient solving.
- **Ride-through verification:** Automated IEEE 2800 LVRT/HVRT and NERC PRC-029 checks with JSON reports.
- **Power flow & DER hosting:** PSS/E, PowerFactory, and PSLF transmission cases plus OpenDSS unbalanced distribution and hosting-capacity analysis.
- **COMTRADE waveforms:** Read and write IEEE C37.111 transient recordings for comparison against field data.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Import:** PSCAD .pscx, PSS/E .raw, PowerFactory .dsl/.dgs, PSLF .epc, OpenDSS .dss
2. **Simulate:** EMT, RMS & power flow solvers
3. **Record:** COMTRADE waveforms
4. **Comply:** IEEE 2800 / NERC PRC-029 / ENTSO-E RfG report

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx pscad verify-ieee2800 SolarPlant_250MW.pscx --tstop 3.0 --step 20us -o report.json
msx psse solve case.raw
msx psse diagram case.raw
```

# Oil, Gas & Subsurface

**Tagline:** Flow assurance, pipelines & reservoirs

**Headline:** Flow assurance from reservoir to export pipeline

**Target Languages:** `olga`, `lps`, `eclipse`, `tough`, `phreeqc`, `aspen`, `gproms`, `sima`, `modelica`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** ISO 20765-1, ISO 20765-2, TOUGH2 / TOUGH3 EOS, USGS PHREEQC, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Siloed disciplines:** Reservoir, wells, pipelines, and facilities teams each use different simulators.
- **Costly transients:** Slugging, shutdown, and restart studies need many long runs across scenarios.
- **Hard-to-audit decks:** Large keyword decks are difficult to review, lint, and version-control.

### Key Capabilities
- **Multiphase transients:** Simulate OLGA subsea tie-backs and risers, and plot pipeline profiles.
- **Thermodynamics:** Flash calculations and phase envelopes from compositional fluid definitions.
- **Pipeline networks:** PipelineStudio TGNET/TLNET hydraulics with ISO 20765 gas properties.
- **Reservoir & scaling:** Parse ECLIPSE and TOUGH decks and evaluate PHREEQC mineral saturation indices.

2. **Flowline:** OLGA multiphase
3. **Network:** PipelineStudio hydraulics
4. **Facility:** Aspen & gPROMS flowsheets

```bash
msx olga simulate subsea_tieback.opi --duration=3600 --out=traj.csv
```

# Nuclear

**Tagline:** Reactor thermal-hydraulics & point kinetics
**Summary:** Parse RELAP5-3D card decks, simulate non-equilibrium two-phase hydrodynamics with delayed-neutron point kinetics, and project loops to Modelica for system-level studies.
**Headline:** Reactor thermal-hydraulics you can read, diff, and verify

**Target Languages:** `relap5`, `modelica`, `fortran`, `sysml2`, `reqif`, `oscal`, `csv`
**Supported Standards:** RELAP5-3D input decks, SysML v2, ReqIF, NIST OSCAL 1.1, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **80-column legacy decks:** Safety-critical models are written as fixed-format cards, which makes review error-prone.
- **Traceability for licensing:** Regulators expect clear links between requirements, models, and results.
- **Long iteration loops:** Desktop-only workflows slow down parametric and uncertainty studies.

### Key Capabilities
- **Card deck parsing:** High-fidelity parsing of 80-column RELAP5 input with structural linting.
- **Two-phase hydrodynamics:** Non-equilibrium two-phase flow lowered to DAEs.
- **Point kinetics:** 6-group delayed neutron point kinetics coupled to thermal-hydraulics.
- **Requirement traceability:** Link models to SysML v2 / ReqIF safety requirements.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Import:** RELAP5 card decks
2. **Lint:** Structural & unit checks
3. **Simulate:** Two-phase + kinetics
4. **Trace:** Requirements evidence

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx lint ./decks --format json
msx mc Loop loop.mo
msx verify Loop loop.mo --format sarif
```

# Electronics, RF & Telecommunications

**Tagline:** SPICE, compact models, IBIS, S-parameters, DWDM & 5G RAN
**Summary:** Simulate SPICE netlists, compile Verilog-A compact models, integrate IBIS buffers and Touchstone S-parameters, and model DWDM optical transport, 5G NR / LTE RAN coverage, and TIA-598-D outside-plant fiber networks.
**Headline:** Analog, RF, signal integrity, and optical/wireless telecom in one open toolchain

**Target Languages:** `spice`, `verilog-a`, `ibis`, `touchstone`, `optical`, `ran`, `fiber`, `modelica`, `c`
**Supported Standards:** IEEE 1857 Verilog-A / AMS, IBIS & Touchstone 1.0 / 2.0, ITU-T G.694.1 DWDM & Telcordia SR-4731 OTDR (.sor), 3GPP TR 38.901 5G NR & NSMA WG16 (.adf / .msi), TIA-598-D Outside-Plant Fiber, SPICE netlists & FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Fragmented EDA flows:** Circuit, device, and channel models each need a different simulator.
- **Non-passive macromodels:** Measured S-parameters produce unstable time-domain simulations if they aren't passive.
- **System context missing:** Electronics are rarely simulated together with the mechanical and thermal system around them.

### Key Capabilities
- **Circuit analysis:** SPICE operating point, transient, and AC analyses from the CLI.
- **Compact models:** Compile Verilog-A behavioral models to DAEs and export SPICE netlists.
- **Rational macromodels:** Vector fitting with Hamiltonian passivity enforcement for Touchstone data.
- **Optical, 5G RAN & Fiber:** DWDM OSNR/GSNR & OTDR trace analysis, 3GPP 38.901 RF coverage, and TIA-598-D strand splicing.

### End-to-End Workflow
1. **Netlist:** SPICE + Verilog-A devices
2. **Channel:** Touchstone, IBIS, DWDM & RAN
3. **Simulate:** OP, transient, AC & link budgets
4. **Integrate:** Modelica / FMU export

### Representative CLI Workflow
```bash
msx spice simulate LowPassFilter.cir --analysis op
msx spice simulate PowerSupply.cir --analysis tran --tstep 1e-6 --tstop 0.02 --out transient.csv
msx spice simulate AudioAmplifier.sp --analysis ac --format csv --out bode.csv
```

# Robotics & Industrial Automation

**Supported Standards:** IEC 61131-3 / PLCopen XML, IEC 62714 AutomationML (CAEX), URDF / Xacro, OpenUSD (Pixar / ASWF / AOUSD), STEP AP242, ISO 23952 QIF 3.0, FMI 2.0 / 3.0

### Industry Challenges & Solutions
- **Control vs. plant gap:** PLC logic is tested on hardware late, after mechanical design is frozen.
- **Format conversions:** Robot descriptions, CAD, and mechanism models must be converted by hand.
- **Unsafe edge cases:** Interlocks and state machines fail in ways that tests rarely cover.

### Key Capabilities
- **Robot dynamics:** URDF/Xacro kinematics with Featherstone dynamics and Modelica export.

- **Mechanism & metrology:** Mobility analysis for Adams/SIMPACK and ISO 23952 QIF GD&T inspection.

### End-to-End Workflow

2. **Control:** PLCopen & IEC 61131-3
3. **Simulate:** Virtual commissioning
4. **Verify:** Safety & QIF metrology

### Representative CLI Workflow

# Linter Rules Reference

ModelScript ships **1127 diagnostic rules** across **80 languages**. This page is generated from each language's rule catalog (for example `languages/modelica/src/errors.ts`), so codes, severities and message templates match what the tools report. Text in `<angle brackets>` is filled in from your model.

## Running the linters

Diagnostics appear as you type in VS Code and Studio through the language server. From the command line:

```bash
# Languages handled by the unified linter (detected by file extension)
msx lint ./models
msx lint ./models --format json --strict

# Domain formats with their own command
msx spice lint SensorFrontEnd.net
```

The **CLI** column below shows which command reports each language's rules.

## Modelica {#modelica}

Acausal multi-domain physics. **226 rules** · `@modelscript/modelica` · Source: `languages/modelica/src/errors.ts` · [Language guide](../languages/modelica.md)

**`M1xxx` — Syntax & parse**

| <span id="modelica-m1002"></span>`M1002` | `parse-missing`              | [error] | Parse error: '<code>&lt;expected&gt;</code>' expected.                                                                               |
| <span id="modelica-m1003"></span>`M1003` | `empty-array-constructor`    | [error] | Parse error: Empty array constructors are not valid in Modelica.                                                                     |
| <span id="modelica-m1004"></span>`M1004` | `identity-first-arg-integer` | [error] | First argument to identity in component <code>&lt;compName&gt;</code> must be Integer expression.                                    |
| <span id="modelica-m1005"></span>`M1005` | `subscripted-modifier`       | [error] | Subscripting modifiers is not allowed. Apply the modification on the whole identifier using an array-expression or an each-modifier. |

| <span id="modelscript-m3002"></span>`M3002` | `invalid-binary-operand`  | [error] | Operator '<code>&lt;op&gt;</code>' cannot be applied to operands of type '<code>&lt;type&gt;</code>'.                        |
| <span id="modelscript-m3003"></span>`M3003` | `const-reassignment`      | [error] | Cannot assign to '<code>&lt;name&gt;</code>' because it is a constant.                                                       |
| <span id="modelscript-m4001"></span>`M4001` | `non-iterable-collection` | [error] | Expression '<code>&lt;expr&gt;</code>' in 'for' clause is not iterable.                                                      |
| <span id="modelscript-m4002"></span>`M4002` | `flwor-unbound-variable`  | [error] | Variable '<code>&lt;varName&gt;</code>' in FLWOR clause is not bound in preceding 'for' or 'let' clauses.                    |
| <span id="modelscript-m5001"></span>`M5001` | `argument-count-mismatch` | [error] | Function '<code>&lt;fnName&gt;</code>' expects <code>&lt;expected&gt;</code> arguments, but got <code>&lt;actual&gt;</code>. |
| <span id="modelscript-m5002"></span>`M5002` | `unknown-struct-field`    | [error] | Struct '<code>&lt;structName&gt;</code>' has no field named '<code>&lt;fieldName&gt;</code>'.                                |

# Export & Exchange Formats Reference

ModelScript serves as an open interoperability hub across systems engineering, multi-physics simulation, CAD/ECAD, formal verification, and regulatory compliance. Through `@modelscript/exchange`, `@modelscript/cad`, `@modelscript/runtime`, and `@modelscript/simulate`, the platform natively imports and exports **over 30 industry-standard formats**.

---

## 1. Functional Mock-up Interface (FMI 2.0 & FMI 3.0)

ModelScript compiles flattened DAE systems into self-contained `.fmu` archives (and imports external third-party `.fmu` binaries) conforming to the Modelica Association **FMI 2.0** and **FMI 3.0** specifications for both **Model Exchange (ME)** and **Co-Simulation (CS)**.

```bash
# Export an FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation FMU with embedded C99 source and WebAssembly binary
npx msx fmu DC_Motor motor.mo --fmi-version 3 --type cs --wasm --output DC_Motor.fmu

# Export a universal FMI 2.0 + 3.0 archive supporting both ME and CS
npx msx fmu ThermalPlant plant.mo --fmi-version both --type both --target all -o ThermalPlant.fmu

# Import an external third-party FMU and synthesize a typed Modelica wrapper block
npx msx import-fmu ./vendor/BatteryController.fmu -o BatteryControllerWrapper.mo
```

### Archive Layout & Capabilities

| Artifact Path                            | Standard      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| :--------------------------------------- | :------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `modelDescription.xml`                   | FMI 2.0 / 3.0 | Declares `ModelVariables`, causalities (`input`, `output`, `parameter`, `local`), physical units, `ModelStructure` (`Outputs`, `Derivatives`, `InitialUnknowns`), directional derivative sparsity patterns, and FMI 3.0 `Clock` / multidimensional array dimensions. |
| `sources/*.c`, `sources/*.h`             | ANSI C99      | Zero-dependency generated C99 implementation of `fmi2*` / `fmi3*` entry points, analytic Jacobians (`fmi2GetDirectionalDerivative` / `fmi3GetDirectionalDerivative`), and embedded RK4/BDF Co-Simulation steppers.                                                   |
| `binaries/<platform>/*.so\|.dll\|.dylib` | Native ABI    | Pre-compiled host shared libraries generated when `--compile` is passed.                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `binaries/wasm32-wasi/<model>.wasm`      | WebAssembly   | Portable, sandboxed WASM FMU binary generated when `--wasm` or `--target wasm` is passed, executable directly in browser workers and edge runtimes.                                                                                                                  |

### Universal Binary FMUs & In-WASM CPU Emulation

A major limitation of traditional FMI co-simulation is platform lock-in: an FMU containing a Windows x86 `.dll` cannot run on Linux or Apple Silicon without native source access.

Through `@modelscript/exchange/pe-emulator`, ModelScript includes **user-space CPU emulators and binary loaders executing inside WebAssembly**:

- **Cross-Architecture Execution**: Runs legacy Windows x86/x64 (`.dll`), Linux ELF (`.so`), and macOS Mach-O (`.dylib`) binary FMUs directly inside Node.js, browsers, or cloud runners without installing Wine or virtual machines.
- **CPU Translation Engines**:
  - **x86 / x86-64 Engine (`x86-cpu.ts`)**: Decodes instruction prefixes, registers, and floating-point/AVX2 vector instructions into typed array memory operations.
  - **AArch64 Engine (`aarch64-cpu.ts`)**: Decodes 64-bit ARM instruction streams and executes floating-point NEON vectors.
  - **C Runtime Shims (`c-runtime-shims.ts`)**: Traps standard C library calls (`malloc`, `free`, `sin`, `cos`, `printf`, `memcpy`) and routes them directly to host memory for native execution speed.
- **In-Browser C Compilation Worker (`wasm-compiler-worker.ts`)**:
  - Compiles FMI C99 source code into sandboxed WebAssembly modules on the fly directly inside browser WebWorkers.
  - Eliminates the need for server-side GCC/Clang compilation infrastructure when simulating customer models in the browser.

---

## 2. System Structure and Parameterization (SSP 1.0 & SSV 1.0)

ModelScript natively parses, lints (`SSP_*` and `SSV_*` rules), simulates, and packages **Modelica Association SSP 1.0** system containers:

| Extension | XML Namespace                                                  | Purpose                                                                                                                                                   |
| :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.ssp`    | ZIP Container                                                  | Bundles `SystemStructure.ssd`, `resources/*.fmu` components, parameter sets (`*.ssv`), and signal dictionaries (`*.ssm`).                                 |
| `.ssd`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureDescription`      | Defines hierarchical system architectures, FMU component references, typed connectors, causal signal connections, and `<ssd:DefaultExperiment>` metadata. |
| `.ssv`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureParameterValues`  | Externalizes parameter sets (`Real`, `Integer`, `Boolean`, `String`, `Enumeration`, and units) for variant management without recompiling FMUs.           |
| `.ssm`    | `http://ssp-standard.org/SSP1/SystemStructureParameterMapping` | Maps abstract parameter names in `.ssv` catalogs to concrete hierarchical component paths.                                                                |

```bash
# Lint an SSP architecture and its SSV parameter bindings
npx msx lint SystemStructure.ssd NominalParams.ssv

# Export a multi-project PSCAD workspace to an SSP 1.0 container
npx msx pscad export-ssp GridInterconnection.pswx -o GridInterconnection.ssp
```

---

## 3. Formal Verification Formats

The `msx export-formal` command translates SysML v2 models (constraints, requirements, and state machines) into three formal verification formats for external solvers and model checkers:

```bash
# Export constraints to SMT-LIB v2.6 for Z3 / cvc5 (logic auto-detected as QF_LRA or QF_NRA)
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format smt2 -o fcs.smt2

# Export state machines to nuXmv with an extra safety invariant
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format nuxmv --module FlightControl --invariants "altitude >= 0" -o fcs.smv

# Export assume-guarantee contracts to OCRA
npx msx export-formal FlightControl.sysml --format ocra -o fcs.oss
```

| Format Flag | Extension | Target Toolchains | Encoding Semantics                                                                                                                     |
| :---------- | :-------- | :---------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `smt2`      | `.smt2`   | Z3, cvc5          | SMT-LIB v2.6 with a `set-logic` directive (`--logic QF_LRA\|QF_NRA\|QF_IDL\|ALL`) and optional `--minimize` / `--maximize` objectives. |
| `nuxmv`     | `.smv`    | nuXmv             | Symbolic transition system module with optional `INVARSPEC` (`--invariants`) and `LTLSPEC` (`--ltl`) properties.                       |
| `ocra`      | `.oss`    | OCRA              | Contract-based component specification; `--module` sets the top-level component name.                                                  |

## 4. CI/CD Quality Gates & Regulatory Compliance Dossiers

The `msx verify`, `msx dhf`, `msx dossier`, and `msx gatekeeper` commands serialize static diagnostics, formal proof certificates, grid interconnection scorecards, and requirement traceability matrices into industry-standard CI/CD and regulatory formats:

```bash
# SARIF v2.1.0 for GitHub Code Scanning / Azure DevOps Security Tab
npx msx verify system.mo --format sarif --report linter-report.sarif

# CTRF (Common Test Report Format) JSON for unified CI dashboards
npx msx verify system.mo --format ctrf --report ctrf-report.json

# JUnit XML for Jenkins, GitLab CI, and CircleCI test summaries
npx msx verify system.mo --format junit --report junit-report.xml

# FDA 21 CFR Part 820 / ISO 13485 / ISO 26262 Design History File (DHF) Dossier
npx msx verify system.mo --format dhf --report dossier.md
npx msx dhf export ./workspace --format markdown -o DHF_Dossier.md

# NERC RSAW & NIST OSCAL 1.1 compliance dossier with FERC CEII watermark & Ed25519 signature
npx msx dossier build plant-manifest.json --out plant-rsaw.md --key keys/ed25519.pem

# Automated 5-stage ISO / Transmission Planner Grid Code Gatekeeper scorecard
npx msx gatekeeper evaluate submission.zip --interconnection Western --mva 150 --kv 230 --out scorecard.json
```

| Format / Dossier                | Schema / Standard                       | Key Payload Contents                                                                                                                                        |
| :------------------------------ | :-------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **SARIF** (`sarif`)             | OASIS SARIF v2.1.0                      | Rule descriptors (`M1000`–`M6040`, `S1001`–`S5008`), physical file locations (1-indexed line/column spans), severity levels, and counterexample code flows. |
| **CTRF** (`ctrf`)               | CTRF v0.0.0 JSON                        | Standardized `results.summary` (`tests`, `passed`, `failed`, `skipped`) and per-property verification duration and witness traces.                          |
| **JUnit** (`junit`)             | JUnit XML                               | `<testsuites>` and `<testcase>` elements with `<failure>` stack traces for falsified invariants or lint errors.                                             |
| **DHF** (`dhf`)                 | FDA 21 CFR 820.30 / ISO 13485           | End-to-end Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM), formal proof summaries, simulation verification evidence, and SHA-256 artifact integrity digests.        |
| **NERC RSAW / OSCAL** (`dossier`)| NERC PRC-024-3 / MOD-026 / OSCAL 1.1.2 | Automated Reliability Standard Audit Worksheet (RSAW), NIST OSCAL Assessment Results JSON, FERC CEII header watermarks, and Ed25519 cryptographic tokens.   |
| **Grid Gatekeeper** (`gatekeeper`)| NERC MOD-032-1 / IEEE Std 2800-2022   | 5-stage interconnection screening scorecard (MOD-032 completeness, 20 s flat-start drift, weak-grid $\text{SCR}=1.5$, IEEE 2800 LVRT/HVRT, EMT-RMS parity). |

ModelScript bridges descriptive MBSE specifications and semantic knowledge graphs with executable physics:

| Standard                         | Extensions / Media Types                                                  | CLI Command / API                                                                | Description                                                                                                                                                                         |

| **OMG ReqIF 1.2**                | `.reqif`, `.reqifz`                                                       | `msx reqif <import\|export>`                                                     | Bidirectional mapping between DOORS/Polarion-compatible ReqIF `SPEC-OBJECT` / `SPEC-RELATION` hierarchies and SysML v2 `requirement def` / `satisfy` blocks.                        |
| **OASIS OSLC 3.0 & TRS 3.0**     | `.ttl`, `.jsonld`, `.rdf`                                                 | `msx oslc <export\|serve>`                                                       | Exposes requirements (`oslc_rm:Requirement`) and architecture resources (`oslc_am:Resource`) with Tracked Resource Set (TRS 3.0) incremental change logs and delegated UI previews. |
| **W3C OWL 2 / RDF / SPARQL 1.1** | `.owl` (Functional Syntax), `.ttl` (Turtle), `.nt` (N-Triples), `.jsonld` | `/api/v1/libraries/rdf`, `/api/v1/libraries/sparql`, MCP `query_ontology_sparql` | Extracts ontological axioms, executes OWL 2 RL forward-chaining reasoning, and answers SPARQL 1.1 queries over workspace models.                                                    |

## 6. Industrial Digital Twin & Open Hardware Packaging (DDP, AASX, OKH)

For manufacturing handover, Industry 4.0 asset integration, and open-source hardware certification, ModelScript supports three complementary packaging standards:

```bash
# Pack a workspace into an ISO/PAS 81346 Digital Data Package (.ddp)
npx msx ddp pack ./workspace -o PumpStation.ddp

# Convert a DDP archive into an IDTA Asset Administration Shell v3.0 (.aasx) package
npx msx ddp to-aasx PumpStation.ddp -o PumpStation.aasx
```

| Standard                      | Format / Endpoint                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                 |
| :---------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **ISO/PAS 81346 DDP**         | `.ddp` (ZIP + XML/JSON)                            | Structures multi-domain engineering deliverables by function (`=`), product (`-`), and location (`+`) reference designation aspect trees.                   |
| **IDTA AAS v3.0**             | `.aasx` (Open Packaging Conventions) & `?lens=aas` | Packages Asset Administration Shells containing standardized `Nameplate`, `TechnicalData`, `HandoverDocumentation`, and `SimulationModels` (FMU) submodels. |
| **DIN SPEC 3105 / OSHWA OKH** | `okh.json` / `okh.toml` & `?lens=okh`              | Generates Open Know-How (OKH v1.0) manifests detailing bill of materials (BOM), CAD/ECAD design files, manufacturing tolerances, and SPDX licenses.         |

## 9. Surrogate Modeling & Machine Learning (ONNX, C99, Modelica ROM)

The `msx surrogate` pipeline exports trained Reduced-Order Models (MLP neural networks, multivariate polynomials, and Radial Basis Functions) with embedded domain-validity guardrails:

```bash
# Train an MLP surrogate and export ONNX, standalone C99, and pure Modelica (.mo) simultaneously
npx msx surrogate Compressor compressor.mo \
  --inputs "rpm,pressureRatio" \
  --input-bounds "rpm:1000:12000,pressureRatio:1.1:4.5" \
  --outputs "massFlow,efficiency" \
  --format all \
  --out-file build/compressor_rom
```

- **ONNX (`.onnx`)**: Serializes weights, biases, input normalization scalers, and activation layers (`Tanh`, `ReLU`, `GELU`) as a standard ONNX protobuf graph for deployment in ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, or PyTorch. Can also be imported via `--from-onnx`.
- **Standalone ANSI C99 (`.c` / `.h`)**: Zero-dependency static C inference function with compile-time weight arrays and bounding-box extrapolation flags for embedded MCU deployment.
- **Modelica Block (`.mo`)**: Self-contained Modelica `block` containing pure matrix/vector equations, `isExtrapolating` boolean output port, and `assert()` guardrails.

## 10. Simulation Trajectories & Scientific Data (CSV, JSON, MAT v4, HDF5, Parquet)

Simulation and Monte Carlo runners (`msx simulate`, `msx mc`, and Cloud HPC workers) produce structured time-series outputs:

```bash
# Export standard RFC 4180 CSV trajectory
npx msx simulate DC_Motor motor.mo --stop-time 5.0 --format csv > trajectory.csv

# Export structured JSON trajectory with variable metadata and solver statistics
npx msx simulate DC_Motor motor.mo --stop-time 5.0 --format json > trajectory.json
```

| Format                      | Source / Consumer                                                      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| :-------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **CSV (`.csv`)**            | `msx simulate --format csv`, `msx mc --format csv`, `@modelscript/csv` | Leading monotonic `time` column followed by state, derivative (`der(...)`), and algebraic variable columns; directly consumable by `Modelica.Blocks.Tables.CombiTimeTable` and `msl-comparison-runner`. |
| **JSON (`.json`)**          | `msx simulate --format json`, `msx mc --format json`                   | Contains `time: number[]`, `signals: Record<string, number[]>`, `units: Record<string, string>`, `events`, and solver convergence telemetry.                                                            |
| **MATLAB Level 4 (`.mat`)** | OpenModelica / Dymola compatibility                                    | Dual-matrix (`Aclass`, `name`, `description`, `dataInfo`, `data_1` parameters, `data_2` trajectories) binary format for legacy post-processing scripts.                                                 |
| **Apache Parquet & HDF5**   | Cloud HPC (`msx cloud download`) & Digital Twin Archive                | Columnar Zstandard-compressed trajectory storage for multi-gigabyte Monte Carlo ensembles and long-horizon operational twin logs.                                                                       |
